events.example:
nf.worlds.default():on("block_break", function(event)
  if event.state == "minecraft:diamond_ore" then
    event:cancel()
  end
end)

events.name: block_place
events.doc: A player is placing a block in this world: before `nf.on("block_place")`, with the same event.

events.name: entity_spawn
events.doc: An entity is coming into this world: before `nf.on("entity_spawn")`, with the same event, so `event:cancel()` here stops it and `event:stop()` keeps it from `nf`.
events.example:
nf.worlds.default():on("entity_spawn", function(event)
  if event.entity:kind() == "minecraft:phantom" then
    event:cancel()
  end
end)

events.name: dusk
events.doc: Night fell here: the time of day went from day (23000 to 12999) into night (13000 to 22999), by the clock or by `/time set`. Heard before `nf.on("world_dusk")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. The runtime looks at the clock every tick, and only while something listens; a jump from one night to the next (a whole day skipped) is no change, so nothing is heard.
events.example:
nf.worlds.default():on("dusk", function(event)
  for _, player in ipairs(event.world:players()) do
    player:send_message("<gray>Night falls.")
  end
end)

events.name: dawn
events.doc: Day broke here: the time of day went from night (13000 to 22999) into day (23000 to 12999), by the clock or by `/time set` (sleeping through the night too). Heard before `nf.on("world_dawn")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: block_explode
events.doc: A block exploded: a bed in the nether or the end, a respawn anchor charged away from the overworld. `event:cancel()` stops the explosion breaking anything; assign `event.breaks_blocks = false` to keep every block standing but still hurt what is near, or `event.yield` to change how much of what breaks drops. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_explode")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: block_ignite
events.doc: A block is catching fire: flint and steel, a fire charge, lava, lightning, fire spreading, an explosion. `event:cancel()` keeps it from burning. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_ignite")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: block_burn
events.doc: A block is burning away in a fire. `event:cancel()` keeps it there (it may still catch fire again). In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_burn")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: block_spread
events.doc: A block is spreading to another: grass, mycelium, moss, vines, mushrooms, fire, sculk. `event.block` is where it spreads to, `event.source` where from. `event:cancel()` stops it. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_spread")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: block_flow
events.doc: Water or lava is flowing into another block (or a dragon egg teleporting there). `event:cancel()` stops it. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_flow")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: block_grow
events.doc: A crop, sapling stage, sugar cane, cactus, bamboo, pumpkin or melon is growing by itself (bone meal included). `event:cancel()` stops it. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_grow")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: block_fade
events.doc: A block is fading by itself: ice or snow melting, coral dying, fire burning out, farmland drying. `event:cancel()` keeps it as it is. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_fade")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: block_form
events.doc: A block is forming by itself: snow falling, ice freezing, concrete setting, obsidian or cobblestone from lava, frost walker ice or a snow golem's trail (`event.entity` says which). `event:cancel()` stops it. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_form")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: leaves_decay
events.doc: Leaves are decaying, far from any log. `event:cancel()` keeps them. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("leaves_decay")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: piston_extend
events.doc: A piston is pushing out. `event:cancel()` keeps it in, and everything it would push where it is. In this world: heard before `nf.on("piston_extend")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: piston_retract
events.doc: A piston is pulling back. `event:cancel()` keeps it out, and (for a sticky one) the block it would pull where it is. In this world: heard before `nf.on("piston_retract")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: block_redstone
events.doc: A block's redstone power is changing: a lever, a button, a pressure plate, a redstone lamp or wire. Assign `event.to` to give it another power. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_redstone")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: sign_change
events.doc: A player finished writing on a sign. `event:cancel()` keeps the sign as it was. In this world: heard before `nf.on("sign_change")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: block_start_break
events.doc: A player started hitting a block to break it. `event:cancel()` stops them breaking it; assign `event.instant = true` to break it at once, or `false` to make them wait for it. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_start_break")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: block_drop_item
events.doc: A block a player broke is dropping its items, its contents included (a chest's, a furnace's): after `block_break`, once it has gone. `event:cancel()` drops nothing. In this world: heard before `nf.on("block_drop_item")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: weather_change
events.doc: It is starting or stopping raining (or snowing) in a world. `event:cancel()` keeps the weather it has. In this world: heard before `nf.on("weather_change")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: thunder_change
events.doc: A thunderstorm is starting or stopping in a world. `event:cancel()` keeps the weather it has. In this world: heard before `nf.on("thunder_change")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: lightning_strike
events.doc: Lightning is striking: a storm, a trident with channeling, a command or a script. `event:cancel()` stops it. In this world: heard before `nf.on("lightning_strike")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: chunk_load
events.doc: A chunk came into memory: someone came near, or it was generated for the first time (`event.generated`). The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("chunk_load")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: chunk_generated
events.doc: A chunk was generated, the first time it was loaded: its terrain, structures and the game's decorations are in place, so a script can add its own (a centity in a grove, a shrine on a hill). Its blocks are `event.x * 16` to `event.x * 16 + 15` across, the same along `z`, and can be read and changed in the handler; the chunks beside it may not be generated yet, so keep what you place inside it. Once per chunk, ever: one generated while no script listened isn't heard later. It happens for every new chunk a player explores, so keep handlers quick and leave most chunks alone. The server only reports these while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. In this world: heard before `nf.on("chunk_generated")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.
events.example:
nf.on("chunk_generated", function(event)
  if event.world:name() ~= "wilds" or math.random() > 0.2 then
    return
  end
  local ground = event.world:highest_block(vec3(event.x * 16 + 8, 0, event.z * 16 + 8))
  if ground and ground:biome() == "minecraft:dark_forest" then
    nf.centities.spawn("grove_spirit", event.world:location(ground:position() + vec3(0.5, 1, 0.5)))
  end
end)

events.name: chunk_unload
events.doc: A chunk is leaving memory, as everyone has gone away. Its blocks can still be read and changed in the handler. In this world: heard before `nf.on("chunk_unload")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

events.name: furnace_smelt
events.doc: A furnace, smoker or blast furnace finished smelting one item. `event:cancel()` stops it: the item stays unsmelted. Assign `event.result` to make something else. In this world: heard before `nf.on("furnace_smelt")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there.

functions.name: name
functions.doc: Its name, as `nf.worlds.get` takes it: `"world"`, `"world_nether"`.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether the server has it loaded now.

functions.name: environment
functions.doc: What kind of world it is, or `nil` once it has gone. A world of a custom dimension type says `"normal"`.

functions.name: location
functions.doc: A `Location` in this world, for the functions that take one (`player:teleport`, `nf.centities.spawn`). Give both `yaw` and `pitch`, or neither for a location with no facing; a `yaw` alone faces level.

params.name: position
params.doc: Where.

params.name: yaw
params.doc: Which way it faces horizontally, in degrees (0 south, 90 west).

params.name: pitch
params.doc: How far up or down, in degrees (−90 up, 90 down).

functions.example: player:teleport(nf.worlds.default():location(vec3(0, 80, 0), 180, 0))

functions.name: time_of_day
functions.doc: The time of day in ticks, 0 to 23999: 0 is sunrise, 6000 noon, 12000 sunset, 18000 midnight. `nil` once the world has gone. It's the game's clock, not the wall clock (`nf.server.unix_time()`).

functions.name: set_time_of_day
functions.doc: Sets the time of day, keeping the day count. Taken modulo 24000. Doesn't stop the clock (that's the daylight cycle game rule).

params.name: ticks
params.doc: 0 sunrise, 6000 noon, 12000 sunset, 18000 midnight.

returns.doc: `false` when the world has gone.

functions.name: is_night
functions.doc: Whether it is night here: the time of day is 13000 to 22999, from dusk to just before sunrise, as `/time set night` and a centity's `"night"` spawn time mean it. `false` once the world has gone.

functions.name: is_day
functions.doc: Whether it is day here: the time of day is 23000 to 12999, the rest of `is_night`'s. `false` once the world has gone.

functions.name: day_count
functions.doc: How many whole days have gone by in this world, or `nil` once it has gone.

functions.name: moon_phase
functions.doc: Tonight's moon, or `nil` once the world has gone. It moves on a phase each day: full, waning gibbous, last quarter, waning crescent, new, waxing crescent, first quarter, waxing gibbous, then full again.
functions.example:
if world:moon_phase() == "full_moon" then
  nf.server.broadcast("<red>The moon is full tonight.")
end

functions.name: weather
functions.doc: The weather now, or `nil` once the world has gone. Thunder always comes with rain.

functions.name: set_weather
functions.doc: Changes the weather, for `options.ticks` or for as long as the game would have kept it. A `ticks` below 1 is an error, as is a key `options` doesn't take.

returns.doc: `false` when the world has gone.

functions.example: world:set_weather("thunder", { ticks = 20 * 60 })

functions.name: sky
functions.doc: The sky set over the world (`world:set_sky`), as the calling script names it, or `nil` for none (or once the world has gone). A player's own (`player:set_sky`) is theirs alone.

functions.name: set_sky
functions.doc: Sets a sky of the project's over the world (`skies/<id>.json`): everyone in it sees its colours in place of the biomes' own, the sky, fog, clouds and water, fading over `options.fade_ticks`, until it's cleared or another is set. Only what players are shown changes: the world, its biomes, its mobs and its weather are as they were, and a restart clears it. A player's own sky (`player:set_sky`) is shown them instead. A sky the project has no file for is an error, and so is one added since the server started (its colours are biomes, which the game learns as it starts: restart the server).

params.name: sky
params.doc: A sky of the project's (its file's name under `skies/`, or `namespace:id` for one a package it depends on exports).

returns.doc: `false` when the world has gone.

functions.example: world:set_sky("blood_moon", { fade_ticks = 100 })

functions.name: clear_sky
functions.doc: Takes the world's sky away (`world:set_sky`): its biomes' own colours come back over `options.fade_ticks`. Nothing when it has none.
functions.example: world:clear_sky({ fade_ticks = 100 })

functions.name: spawn_location
functions.doc: Where players appear in this world when nothing else decides, or `nil` once the world has gone.

functions.name: set_spawn_location
functions.doc: Moves the world's spawn. A `Location` in another world is an error.

params.name: location_or_position
params.doc: Where: a `Location` in this world (its facing is used, when it has one) or a position.

returns.doc: `false` when the world has gone.

functions.name: min_height
functions.doc: The lowest block y there can be, or `nil` once the world has gone.

functions.name: max_height
functions.doc: One above the highest block y there can be, or `nil` once the world has gone.

functions.name: block
functions.doc: The block at a position: a handle that reads the world live, so it sees later changes. The position is floored to the block it's in. `nil` once the world has gone.

params.name: position
params.doc: Any point in the block.

functions.example: local below = this:world():block(this:position() - vec3(0, 1, 0))

functions.name: blocks
functions.doc: Every block in a box, read in one call: for code that needs many blocks at once (a mob's collision, a flood fill of a room), where a `world:block` and a `:kind()` per block would cost each one. The corners are floored to the blocks they're in and both are included, in any order. What each block is given as is `options.what`. At most 32,768 blocks (32 × 32 × 32): a bigger box is an error. `nil` when any of the box is in a chunk that isn't loaded, or the world has gone.

params.name: from
params.doc: One corner: any point in its block.

params.name: to
params.doc: The opposite corner, included: any point in its block.

functions.example:
local box = world:blocks(vec3(0, 60, 0), vec3(15, 70, 15), { what = "class" })
if box then
  -- A block within the box, counted from its corner.
  local function at(x, y, z)
    return box.cells[1 + x + box.size_x * (z + box.size_z * y)]
  end
  if at(0, 0, 0) == 2 then log("solid") end
end

functions.name: flood
functions.doc: Fills outward from a block through every block `options.through` names, one neighbour at a time, as far as it reaches: the blocks of a tree (`through = { "#minecraft:logs" }`), the air of a room (`through = { "passable" }`), a lake. It answers every block it filled (`positions`, nearest first by steps) and every block it stopped at (`edges`: a room's walls), with what each is when asked (`kinds`), and `stopped` says why it didn't finish when it didn't: it hit its `limit`, a chunk that isn't loaded or the world's top or bottom (`"unloaded"`: a room open to the sky or the unknown), or its `bounds`. It runs in the server, reading the blocks a box at a time, so a fill of thousands of blocks costs a script one call. A start block it can't fill through answers no positions, and the start as an edge. Blocks in chunks that aren't loaded can't be read or changed: that answers `nil` or `false`, and never loads the chunk (`world:load_chunk` does).

params.name: start
params.doc: Any point in the block to start from.

returns.doc: `nil` once the world has gone.

functions.example:
local room = world:flood(assert(player:position()), { through = { "passable" }, except = { "#minecraft:doors" }, limit = 750, kinds = true })
if room and not room.stopped then
  log(#room.positions .. " blocks of air, walled in by " .. #room.edges)
end

functions.name: set_block
functions.doc: Changes the block at a position. A block state the server doesn't have (an unknown block, property or value) is an error. Blocks in chunks that aren't loaded can't be read or changed: that answers `nil` or `false`, and never loads the chunk (`world:load_chunk` does).

params.name: position
params.doc: Any point in the block.

params.name: state
params.doc: A block state: `"minecraft:stone"`, `"minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east]"`. Properties left out take their defaults.

returns.doc: Whether it changed: `false` in an unloaded chunk or a world that's gone.

functions.example: world:set_block(vec3(10, 64, 10), "minecraft:gold_block")

functions.name: fill_blocks
functions.doc: Sets every block in the box between two corners (both included) to one state. One call changes at most 32768 blocks: a bigger box is an error (`fill_gradually` spreads a big fill over several ticks). A block state the server doesn't have is an error. Blocks in unloaded chunks are skipped.

params.name: from
params.doc: One corner.

params.name: to
params.doc: The opposite corner.

params.name: state
params.doc: A block state, as `set_block` takes it.

returns.doc: How many blocks it changed: 0 in a world that has gone.

functions.example:
nf.task(function()
  for y = 64, 127 do
    world:fill_blocks(vec3(0, y, 0), vec3(63, y, 63), "minecraft:air")
    nf.wait(1)
  end
end)

functions.name: fill_gradually
functions.doc: Sets every block in the box between two corners (both included) to one state, like `fill_blocks`, but over as many ticks as it takes, for a box too big for one call: up to 16777216 blocks (256 × 256 × 256). It goes a few thousand blocks a tick, shared with every other gradual placement and fill on the server (the owner's `structures.blocks-per-tick` in `config.yml`), so even a big one never stalls the server; each package may have a few going at once (`structures.max-jobs-per-package`), past which one fails at once. It goes a chunk's column at a time, from the bottom up, loading the chunks the box covers as it reaches them (`fill_blocks` skips unloaded ones). A bigger box, a block state the server doesn't have, or a `per_tick` below 1 is an error at once. The world going, or this script stopping, stops it part way, and what was set stays. It takes as many ticks as the fill does, so its changed arrives later: give `callback`, which is called with `changed, err` once it's done, or call it inside a task (`nf.task`) without one, and it waits and returns `changed, err`. Without a callback outside a task, it's an error. When it fails, `changed` is `nil` and `err` says why.

params.name: from
params.doc: One corner.

params.name: to
params.doc: The opposite corner.

params.name: state
params.doc: A block state, as `set_block` takes it.

params.name: callback
params.doc: Called on the main thread once it's done, as this script's code, with how many blocks it changed (a block that was already that state is not counted) (or `nil` and why not). Not called if the script has stopped by then.

functions.example:
world:fill_gradually(vec3(-200, 0, -200), vec3(199, 120, 199), "minecraft:air", nil, function(changed, err)
  if err then
    print("The clear-out stopped: " .. err)
  else
    nf.server.broadcast(changed .. " blocks cleared")
  end
end)

returns.doc: Only without a callback, in a task: how many blocks it changed (a block that was already that state is not counted), or `nil`.
Why it failed, when it did; `nil` when it worked.

functions.name: highest_block
functions.doc: The highest block at a column that isn't air, ignoring the position's `y`. `nil` in an unloaded chunk, or a world that has gone.

params.name: position
params.doc: Any point in the column.

functions.name: is_chunk_loaded
functions.doc: Whether the chunk a position is in is loaded: whether its blocks can be read and changed now.

params.name: position
params.doc: Any point in the chunk.

functions.name: load_chunk
functions.doc: Loads the chunk a position is in, now, generating it if it's new: that can take a while, so do it rarely. The server unloads it again when nobody is near, as it does any chunk.

params.name: position
params.doc: Any point in the chunk.

returns.doc: Whether it's loaded: `false` for a world that has gone.

functions.name: locate_biome
functions.doc: Finds the nearest place where the world's generator puts a biome, as `/locate biome` does: it asks the generator, so it finds places in chunks nobody has been to, and never loads or generates a chunk. It looks out from `options.near` in a square spiral, every 32 blocks across and 64 up and down, so the place it gives is in the biome but may be up to 32 blocks past its nearest edge, and a biome narrower than that can be missed. A biome the world's generator never places (a nether biome in the overworld) is found nowhere at once. An id that isn't a biome on this server (a bare id that isn't one of the project's is an error saying how to write the game's), or a `radius` out of range, is an error at once. Finding nothing within the radius, or a world that has gone, fails. It works off the main thread, so its position arrives later: give `callback`, which is called with `position, err` once it's done, or call it inside a task (`nf.task`) without one, and it waits and returns `position, err`. Without a callback outside a task, it's an error. When it fails, `position` is `nil` and `err` says why.

params.name: id
params.doc: The biome, named as a file names one: the project's own by its id (`"ruby_grove"`, `biomes/ruby_grove.json`), a package's `"acme:grove"` (if it exports it), the game's always written in full (`"minecraft:desert"`).

params.name: callback
params.doc: Called on the main thread once it's done, as this script's code, with the place it found: a block position in this world, at the height it found the biome (or `nil` and why not). Not called if the script has stopped by then.

functions.example:
nf.task(function()
  local desert, err = world:locate_biome("minecraft:desert", { near = player:position() })
  if not desert then
    player:send_message("No desert near: " .. err)
    return
  end
  local ground = world:highest_block(desert)
  if ground then
    player:teleport(world:location(ground:position() + vec3(0.5, 1, 0.5)))
  end
end)

returns.doc: Only without a callback, in a task: the place it found: a block position in this world, at the height it found the biome, or `nil`.
Why it failed, when it did; `nil` when it worked.

functions.name: players
functions.doc: Everyone in this world now. Empty once the world has gone.

functions.name: centities
functions.doc: The live centity instances in this world: the same as `nf.centities.all` with this world as the filter's `world`.

params.name: filter
params.doc: Only some of them, as `nf.centities.all` takes it. Its `world`, if given, must be this one.

functions.name: entities
functions.doc: The entities in this world's loaded chunks, players included (as `Player` handles), or those the filter picks. Never the entities centities are drawn with. Empty once the world has gone. A filter key that isn't one of `EntityFilter`'s is an error.

params.name: filter
params.doc: Only one kind, one tag, living ones, or those near a point.

functions.example:
for _, zombie in ipairs(world:entities({ kind = "minecraft:zombie", near = here, radius = 16 })) do
  zombie:set_glowing(true)
end

functions.name: spawn_entity
functions.doc: Spawns an entity, set up as `options` say before anything sees it (its `entity_spawn` handlers included). A kind the server doesn't have, or one that can't be spawned (a player), is an error.

params.name: kind
params.doc: What: `"minecraft:zombie"`.

params.name: location_or_position
params.doc: Where: a `Location` in this world (facing its way, when it has a facing), or a position.

returns.doc: The new entity, or `nil` when the world has gone, its chunk isn't loaded, or an `entity_spawn` handler (or another plugin) cancelled it.

functions.name: spawn_item
functions.doc: Drops an item stack at a position, as if a block broke there. An item table with a misspelled field, or an item the server doesn't have, is an error.

params.name: position
params.doc: Where, in this world.

returns.doc: The dropped item, or `nil` when the world has gone, its chunk isn't loaded, or something cancelled it.

functions.name: spawn_particle
functions.doc: Spawns particles at a position. The particle's id comes from the server (`"minecraft:flame"`), and which options it takes depends on its kind: `color` and `size` for dust, `color` for coloured particles, `block_state` for block particles, `item` for item particles. An unknown particle, an option it doesn't take, or one it needs left out is an error. Particles that need data NetherForge can't send (vibrations, trails) are an error too. Players see them within 32 blocks, or 128 with `force`.

params.name: particle
params.doc: A particle id: `"minecraft:flame"`, `"minecraft:dust"`.

params.name: position
params.doc: Where, in the world.

returns.doc: `false` when the world has gone.

functions.name: play_sound
functions.doc: Plays a sound at a position, for everyone near enough to hear it. A Minecraft sound (`"minecraft:block.note_block.pling"`, checked against the server's sounds) or a resource pack sound (`"<pack>/<key>"`, like `"ui/click"`, your package's own, or another loaded package's as `"<namespace>:<pack>/<key>"`: [looks are values](packages.md#looks-are-values)). An unknown sound is an error.

params.name: sound
params.doc: A sound id.

params.name: position
params.doc: Where it comes from, in the world.

returns.doc: `false` when the world has gone.

functions.example: world:play_sound("minecraft:block.note_block.pling", block:position(), { pitch = 1.5 })

functions.name: explode
functions.doc: Makes an explosion at a position, as TNT would (TNT's power is 4): it damages and knocks back entities, and breaks blocks unless `break_blocks` is `false`.

params.name: position
params.doc: Its centre.

params.name: power
params.doc: How strong: 4 is TNT, 6 a charged creeper. At least 0.

returns.doc: Whether it went off: `false` when another plugin stopped it, or the world has gone.

functions.name: strike_lightning
functions.doc: Strikes lightning at a position: it sets fire and hurts what it hits, unless `effect_only`.

params.name: position
params.doc: Where it lands.

returns.doc: `false` when the world has gone.

functions.name: raycast
functions.doc: Casts a ray from a point and answers the first thing it hits within `max_distance`: a block's collision shape, an entity's hitbox, or a centity's hitbox (tested with the same shapes clicks are). `nil` when it hits nothing, and in a world that has gone. Blocks in unloaded chunks aren't hit.

params.name: from
params.doc: Where the ray starts, in the world.

params.name: direction
params.doc: Which way it goes: any length but zero.

params.name: max_distance
params.doc: How far it reaches, in blocks.

functions.example:
local world, eyes, facing = player:world(), player:eye_position(), player:direction()
local hit = world and eyes and facing and world:raycast(eyes, facing, 20)
if hit and hit.centity then
  hit.centity:play_animation("wobble")
end

functions.name: overlap_box
functions.doc: Everything whose hitbox is inside or touches a box, nearest the box's middle first. It finds centities by their hitboxes (each shown node's boxes, as `raycast` and physics see them; a hidden node has none), players and other entities by theirs, as `options` allows: everything, by default. A centity is found once, by its nearest node. Only what's in loaded chunks is found. An empty list (or `nil`) in a world that has gone.

params.name: min
params.doc: One corner, in the world.

params.name: max
params.doc: The opposite corner. The corners may come in either order.

functions.example:
local corner = vec3(0, 64, 0)
for _, hit in ipairs(world:overlap_box(corner, corner + vec3(4, 3, 4), { players = false })) do
  if hit.centity then
    hit.centity:remove()
  end
end

functions.name: overlap_sphere
functions.doc: Everything whose hitbox comes within `radius` of a point, nearest first: what an explosion or an aura reaches. It finds centities by their hitboxes (each shown node's boxes, as `raycast` and physics see them; a hidden node has none), players and other entities by theirs, as `options` allows: everything, by default. A centity is found once, by its nearest node. Only what's in loaded chunks is found. An empty list (or `nil`) in a world that has gone.

params.name: center
params.doc: The middle, in the world.

params.name: radius
params.doc: In blocks, at least 0.

functions.example:
for _, hit in ipairs(world:overlap_sphere(vec3(0, 64, 0), 4, { entities = false })) do
  log(hit.distance)
end

functions.name: overlap_cone
functions.doc: Everything whose hitbox reaches into a cone from a point, nearest first: what a swing or a breath in front of someone reaches. A hitbox counts when its point nearest the cone's axis is within `length` of the tip and within `angle` of the axis, or the tip is inside it. It finds centities by their hitboxes (each shown node's boxes, as `raycast` and physics see them; a hidden node has none), players and other entities by theirs, as `options` allows: everything, by default. A centity is found once, by its nearest node. Only what's in loaded chunks is found. An empty list (or `nil`) in a world that has gone.

params.name: origin
params.doc: The cone's tip, in the world.

params.name: direction
params.doc: Which way it opens: any length but zero.

params.name: length
params.doc: How far it reaches from the tip, in blocks, at least 0.

params.name: angle
params.doc: How wide it opens, in degrees from its axis to its side: 0 to 180 (90 is everything in front, 180 a sphere).

functions.example:
local eyes, facing = assert(player:eye_position()), assert(player:direction())
for _, hit in ipairs(world:overlap_cone(eyes, facing, 3, 45, { exclude = { player } })) do
  if hit.centity then
    hit.centity:emit("game:struck", { by = player })
  end
end

functions.name: sweep
functions.doc: Moves a sphere of `options.radius` (0, a point, by default) from one point to another and answers everything it touches on the way, in the order it meets them: what a fast or piercing shot passes through in a tick, which a ray (stopping at the first thing) can't say. Blocks stop it unless `blocks = false`: the block it meets is then the last hit, with its `normal`, and nothing past it is found. It finds centities by their hitboxes (each shown node's boxes, as `raycast` and physics see them; a hidden node has none), players and other entities by theirs, as `options` allows: everything, by default. A centity is found once, by its nearest node. Only what's in loaded chunks is found. An empty list (or `nil`) in a world that has gone.

params.name: from
params.doc: Where it starts, in the world.

params.name: to
params.doc: Where it would end.

functions.example:
local position, velocity = vec3(0, 65, 0), vec3(2, 0, 0)
local hits = world:sweep(position, position + velocity, { radius = 0.25, players = false })
for _, hit in ipairs(hits) do
  if hit.block then
    break -- it struck a wall
  elseif hit.centity then
    hit.centity:emit("game:hit", { damage = 5 })
  end
end

functions.name: nearest
functions.doc: The nearest thing whose hitbox comes within `radius` of a point, or `nil` when there's nothing: what a homing shot or a mob looking for a target wants. With `line_of_sight = true`, only something a ray from the point reaches without a block in the way. It finds centities by their hitboxes (each shown node's boxes, as `raycast` and physics see them; a hidden node has none), players and other entities by theirs, as `options` allows: everything, by default. A centity is found once, by its nearest node. Only what's in loaded chunks is found. An empty list (or `nil`) in a world that has gone.

params.name: position
params.doc: Where to look from, in the world.

params.name: radius
params.doc: How far to look, in blocks, at least 0.

functions.example:
local target = world:nearest(assert(this:position()), 16, { centities = false, line_of_sight = true })
if target and target.entity then
  this:look_at(target.position)
end

functions.name: game_rule
functions.doc: A game rule's value: a `boolean` or an `integer`, depending on the rule. `nil` once the world has gone. A rule the server doesn't have is an error.

params.name: rule
params.doc: Its id, as the server names it: `"keep_inventory"`, `"random_tick_speed"`.

functions.name: set_game_rule
functions.doc: Sets a game rule in this world. A rule the server doesn't have, or a value of the wrong type for it (a `boolean` rule given a number), is an error.

params.name: rule
params.doc: Its id: `"keep_inventory"`.

params.name: value
params.doc: A `boolean` or an `integer`, as the rule takes.

returns.doc: `false` when the world has gone.

functions.example: world:set_game_rule("keep_inventory", true)

functions.name: spawn_limit
functions.doc: How many mobs of a spawn category the game keeps around each player here before it stops spawning more (the mob cap, per player, scaled by how many chunks are loaded around them), or `nil` once the world has gone. It's this world's own setting, or the server's (`bukkit.yml`) when the world has none.

params.name: category
params.doc: Which mobs count: `"monster"` for hostile ones, `"animal"` for farm animals, `"ambient"` for bats, and so on.

functions.name: set_spawn_limit
functions.doc: Sets this world's mob cap for a spawn category (see `world:spawn_limit`). `0` stops that category spawning naturally. A negative number goes back to the server's own setting. Mobs already there stay.

params.name: category
params.doc: Which mobs count.

params.name: limit
params.doc: The most of them there may be.

returns.doc: `false` when the world has gone.

functions.example: world:set_spawn_limit("monster", 30)

functions.name: spawn_interval
functions.doc: How many ticks pass between the game's attempts to spawn mobs of a spawn category here, or `nil` once the world has gone. It's this world's own setting, or the server's (`bukkit.yml`) when the world has none.

params.name: category
params.doc: Which mobs.

functions.name: set_spawn_interval
functions.doc: Sets how many ticks pass between spawn attempts for a spawn category in this world (see `world:spawn_interval`): lower is faster. `0` stops that category spawning naturally. A negative number goes back to the server's own setting.

params.name: category
params.doc: Which mobs.

params.name: ticks
params.doc: Ticks between attempts.

returns.doc: `false` when the world has gone.

functions.example: world:set_spawn_interval("monster", 2)

functions.name: is_managed
functions.doc: Whether this project may unload it (`world:unload`): it's one the project's scripts created (`nf.worlds.create`, `nf.worlds.copy`) or named in `netherforge.json`'s `managedWorlds`, and it isn't the server's main world. Any script can find, load and use any world; only managed ones can be taken away.

functions.name: unload
functions.doc: Unloads the world: players in it are moved out first (to the spawn of `options.move_players_to`, else of the main world), then the server saves it (unless `save` is `false`) and lets it go. With `delete`, its files are deleted too, off the main thread, and the project forgets it. Only a world this project manages can be unloaded (see `world:is_managed`): any other, the server's main world included, is an error, as is a `move_players_to` in this same world. A world it created stays the project's after a restart; find it again with `nf.worlds.load`.

returns.doc: Whether it was unloaded: `false` when it had gone already, or the server (another plugin) kept it.

functions.example: arena:unload({ save = false, delete = true, move_players_to = nf.worlds.get("lobby") })

functions.name: border
functions.doc: The world's border: the wall players can't pass, shown to everyone in the world (except a player given a border of their own with `player:border()`). `nil` once the world has gone.
functions.example:
local border = world:border()
if border then
  border:set_center(vec3(0, 0, 0))
  border:set_size(200)
  border:set_size(20, { ticks = 20 * 60 })
end

functions.name: save_structure
functions.doc: Saves the box between two corners (both included) as a structure named `id`, to place later with `place_structure`: an arena to reset, a prefab to stamp. It's saved in the server's data folder, not the project, and kept across restarts; saving the same id again replaces it. An id that isn't an id (lowercase letters, digits and `_`), or that one of the project's structures (`structures/<id>.nbt`) or builds (`builds/<id>/`) already has, is an error, as is a box over 48 blocks along any side. Air is saved too, so placing it puts back the empty space as well; it loads the chunks the box covers, as `/place` does.

params.name: id
params.doc: Its name: `"arena_reset"`.

params.name: from
params.doc: One corner.

params.name: to
params.doc: The opposite corner.

returns.doc: Whether it was saved: `false` when the world has gone, or the file couldn't be written.

functions.example: world:save_structure("arena_reset", vec3(0, 60, 0), vec3(47, 90, 47), { entities = false })

functions.name: place_structure
functions.doc: Places a structure with its smallest corner at `position` (before it's turned): one of the project's (`structures/<id>.nbt`) or one a script saved (`save_structure`). Loads the chunks it covers, as `/place` does, all in this tick: `place_gradually` spreads a big one over several. A build (`builds/<id>/`) is always placed that way, so naming one here is an error, as is a structure there's none of, one whose file can't be read, a `rotation` that isn't a multiple of 90 or an `integrity` outside 0 to 1.

params.name: id
params.doc: Which structure.

params.name: position
params.doc: Where its smallest corner goes, floored to a block.

returns.doc: `false` when the world has gone.

functions.example: world:place_structure("arena_reset", vec3(0, 60, 0), { rotation = 90, mirror = "none", integrity = 1, entities = false })

functions.name: place_gradually
functions.doc: Places a structure or a build (`builds/<id>/`, a structure too big for one file) like `place_structure`, its smallest corner at `position` before it's turned, but over as many ticks as it takes. It goes a few thousand blocks a tick, shared with every other gradual placement and fill on the server (the owner's `structures.blocks-per-tick` in `config.yml`), so even a big one never stalls the server; each package may have a few going at once (`structures.max-jobs-per-package`), past which one fails at once. Its blocks go in from the bottom up (a build's a part at a time), loading the chunks it covers as it reaches them, then its entities, once every block is in. Blocks go in as they were saved, with no updates to their neighbours, as `/place` puts them. A structure or build there's none of, a `rotation` that isn't a multiple of 90, an `integrity` outside 0 to 1 or a `per_tick` below 1 is an error at once. A part that can't be read, the world going, or this script stopping stops it part way, and what was placed stays. It takes as many ticks as the placing does, so its placed arrives later: give `callback`, which is called with `placed, err` once it's done, or call it inside a task (`nf.task`) without one, and it waits and returns `placed, err`. Without a callback outside a task, it's an error. When it fails, `placed` is `nil` and `err` says why.

params.name: id
params.doc: Which structure or build.

params.name: position
params.doc: Where its smallest corner goes, floored to a block.

params.name: callback
params.doc: Called on the main thread once it's done, as this script's code, with how many blocks it placed (those `integrity` left out, or outside the world's heights, are not counted) (or `nil` and why not). Not called if the script has stopped by then.

functions.example:
nf.task(function()
  local placed, err = world:place_gradually("castle", vec3(0, 64, 0), { rotation = 90 })
  if not placed then
    print("The castle stopped part way: " .. err)
    return
  end
  nf.server.broadcast("The castle is up: " .. placed .. " blocks")
end)

returns.doc: Only without a callback, in a task: how many blocks it placed (those `integrity` left out, or outside the world's heights, are not counted), or `nil`.
Why it failed, when it did; `nil` when it worked.

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `world:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: WorldBorder
classes.doc: A border: the wall at the edge of a square area, which players can't walk through and which hurts them outside it. Either a world's (`world:border()`), which everyone in the world sees, or one player's own (`player:border()`), which only they see and which the server draws for them but doesn't enforce: it doesn't hurt them, and doesn't stop what isn't them. Sizes and positions are blocks; times are ticks (20 a second). Its methods answer `nil` or `false` once its world has gone, or for a player's own, once they've left or gone back to their world's (`player:reset_border()`).

functions.name: center
functions.doc: Its centre, with `y` 0, or `nil` once it has gone.

functions.name: set_center
functions.doc: Moves its centre. `y` is ignored. More than 29,999,984 blocks out is an error.

params.name: center
params.doc: Where.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone.

functions.name: size
functions.doc: How wide it is, side to side, in blocks: while it's growing or shrinking, how wide it is now. `nil` once it has gone.

functions.name: set_size
functions.doc: Changes how wide it is: at once, or moving steadily there over `options.ticks`. A size below 1 or over 59,999,968, or negative `ticks`, is an error.

params.name: size
params.doc: Side to side, in blocks.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone.

functions.example: border:set_size(50, { ticks = 20 * 30 }) -- shrinks to 50 over 30 seconds

functions.name: damage
functions.doc: How it hurts players outside it, or `nil` once it has gone.

functions.name: set_damage
functions.doc: Changes how it hurts players outside it; what `damage` leaves out stays as it was. A negative value is an error. A player's own border is only drawn, so this changes nothing for them.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone.

functions.example: border:set_damage({ amount = 0.5, buffer = 2 })

functions.name: warning
functions.doc: When players' screens turn red as it comes near, or `nil` once it has gone.

functions.name: set_warning
functions.doc: Changes when players' screens turn red; what `warning` leaves out stays as it was. A negative value is an error.

returns.doc: `false` once it has gone.

functions.example: border:set_warning({ distance = 5, ticks = 20 * 15 })

functions.name: contains
functions.doc: Whether a place is inside it. A `Location` in another world is outside a world's border; a player's own border has no world, so only the position counts. `false` once it has gone.

params.name: location_or_position
params.doc: Where: a `Location`, or a position.

functions.example:
local here = player:location()
if here and not border:contains(here) then
  player:send_message("<red>Get back inside!")
end

classes.name: Block
classes.doc: One block position in one world. The handle is the position, not what's there: it reads the world live, so a `Block` kept from earlier sees later changes. Blocks in chunks that aren't loaded can't be read or changed: that answers `nil` or `false`, and never loads the chunk (`world:load_chunk` does).

functions.name: world
functions.doc: The world it's in.

functions.name: position
functions.doc: Its corner with the smallest x, y and z: whole numbers, in the world.

functions.name: location
functions.doc: Its corner as a `Location`, with no facing.

functions.name: kind
functions.doc: What block it is, like `"minecraft:stone"`, or `nil` in an unloaded chunk.

functions.name: state
functions.doc: Its whole block state, like `"minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=bottom,shape=straight,waterlogged=false]"` (properties sorted), or `nil` in an unloaded chunk.

functions.name: property
functions.doc: One property's value, like `"east"` for `facing`, or `nil` when the block has no such property or its chunk isn't loaded.

params.name: name
params.doc: The property: `"facing"`.

functions.name: properties
functions.doc: Every property and its value; empty for a block without any, and `nil` in an unloaded chunk.

functions.name: is_air
functions.doc: Whether it's air (any kind). `false` in an unloaded chunk.

functions.name: is_solid
functions.doc: Whether it's solid: something players stand on and can't walk through. `false` in an unloaded chunk.

functions.name: is_liquid
functions.doc: Whether it's water or lava. `false` in an unloaded chunk.

functions.name: set_state
functions.doc: Changes it, as `world:set_block` does. A block state the server doesn't have is an error.

params.name: state
params.doc: A block state: `"minecraft:stone"`.

returns.doc: `false` in an unloaded chunk.

functions.name: set_property
functions.doc: Changes one property, keeping the rest of its state. A property the block doesn't have, or a value it can't take, is an error.

params.name: name
params.doc: The property: `"facing"`.

params.name: value
params.doc: Its new value: `"north"`.

returns.doc: `false` in an unloaded chunk.

functions.example:
local door = world:block(vec3(10, 64, 10))
if door then
  door:set_property("open", "true")
end

functions.name: break_naturally
functions.doc: Breaks it as a player would: it drops what it would drop (for that tool, when given) and turns to air.

params.name: tool
params.doc: What it was broken with, for its drops: silk touch, fortune, or the wrong tool dropping nothing.

returns.doc: Whether it broke: `false` for air, or in an unloaded chunk.

functions.name: relative
functions.doc: The block at an offset from this one.

params.name: offset
params.doc: An offset in blocks (floored), or the face of the neighbour: `"up"` is the block above.

functions.example: local above = block:relative("up")

functions.name: inventory
functions.doc: What a container block holds (a chest, a barrel, a hopper, a furnace, a shulker box), as an `Inventory`: the same one players see. A double chest's is both halves. `nil` for a block that isn't a container, and in an unloaded chunk.
functions.example:
local chest = world:block(vec3(10, 64, 10)):inventory()
if chest then
  chest:add_item({ kind = "minecraft:bread", count = 8 })
end

functions.name: custom
functions.doc: The project block that's here, as a `CustomBlock` (the same handle: one position, one block), or `nil` when what's here isn't one of the project's blocks, or its chunk isn't loaded.
functions.example:
local custom = world:block(vec3(10, 64, 10)):custom()
if custom then
  log(custom:id())
end

functions.name: light_level
functions.doc: How bright it is there, 0 to 15: the brighter of block light and sky light. `nil` in an unloaded chunk.

functions.name: sky_light_level
functions.doc: How much sky light reaches it, 0 to 15, whatever the time of day. `nil` in an unloaded chunk.

functions.name: biome
functions.doc: The biome here, named as `locate_biome` takes one: a biome of the project reads as its id (`"ruby_grove"`), a package's as `"acme:grove"` (to a package's own scripts, its own is bare), the game's as `"minecraft:plains"`. The game keeps biomes per 4×4×4 blocks, so neighbouring blocks share one. `nil` in an unloaded chunk.
functions.example:
if block:biome() == "minecraft:snowy_plains" then
  block:set_state("minecraft:snow_block")
end

functions.name: data
functions.doc: This position's own table for scripts to keep things in, saved with the chunk: the same table every time, shared by every script. Change it in place; it's saved when the server autosaves, when the chunk unloads and when the server stops. It stays with the position, whatever happens to the block. It may hold strings, numbers, booleans, tables of them (keyed by strings, or a list numbered from 1), and the API's own values: `Vec3`s, `Location`s, `Item` tables, and `Player`, `Entity`, `Centity` and `World` handles, which come back as the same types (a handle to something gone answers `nil` or `false`, as handles do). Anything else (a function, a `Menu` window, a `Subscription`) is skipped when it's saved, with a line in the log naming where it was (`data.inventory[3]: a function can't be saved`). `nil` in an unloaded chunk.
functions.example:
local data = block:data()
if data then
  data.uses = (data.uses or 0) + 1
end

classes.name: CustomBlock
classes.doc: A block of the project's own at a position, which is a `Block` like any other: it reads the world live, so one kept from earlier turns into whatever is there now (`block:custom()` says whether it still is one). The game holds it as a state of its carrier (a note block's, tripwire's or a leaves block's) its resource pack draws as the block, so `kind()` and `state()` answer that; `id()` and `project()` say which block it is. `data()` is its own table: it starts empty when the block is placed and is gone when the block is, whatever replaced it. `break_naturally` rolls its loot table; replacing or filling over it with `set_state` or `world:fill_blocks` removes it without drops.

functions.name: id
functions.doc: Its id: its project block's folder name under `blocks/`, or `namespace:id` for one a package it depends on exports, as the calling script names it. `nil` once what's here isn't a block of the project's.

functions.name: project
functions.doc: The project block it's one of, or `nil` once what's here isn't one.

functions.name: facing
functions.doc: The way its front faces, for a block that turns (`rotation` in its `block.json`): what it was placed facing, or turned to since. `nil` for a block that doesn't turn, or once what's here isn't one.

functions.name: set_facing
functions.doc: Turns it to face another way, keeping everything else about it: its table, its centity (turned with it). `false` when it doesn't turn that way (it doesn't turn, or turns only `horizontal` and this is up or down), or once what's here isn't one of the project's blocks.

params.name: facing
params.doc: Which way its front faces.

functions.example:
local chair = block:custom()
if chair and chair:facing() ~= "north" then
  chair:set_facing("north")
end

classes.name: ProjectBlock
classes.doc: A project block from `blocks/<id>/block.json`: `this` in the block's script, and what `nf.blocks.get` hands out. It's the kind of block, not one placed in the world: its handlers hear what players do with any block of it (see `CustomBlock` for one placed). If the block is deleted, its methods answer `nil` or `false` and its handlers go.

events.name: place
events.doc: A block of this kind is about to be placed: by a player right-clicking with an item that places it (`event.player`, `event.item`), or by a script (`project_block:place`, neither set). `event:cancel()` stops it. It is heard before the world's own `block_place`, which a player's placing also raises (with the state of the game block it's held as, its carrier's, as `state`).
events.example:
this:on("place", function(event)
  if event.player and not event.player:has_permission("mine.build") then
    event:cancel()
  end
end)

events.name: break
events.doc: A player is breaking a block of this kind: before the world's own `block_break`, then `nf.on("block_break")`, with the same event, so `event:cancel()` here stops it. `event.drops` is what its loot table rolled for the tool they hold (none when `requiresTool` and it isn't the right one); assign it, and `event.experience`, to change what drops. Breaking it by a script (`break_naturally`) or an explosion rolls the same drops without this event.

events.name: click
events.doc: A player clicked a block of this kind: `event.click` is `"left"` (hitting it, which also starts breaking it) or `"right"`. It is heard after the player's own `interact` and `nf.on("player_interact")`, so one of them cancelling the click keeps it from here. `event:cancel()` stops what the click would do, which for a right click is placing something against it.
events.example:
this:on("click", function(event)
  if event.click == "right" then
    event.player:send_message("<red>Ruby ore")
  end
end)

events.name: tick
events.doc: Every `tick` ticks (the block's `tick` in `block.json`; without it nothing ticks) for each block of this kind in a loaded chunk. Blocks in chunks that aren't loaded are not ticked, and a block placed or loaded is first ticked a full interval later. Keep per-block state in `event.block:data()`.
events.example:
this:on("tick", function(event)
  local data = event.block:data()
  if data then
    data.age = (data.age or 0) + 1
  end
end)

functions.name: id
functions.doc: Its id: its folder name under `blocks/`.

functions.name: properties
functions.doc: Its `properties` from its `block.json`: the project's own facts about it, any JSON (`{ damage = 12, class = "melee" }`), as a table. A new table each call, so keep it rather than ask in a loop. An empty table when the file has none, `nil` once the block is gone.
functions.example:
local stats = assert(this:properties())
log(stats.damage)

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether the project still has it.

functions.name: place
functions.doc: Places one at the block position a location is in, as `world:set_block` would: whatever is there is replaced, and nothing drops. Its `place` handlers are not asked (a script placing a block isn't a player placing one), and it isn't a `block_place` either. If the block has a centity, it's spawned over the block. `nil` when the chunk isn't loaded, or when the game has no state of its carrier left to hold the block in (the project has more blocks of that carrier than that).

params.name: location
params.doc: Where.

functions.example:
local ore = nf.blocks.get("ruby_ore")
if ore then
  ore:place(player:location())
end

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `block:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: Inventory
classes.doc: A real inventory: a player's (`player:inventory()`), their ender chest, a storage of the project's that they keep (`player:storage(name, size)`), a container block's (`block:inventory()`: a chest, a barrel, a hopper, a furnace) or an entity's (a chest boat, a donkey, a villager). Its item methods work like `Menu`'s. The handle is where the inventory is, so it reads live; once that's gone (a chest broken, a player offline, a chunk unloaded) its methods answer `nil`, `false` or nothing. Slots are numbered from 0. A player's: the hotbar 0 to 8, the rest of the main inventory 9 to 35, armour 36 (feet), 37 (legs), 38 (chest) and 39 (head), the offhand 40, then body armour 41 and a saddle 42 (what the game keeps there for any entity). A double chest's inventory is both halves, 0 to 53.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether it's there now: the player online, the container still a container, the entity in the world and its chunk loaded.

functions.name: kind
functions.doc: What kind of inventory it is: `"player"`, `"ender_chest"`, `"storage"`, `"chest"`, `"barrel"`, `"shulker_box"`, `"hopper"`, `"dispenser"`, `"dropper"`, `"furnace"`, `"brewing"`, … `nil` once it's gone.

functions.name: size
functions.doc: How many slots it has: 43 for a player, 27 for a chest, 54 for a double chest. 0 once it's gone.

functions.name: holder
functions.doc: Whose it is: the `Player` (for a player's inventory, ender chest and storage), the `Entity`, or the `Block`. `nil` once it's gone.

functions.name: item
functions.doc: What is in a slot, or `nil` for an empty one (or once it's gone). A slot outside it is an error.

params.name: index
params.doc: From 0.

functions.name: set_item
functions.doc: Puts an item in a slot, replacing what was there, or empties it. A slot outside it, an item table with a misspelled field, or an item the server doesn't have is an error.

params.name: index
params.doc: From 0.

params.name: item
params.doc: Leave it out (or `nil`) to empty the slot.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: items
functions.doc: Every item in it, keyed by slot. Empty slots are left out, so `pairs` visits only what is there.
functions.example:
for index, item in pairs(player:inventory():items()) do
  log(index, item.kind, item.count)
end

functions.name: add_item
functions.doc: Puts an item wherever it fits, topping up matching stacks first, the way picking something up does. In a player's inventory only the hotbar and main inventory take it, never armour or the offhand.

returns.doc: How many didn't fit: 0 when all of it went in, all of it once the inventory's gone.

functions.name: remove_item
functions.doc: Takes away items that match, from the first slot on, until `count` are gone or none are left.

params.name: match
params.doc: An item kind (`"minecraft:diamond"`), or a partial `Item` that matches a stack when every field it gives matches: `{ kind = "minecraft:paper", name = "<gold>Ticket" }`. Its `data` matches as a subset, so `{ data = { coin = true } }` finds coins whatever else they carry. `count` and `raw` have no place in a match; a field `Item` doesn't have is an error.

params.name: count
params.doc: How many at most. Leave it out for every one that matches.

returns.doc: How many it took.

functions.example: local taken = player:inventory():remove_item({ kind = "minecraft:gold_nugget", data = { coin = true } }, 10)

functions.name: count_item
functions.doc: How many items match, across every slot.

params.name: match
params.doc: An item kind (`"minecraft:diamond"`), or a partial `Item` that matches a stack when every field it gives matches: `{ kind = "minecraft:paper", name = "<gold>Ticket" }`. Its `data` matches as a subset, so `{ data = { coin = true } }` finds coins whatever else they carry. `count` and `raw` have no place in a match; a field `Item` doesn't have is an error.

functions.name: has_item
functions.doc: Whether at least `count` items match.

params.name: match
params.doc: An item kind (`"minecraft:diamond"`), or a partial `Item` that matches a stack when every field it gives matches: `{ kind = "minecraft:paper", name = "<gold>Ticket" }`. Its `data` matches as a subset, so `{ data = { coin = true } }` finds coins whatever else they carry. `count` and `raw` have no place in a match; a field `Item` doesn't have is an error.

params.name: count
params.doc: Default 1.

functions.name: first_slot
functions.doc: The first slot holding an item that matches, or `nil` when none does.

params.name: match
params.doc: An item kind (`"minecraft:diamond"`), or a partial `Item` that matches a stack when every field it gives matches: `{ kind = "minecraft:paper", name = "<gold>Ticket" }`. Its `data` matches as a subset, so `{ data = { coin = true } }` finds coins whatever else they carry. `count` and `raw` have no place in a match; a field `Item` doesn't have is an error.

functions.name: clear
functions.doc: Empties every slot. To empty one, `set_item(index, nil)`.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: viewers
functions.doc: The players who have it open on their screen now: for a storage, those looking at a window with a slot bound to it. (A player's own inventory, open in their own inventory screen, doesn't count: the server can't tell.)

classes.name: BossBar
classes.doc: A bar across the top of players' screens, made by `nf.bossbars.create`. It shows to the players it's shown to (`show_to`), and stays theirs when they leave and come back. It belongs to the script that made it and goes when that script unloads (or `remove()`): from then on its methods answer `nil` or `false`.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether it's still there: `false` once it's removed or its script has unloaded.

functions.name: show_to
functions.doc: Shows it to a player, now if they're online and again whenever they join.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: hide_from
functions.doc: Stops showing it to a player.

returns.doc: Whether they were among its viewers: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: viewers
functions.doc: Everyone it's shown to, online or not: by `show_to`, and for an attached bar, whoever is near its centity now. Empty once it's gone.

functions.name: text
functions.doc: What it says, as MiniMessage, or `nil` once it's gone.

functions.name: set_text
functions.doc: Changes what it says.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: icon
functions.doc: The glyph drawn at its left end, or `nil` when it has none (or it's gone).

functions.name: set_icon
functions.doc: Draws a glyph at its left end, or none with `nil`. A glyph no resource pack has is an error.

params.name: icon
params.doc: `<pack>/<key>`, like `"ui/boss_king_slime"`, or another loaded package's as `<namespace>:<pack>/<key>` ([looks are values](packages.md#looks-are-values)).

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: progress
functions.doc: How full it is, 0 to 1, or `nil` once it's gone.

functions.name: set_progress
functions.doc: Fills it to a fraction. Outside 0 to 1 is an error.

params.name: progress
params.doc: 0 to 1.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.example: bar:set_progress(time_left / round_length)

functions.name: color
functions.doc: Its colour, or `nil` once it's gone.

functions.name: set_color
functions.doc: Changes its colour.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: style
functions.doc: Whether it's one bar or split into notches, or `nil` once it's gone.

functions.name: set_style
functions.doc: Makes it one bar, or splits it into 6, 10, 12 or 20 notches.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: attach
functions.doc: Ties it to a centity: it shows to every player within `range` of it (in its world) and hides from them as they go, and with `health` its progress follows the centity's health: what a boss's bar does. Players it was shown to with `show_to` keep it. A bar attached again moves to the new centity.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone, or the centity has.

functions.example:
local bar = nf.bossbars.create({ text = "<red>King Slime", color = "blue" })
bar:attach(this, { range = 64 })

functions.name: detach
functions.doc: Unties it from its centity: the players it showed to by being near it stop seeing it.

functions.name: attached
functions.doc: The centity it's attached to, or `nil`.

functions.name: remove
functions.doc: Takes it off every screen for good.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone already.

classes.name: Sidebar
classes.doc: The panel of lines at the right of one player's screen, from `player:sidebar()`: up to 15 lines of MiniMessage under a title, without the score numbers vanilla shows. Setting its title or lines shows it. A sidebar needs a scoreboard of the player's own, so while it shows NetherForge gives them one that copies the server's teams and the lines under name tags (the project's own changes at once, anyone else's within a second), keeping team colours and name tags working; hiding it gives them the server's back. It's cleared when they leave. For someone offline its methods answer `nil` or `false`.

functions.name: title
functions.doc: Its title, as MiniMessage, or `nil` when it has none (or they're offline).

functions.name: set_title
functions.doc: Changes its title, and shows it.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: lines
functions.doc: Its lines, top first, as MiniMessage. Empty when it has none (or they're offline).

functions.name: set_lines
functions.doc: Replaces its lines, and shows it. More than 15 is an error.

params.name: lines
params.doc: MiniMessage, top first. Lines may repeat; an empty string is a blank line.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.example:
player:sidebar():set_title("<gold><b>Arena")
player:sidebar():set_lines({ "Kills: " .. kills, "", "<gray>play.example.net" })

functions.name: is_visible
functions.doc: Whether they see it now. `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: set_visible
functions.doc: Shows it, or hides it and gives them the server's scoreboard back, keeping its title and lines for next time.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.name: clear
functions.doc: Takes its title and lines away and hides it, giving them the server's scoreboard back.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

classes.name: Team
classes.doc: A scoreboard team, made by `nf.teams.create`: what goes before and after its members' names (over their heads and in the player list), the colour of those names and of their glow, whether members can hurt each other, see each other while invisible, see name tags and push each other. Members are players and other entities. Teams live on the server's scoreboard, so every player sees them (while a player's sidebar shows, its scoreboard copies them). A team belongs to the script that made it and goes when that script unloads (a reload, the server stopping), members and all, so the script's body makes it again; from then on its methods answer `nil` or `false`. On the server's scoreboard it's called `nf.<name>` (what `/team` commands name it), so it never collides with a team made with `/team` or by another plugin, and NetherForge never touches those.

functions.name: name
functions.doc: Its name, as `nf.teams.create` was given it (without the `nf.` the scoreboard adds).

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether it's still there: `false` once it's removed or its script has unloaded.

functions.name: add_member
functions.doc: Puts a player or entity in it, taking them out of any other team they're in (one team at a time is Minecraft's rule). A player stays in it when they leave and come back, and can be added while offline.

params.name: member
params.doc: A player or any other entity.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone, or once the entity has.

functions.example: red:add_member(player)

functions.name: remove_member
functions.doc: Takes a player or entity out of it.

params.name: member
params.doc: A player or any other entity.

returns.doc: Whether they were in it: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: has_member
functions.doc: Whether a player or entity is in it. `false` once it's gone.

params.name: member
params.doc: A player or any other entity.

functions.name: members
functions.doc: Its members that are here: players online (as `Player`) and entities in loaded chunks. Empty once it has gone.

functions.name: display_name
functions.doc: What it's called where Minecraft names a team (the `/team list` output), as MiniMessage; `nil` once it's gone.

functions.name: set_display_name
functions.doc: Changes what it's called.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: prefix
functions.doc: What goes before each member's name, over their head and in the player list, as MiniMessage; `nil` once it's gone.

functions.name: set_prefix
functions.doc: Changes what goes before each member's name.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage; `""` for none.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: suffix
functions.doc: What goes after each member's name, as MiniMessage; `nil` once it's gone.

functions.name: set_suffix
functions.doc: Changes what goes after each member's name.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage; `""` for none.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: color
functions.doc: The colour of its members' names, and of their outline when they glow; `nil` when it has none (or once it's gone).

functions.name: set_color
functions.doc: Colours its members' names, and their outline when they glow (a glowing entity's outline is white otherwise). A prefix's own colours still win over it for the prefix.

params.name: color
params.doc: Leave it out for none.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.example:
red:set_color("red")
zombie:set_glowing(true)

functions.name: has_friendly_fire
functions.doc: Whether members can hurt each other. `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: set_friendly_fire
functions.doc: Lets members hurt each other, or stops them.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: can_see_invisible_teammates
functions.doc: Whether members see each other, faintly, while invisible. `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: set_can_see_invisible_teammates
functions.doc: Lets members see each other while invisible, or stops them.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: nametags
functions.doc: Who sees its members' name tags; `nil` once it's gone.

functions.name: set_nametags
functions.doc: Changes who sees its members' name tags.

params.name: visibility
params.doc: `"always"` (the default), `"never"`, `"hide_for_other_teams"` (only teammates see them) or `"hide_for_own_team"` (only players outside the team see them).

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: collision
functions.doc: Who its members push, and are pushed by; `nil` once it's gone.

functions.name: set_collision
functions.doc: Changes who its members push, and are pushed by.

params.name: rule
params.doc: `"always"` (the default), `"never"`, `"push_other_teams"` (members pass through each other) or `"push_own_team"` (members push only each other).

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone.

functions.name: remove
functions.doc: Takes it off the scoreboard for good; its members are in no team any more.

returns.doc: `false` once it's gone already.

classes.name: Database
classes.doc: A database, from `nf.db()` or `nf.db('network')`. `nf.db()` is this package's own: one SQLite file per package, kept across restarts, which every other package (a dependency, or the project using one) never sees; its tables are made by the package's `migrations/NNN_name.sql` files, applied in order when the project loads. `nf.db('network')` (a name) is a connection to a MySQL or PostgreSQL server that the server's owner set up under `databases:` in the plugin's `config.yml`: shared by every package the owner lists for it, so give tables a name no other package would (`shop_scores`), create them yourself (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`: migrations belong to the package's own database only), and write the SQL in the server's dialect. The handle is the same either way: the same calls, `?` and `params`, rows and `value, err` answers. Every function is asynchronous (see `nf.task`): the work runs on a background thread, so a slow query never holds up the server, and one database runs its work in the order it was given, so a task's `db:execute` is always done before its next `db:query`. Use it from a task (`local rows, err = db:query(...)`) or give a callback. A mistake in the SQL, a constraint a row breaks or a database that couldn't be migrated is `nil, err`, never a thrown error.

functions.name: query
functions.doc: Runs a statement that reads rows and gives them all. Each row is a table keyed by column name; a `NULL` column is left out of its row (so `row.nickname` is `nil`), integers come as `integer`s, reals as `number`s and text as `string`s; what a MySQL or PostgreSQL server has beyond those arrives as one of them (a boolean as `1` or `0`, a `DECIMAL` as a `number`, a date or time as its text, an integer too big for an `integer` as text; `CAST(column AS CHAR)` keeps a decimal exact). A column that holds a blob is an error: `hex(column)` it in the SQL (`encode(column, 'hex')` on PostgreSQL). One SQL statement in the database's own dialect (SQLite's for the package's own database; MySQL's or PostgreSQL's for a connection the server owner set up), with `?` where a value goes: the values come in `params`, never inside the text, so a name a player typed can't become SQL. A second statement after a `;` is an error: use `db:transaction` for several. On PostgreSQL a literal `?` (the JSON operators) is written `??`. It works off the main thread, so its rows arrives later: give `callback`, which is called with `rows, err` once it's done, or call it inside a task (`nf.task`) without one, and it waits and returns `rows, err`. Without a callback outside a task, it's an error. When it fails, `rows` is `nil` and `err` says why.

params.name: sql
params.doc: The statement: `"SELECT name, score FROM scores WHERE score > ?"`.

params.name: params
params.doc: The values for the `?`s, in order: `{ player_name, 5 }`. Each is a `string`, `number`, `integer` or `boolean` (stored as 1 or 0); a hole in the list (`{ 1, nil, 3 }`) is SQL `NULL`, and so are the last `?`s when the list is shorter (Lua can't tell `{ name, nil }` from `{ name }`). Any other kind of value is an error, and more values than `?`s fails the statement.

params.name: callback
params.doc: Called on the main thread once it's done, as this script's code, with the rows, in the order the statement gave them (empty when there are none) (or `nil` and why not). Not called if the script has stopped by then.

functions.example:
local db = nf.db()
nf.task(function()
  local rows, err = db:query("SELECT name, score FROM scores ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT ?", { 10 })
  if not rows then
    log("no scores: " .. err)
    return
  end
  for place, row in ipairs(rows) do
    log(place, row.name, row.score)
  end
end)

returns.doc: Only without a callback, in a task: the rows, in the order the statement gave them (empty when there are none), or `nil`.
Why it failed, when it did; `nil` when it worked.

functions.name: execute
functions.doc: Runs a statement that changes data (`INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`) and says what it changed. It's committed on its own. One SQL statement in the database's own dialect (SQLite's for the package's own database; MySQL's or PostgreSQL's for a connection the server owner set up), with `?` where a value goes: the values come in `params`, never inside the text, so a name a player typed can't become SQL. A second statement after a `;` is an error: use `db:transaction` for several. On PostgreSQL a literal `?` (the JSON operators) is written `??`. It works off the main thread, so its result arrives later: give `callback`, which is called with `result, err` once it's done, or call it inside a task (`nf.task`) without one, and it waits and returns `result, err`. Without a callback outside a task, it's an error. When it fails, `result` is `nil` and `err` says why.

params.name: sql
params.doc: The statement: `"INSERT INTO scores (name, score) VALUES (?, ?)"`.

params.name: params
params.doc: The values for the `?`s, in order: `{ player_name, 5 }`. Each is a `string`, `number`, `integer` or `boolean` (stored as 1 or 0); a hole in the list (`{ 1, nil, 3 }`) is SQL `NULL`, and so are the last `?`s when the list is shorter (Lua can't tell `{ name, nil }` from `{ name }`). Any other kind of value is an error, and more values than `?`s fails the statement.

params.name: callback
params.doc: Called on the main thread once it's done, as this script's code, with how many rows it changed and the last row it inserted (or `nil` and why not). Not called if the script has stopped by then.

functions.example:
nf.task(function()
  local result, err = nf.db():execute("INSERT INTO scores (name, score) VALUES (?, ?)", { player:name(), 10 })
  if not result then
    log("not saved: " .. err)
  end
end)

returns.doc: Only without a callback, in a task: how many rows it changed and the last row it inserted, or `nil`.
Why it failed, when it did; `nil` when it worked.

functions.name: transaction
functions.doc: Runs several statements as one: all of them happen, or, when one fails, none do (the ones before it are undone) and the error says which failed. Other work on the database waits until it is done, so nothing sees it half-way. It works off the main thread, so its results arrives later: give `callback`, which is called with `results, err` once it's done, or call it inside a task (`nf.task`) without one, and it waits and returns `results, err`. Without a callback outside a task, it's an error. When it fails, `results` is `nil` and `err` says why.

params.name: statements
params.doc: The statements, run in order. Rows they would give are ignored: a transaction changes data.

params.name: callback
params.doc: Called on the main thread once it's done, as this script's code, with what each statement changed, in the same order (or `nil` and why not). Not called if the script has stopped by then.

returns.doc: Only without a callback, in a task: what each statement changed, in the same order, or `nil`.
Why it failed, when it did; `nil` when it worked.

classes.name: Menu
