classes.doc: A live menu window from `menus/<id>/`: `this` in the menu's script, and what `player:open_menu`, `nf.menus.shared` and every menu event hand out. One that isn't `shared` exists from the moment it's opened for someone until its last viewer closes it; after that its methods return `nil` or `false` rather than erroring, and its handlers (and its slots') are gone. A shared one lives as long as the project.

events.name: open
events.doc: Someone opened this window: `player:open_menu`, or `menu:open_for`. Then the `MenuTemplate` it was made from (if it was) hears it, then `nf.on("menu_open")`.

events.name: close
events.doc: Someone closed this window, or left the server with it open. Then the `MenuTemplate` it was made from (if it was) hears it, then `nf.on("menu_close")`. When the last viewer of a window that isn't shared closes it, the window goes, and with it every handler on it.

events.name: click
events.doc: Someone clicked while this window was open, in it or in their own inventory below it. A click on one of its slots is heard by that slot first; then the menu; then the `MenuTemplate` it was made from, if it was; then `nf.on("menu_click")`. `event:cancel()` keeps it from moving anything. A locked window starts every click that would move items in or out already cancelled; `event:uncancel()` lets one through.
events.example:
this:on("click", function(event)
  if event.in_menu and event.index == 15 then
    event.player:close_menu()
    event:cancel()
  end
end)

events.name: drag
events.doc: Someone dragged a stack across slots of this window (spreading it out, or dropping one in each). Then the `MenuTemplate` it was made from (if it was) hears it. A locked window starts it already cancelled.

functions.name: id
functions.doc: This window's id: the menu's own id for a shared one, a fresh one for each window of a menu that isn't.

functions.name: kind
functions.doc: Which menu it is: its folder name under `menus/`. Nil once the window is gone, and for a window made from a `MenuTemplate` (see `template()`).

functions.name: template
functions.doc: The `MenuTemplate` this window was made from (`player:open_menu(template)`), or `nil` for a window of a menu file, and once the window or the template is gone.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether the window is still there. One that isn't shared goes when its last viewer closes it.

functions.name: is_shared
functions.doc: Whether this is the one window the whole server shares.

functions.name: context
functions.doc: What the script that opened this window passed along: `player:open_menu(menu, { context = value })`. The very value, not a copy, so a table can carry anything (the item being bought, a callback, the centity that was clicked). Every event on the window carries it too, as `event.context`. `nil` when nothing was passed, and always for a shared window, which nobody opens with a context.
functions.example:
-- opened with player:open_menu("shop", { context = { discount = 0.1 } })
local discount = (this:context() or {}).discount or 0

functions.name: size
functions.doc: How many slots it has. Slots are numbered from 0, left to right, then down.

functions.name: rows
functions.doc: How many rows of slots it has: a chest's 1 to 6, a hopper's 1, a dispenser's 3. `size() / rows()` is how many are in a row.

functions.name: title
functions.doc: The title, as MiniMessage, without the skin drawn in front of it.

functions.name: set_title
functions.doc: Renames the window. Minecraft can't rename a window that's open, so everyone looking sees it close and open again: fine between clicks, wrong every tick.

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage.

returns.doc: `false` once the window is gone.

functions.name: skin
functions.doc: The resource pack skin drawn behind it, as `<pack>/<key>`, or `nil` for the vanilla look.

functions.name: set_skin
functions.doc: Changes the background. A skin is drawn in the title, so this costs the same close-and-open `set_title` does. A skin the server's packages don't have is an error.

params.name: skin
params.doc: `<pack>/<key>`, another loaded package's as `<namespace>:<pack>/<key>` ([looks are values](packages.md#looks-are-values)), or leave it out for the vanilla look.

returns.doc: `false` once the window is gone.

functions.example: this:set_skin("ui/shop_night")

functions.name: is_locked
functions.doc: Whether clicks are kept from moving items into or out of it: such a click reaches handlers already cancelled. Scripts hear the clicks either way.

functions.name: set_locked
functions.doc: Locks or unlocks this window. Not saved: a reload goes back to what the file says.

functions.name: shift_into
functions.doc: Where a shift-click from the player's own inventory goes: into the slots of this window bound to `storage`, from `first` to `last` (storage slot indexes), in order. Stacks top up partial stacks first, then take empty slots, as vanilla does. Each slot's `click` handlers hear the move as a click on it (`event.item` is the stack moving); `event:cancel()` refuses it there, and the item goes to the next slot. Nothing else is tried: an item that no slot takes stays in the player's inventory, and a window's other slots never get it. Applies whether or not the window is locked, and each call replaces the last. A reload forgets it, so the script's body sets it again. The window must be bound to the storage (`slot:bind`), and not be `shared`.

params.name: storage
params.doc: From `player:storage(name, size)`.

params.name: first
params.doc: The first storage slot to try, from 0. Default 0.

params.name: last
params.doc: The last storage slot to try. Default the storage's last slot.

returns.doc: `false` once the window is gone.

functions.example:
nf.on("menu_open", function(event)
  -- nil while they're offline, which a player opening a menu never is.
  local trinkets = assert(event.player:storage("trinkets", 4))
  this:slot(10):bind(trinkets, 0)
  this:shift_into(trinkets)
end)

functions.name: slot
functions.doc: One of its slots, as a handle. A slot outside the window is an error. A handle is the window's id and the index, so it's fine to keep while the window lasts.

params.name: index
params.doc: From 0.

functions.example:
local buy = this:slot(13)
buy:set_item({ kind = "minecraft:emerald", name = "<green>Buy" })

functions.name: item
functions.doc: What is in a slot, or `nil` for an empty one. A slot outside the window is an error.

params.name: index
params.doc: From 0.

functions.name: set_item
functions.doc: Puts an item in a slot, replacing what was there, or empties it. An item table with a misspelled field, or an item id the server doesn't have, is an error.

params.name: index
params.doc: From 0.

params.name: item
params.doc: Leave it out (or `nil`) to empty the slot.

returns.doc: `false` once the window is gone.

functions.example:
local bread = this:item(11)
if bread then
  bread.count = bread.count - 1
  this:set_item(11, bread)
end

functions.name: add_item
functions.doc: Puts an item wherever it fits, topping up matching stacks first, the way picking something up does.

returns.doc: How many didn't fit: 0 when all of it went in.

functions.name: items
functions.doc: Every item in it, keyed by slot. Empty slots are left out, so `pairs` visits only what is there.
functions.example:
for index, item in pairs(this:items()) do
  log(index, item.kind, item.count)
end

functions.name: set_items
functions.doc: Puts several items in at once, by slot, replacing what was in those slots; the others are left alone. Every item is checked before any slot changes, so a mistake (a slot outside the window, a misspelled field, an item the server doesn't have) is an error that leaves the window as it was.

params.name: items
params.doc: Items by slot, from 0: `{ [11] = bread, [15] = cake }`.

returns.doc: `false` once the window is gone.

functions.name: fill
functions.doc: Puts a copy of one item in every empty slot, or in each of the listed slots (empty or not): a border of glass panes, say. A slot outside the window is an error.

params.name: indices
params.doc: The slots to fill, from 0. Leave it out for every empty one.

returns.doc: `false` once the window is gone.

functions.example: this:fill({ kind = "minecraft:gray_stained_glass_pane", hide_tooltip = true })

functions.name: clear
functions.doc: Empties every slot. To empty one, `set_item(index, nil)`.

returns.doc: `false` once the window is gone.

functions.name: viewers
functions.doc: Everyone looking at it now.

functions.name: cursor_item
functions.doc: What a viewer is carrying on their cursor while they have this window open, or `nil` for nothing (and when they aren't looking at it).

functions.name: set_cursor_item
functions.doc: Puts an item on a viewer's cursor, replacing what they were carrying, or empties it. What's on the cursor goes back to their inventory (or drops) when they close the window.

params.name: item
params.doc: Leave it out (or `nil`) to empty the cursor.

returns.doc: `false` when they aren't looking at this window or the window is gone.

functions.name: refresh
functions.doc: Sends the whole window to everyone looking at it again. Changes are sent by themselves, so this is only for when a viewer's screen may be out of step: after a cancelled click left a ghost item on it, say.

returns.doc: `false` once the window is gone.

functions.name: open_for
functions.doc: Shows this very window to someone too: a second pair of eyes on one menu. Its `open` handlers hear it. To give someone a window of their own, use `player:open_menu`.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline or the window is gone.

functions.name: close_for
functions.doc: Closes it for one viewer.

returns.doc: `false` when the window is gone or they weren't looking at it.

functions.name: close_all
functions.doc: Closes it for everyone looking at it.

returns.doc: `false` once the window is gone.

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `menu:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: Slot
classes.doc: One slot of one menu window, from `menu:slot(index)` (`this:slot(index)` in the menu's script). After the window goes, its methods return `nil` or `false` rather than erroring, and its handlers are gone.

events.name: click
events.doc: Someone clicked this slot. Then the menu hears it, then `nf.on("menu_click")`, unless a handler calls `event:stop()`.
events.example:
this:slot(13):on("click", function(event)
  event.player:send_message("<red>Sold out")
  event:cancel()
  event:stop()
end)

functions.name: index
functions.doc: Its number in the window, from 0.

functions.name: menu
functions.doc: The window it belongs to.

functions.name: item
functions.doc: What is in it, or `nil` when it's empty or the window is gone.

functions.name: set_item
functions.doc: Puts an item in it, replacing what was there, or empties it. An item table with a misspelled field, or an item id the server doesn't have, is an error.

params.name: item
params.doc: Leave it out (or `nil`) to empty the slot.

returns.doc: `false` once the window is gone.

functions.name: bind
functions.doc: Makes this slot a view of a slot of a player's `storage`: it shows what's there, and whatever goes in or out of it, by a click, a drag, a shift-click or a script's `set_item` on either, is saved in the storage at once, as the game moves it. So the item is only ever in one place, whatever happens next: the window closing, the player leaving or dying, the server stopping or the project reloading. In a locked window players can still put items in and take them out of a bound slot by hand (double-click gathering stays locked, and a shift-click from their own inventory goes only where `shift_into` says); its `click` handlers can still refuse what doesn't belong (`event:cancel()`). Binding a slot again moves it to the new place. Only a window of a menu that isn't `shared` can be bound, and only to a storage (`player:storage`): another inventory, or a slot outside the storage, is an error.

params.name: storage
params.doc: From `player:storage(name, size)`.

params.name: index
params.doc: Which of its slots, from 0. Default the same number as this slot.

returns.doc: `false` once the window is gone, or the storage's player is offline.

functions.example:
local trinkets = event.player:storage("trinkets", 4)
for i = 0, 3 do
  this:slot(10 + i):bind(trinkets, i)
end

functions.name: bind_equipment
functions.doc: Makes this slot a view of what a player wears in one place, as `bind` does a storage's slot: what goes in or out of it is put on or taken off at once, and when what they wear changes some other way (a right-click with armour, a script's `set_equipment`) the slot shows it by the next tick. Locked windows let players use it by hand, as a bound slot. The game doesn't check what's put on: give the slot a rule (`set_rule({ wearable = "head", max = 1 })`). Only a window of a menu that isn't `shared` can be bound.

params.name: equipment
params.doc: `head`, `chest`, `legs`, `feet` or `off_hand`.

returns.doc: `false` once the window is gone, or they're offline.

functions.example:
local slot = this:slot(11)
slot:bind_equipment(event.player, "head")
slot:set_rule({ wearable = "head", max = 1 })

functions.name: set_rule
functions.doc: Says what this slot takes, or with `nil` lets it take anything again. Whatever a player puts in, by a click, a drag, a number key or a shift-click from their own inventory into `shift_into`'s slots, is held to it: a stack it doesn't take stays where it was, and of one it does, only `max` goes in (the rest stays on the cursor). Its `click` handlers still hear what's let through. Scripts' own `set_item` aren't held to it. A shift-click from below that the game moves itself (no `shift_into`) isn't either, in a window that isn't locked.

returns.doc: `false` once the window is gone.

functions.example:
local trinkets = event.player:storage("trinkets", 4)
local slot = this:slot(10)
slot:bind(trinkets, 0)
slot:set_rule({ property = "accessory", max = 1 })

functions.name: rule
functions.doc: What this slot takes, or `nil` when it takes anything (or the window is gone).

functions.name: accepts
functions.doc: Whether this slot's rule takes this item (any count of it). `true` for a slot without a rule; `false` once the window is gone.

functions.name: unbind
functions.doc: Stops showing a storage's slot (or a player's equipment) here. The slot is emptied, since what it showed is still where it was. Its player leaving unbinds every slot bound to their storage or equipment.

returns.doc: `false` when it wasn't bound, or the window is gone.

functions.name: binding
functions.doc: Which storage slot this slot shows, or `nil` when it shows none.

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `slot:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: MenuTemplate
classes.doc: A menu made by a script with `nf.menus.create` rather than read from `menus/<id>/`: what a window opened from it starts as. Open a window of it with `player:open_menu(template)`, as many as you like, each a `Menu` of its own; handlers on the template hear every one of its windows (after the window's own handlers). It lives as long as the script that created it: when that script unloads, or `remove()` is called, its windows close and its handlers go, and its methods answer `nil` or `false` rather than erroring.

events.name: open
events.doc: Someone opened a window made from this template: after the window's own `open` handlers, before `nf.on("menu_open")`.

events.name: close
events.doc: Someone closed a window made from this template, or left the server with it open: after the window's own `close` handlers, before `nf.on("menu_close")`.

events.name: click
events.doc: Someone clicked while a window made from this template was open: after the clicked slot's and the window's handlers, before `nf.on("menu_click")`. `event.menu` is the window, `event.index` the slot. A locked template's windows start every click that would move items already cancelled; `event:uncancel()` lets one through.
events.example:
template:on("click", function(event)
  if event.in_menu and event.index == 13 then
    event.player:send_message("<green>Bought!")
  end
end)

events.name: drag
events.doc: Someone dragged a stack across slots of a window made from this template: after the window's own `drag` handlers. A locked template's windows start it already cancelled.

functions.name: id
functions.doc: Its id, made up when it was created. It never names a folder under `menus/`, and it's only good while the template lasts.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether it's still there: until `remove()`, or until the script that created it unloads.

functions.name: size
functions.doc: How many slots its windows have.

functions.name: rows
functions.doc: How many rows of slots its windows have: a chest's 1 to 6, a hopper's 1, a dispenser's 3.

functions.name: title
functions.doc: The title its windows start with, as MiniMessage, without the skin.

functions.name: skin
functions.doc: The resource pack skin its windows start with, as `<pack>/<key>`, or `nil` for the vanilla look.

functions.name: is_locked
functions.doc: Whether its windows start locked: clicks that would move items into or out of them reach handlers already cancelled.

functions.name: item
functions.doc: What a slot of a new window starts with, or `nil` for an empty one. A slot outside its windows is an error.

params.name: index
params.doc: From 0.

functions.name: windows
functions.doc: Every window made from it that is still open.

functions.name: remove
functions.doc: Takes it away before its script unloads: its windows close, and its handlers go.

returns.doc: `false` when it was already gone.

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.example:
local picker = nf.menus.create({ type = "hopper", title = "Pick one" })
picker:on("click", function(event)
  event.player:send_message("You picked slot " .. tostring(event.index))
end)

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `template:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: Dialog
classes.doc: A dialog from `dialogs/<id>/`: `this` in the dialog's script, and what `nf.dialogs.get` returns. A dialog holds nothing, so there is one of each for the whole server and showing it is all there is to do with it. Every button runs Lua with the answers to the inputs in hand; none of them is a command. Handlers on it last while the project has the dialog, across reloads of it. One made by `nf.dialogs.create` works the same way, and lasts as long as the script that made it.

events.name: press
events.doc: Someone pressed one of its buttons, with every input's answer in `event.values`: heard by the button first, then the dialog, then `nf.on("dialog_press")`. Escape on a notice is a press of its button, and on a confirmation a press of its second ("no") button.

events.name: close
events.doc: Someone left it without pressing one of its buttons: escape, or the exit button NetherForge gives a dialog (a `multi_action` dialog's "Back", a `dialog_list`'s own button, or the one standing in for a notice's or confirmation's missing button); or a script closed it (`player:close_dialog()`) or opened another dialog over it. Not when they leave the server (`player_quit` covers that), and not for escape on a notice or confirmation that has the button escape presses.

functions.name: id
functions.doc: Its folder name under `dialogs/`, or for one from `nf.dialogs.create`, an id made up for it.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether the project still has this dialog (a reload can take it away), or, for one from `nf.dialogs.create`, whether the script that made it is still running.

functions.name: title
functions.doc: Its title, as MiniMessage.

functions.name: buttons
functions.doc: The button keys, in the order they are drawn: what `event.key` can be.

functions.name: inputs
functions.doc: The input keys, in the order they are asked: the keys of `event.values`.

functions.name: button
functions.doc: One of its buttons, as a handle. A key the dialog has no button for is an error.

params.name: key
params.doc: The button's `key` in `dialog.json`.

functions.name: open_for
functions.doc: Puts it on someone's screen. It's built fresh each time, so what they see is the dialog as it is now, with whatever `options` change for this opening. A project dialog already on their screen is closed (its `close` handlers hear it).

params.name: options
params.doc: What to open it with, for this opening only. A key it doesn't take, an input or body element the dialog doesn't have, or a value of the wrong kind for its input is an error.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline or the dialog is gone.

functions.name: ask
functions.doc: Opens it for `player` and pauses the task until they answer: returns their press, or `nil` if they close it (see the `close` event: escape through NetherForge's exit button, or a script closing it or opening another dialog over it), leave the server, or it couldn't be opened (they're offline, or the dialog is gone). The press still goes to the dialog's handlers and `nf.on("dialog_press")` as usual; `ask` hears it at the dialog, so a button handler that calls `event:stop()` hides it from `ask` too.

params.name: options
params.doc: What to open it with, as for `open_for`.

functions.example:
nf.task(function()
  local answer = nf.dialogs.get("confirm"):ask(player)
  if answer and answer.key == "yes" then
    player:send_message("<green>Done.")
  end
end)

functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: Button
classes.doc: One button of a dialog, from `dialog:button(key)` (`this:button(key)` in the dialog's script). If a reload takes the button away, its methods return `nil` rather than erroring, and its handlers are gone.

events.name: press
events.doc: Someone pressed this button. Then the dialog hears it, then `nf.on("dialog_press")`, unless a handler calls `event:stop()`.

functions.name: key
functions.doc: Its `key` in `dialog.json`: what `event.key` is when it's pressed.

functions.name: dialog
functions.doc: The dialog it belongs to.

functions.name: label
functions.doc: What it says, as MiniMessage, or `nil` once the dialog no longer has it.

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.doc: Like `button:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: ProjectItem
classes.doc: A project item from `items/<id>/item.json`: `this` in the item's script, and what `nf.items.get` hands out. It's the item itself, not one stack of it: its handlers hear what players do with any stack of it, wherever the stack came from. A stack of it is an `Item` table whose `item` is this id. If the item is deleted, its methods answer `nil` or `false` and its handlers go.

events.name: use
events.doc: A player right-clicked with a stack of this item in hand: `event.item` is the stack, `event.hand` which hand. Then the player's own `use_item`, then `nf.on("player_use_item")`, with the same event, so `event:cancel()` here cancels it for all of them and `event:stop()` keeps it from them. `event:cancel()` stops the item being used.

events.name: interact
events.doc: A player clicked a block or the air holding a stack of this item: `event.click` is `"left"` or `"right"`, `event.block` the block (`nil` for the air), `event.item` the stack. Then the player's own `interact`, then `nf.on("player_interact")`, with the same event, so `event:cancel()` here cancels it for all of them and `event:stop()` keeps it from them.

events.name: interact_entity
events.doc: A player right-clicked an entity (not a centity) holding a stack of this item in `event.hand`; read the stack with `event.player:held_item()` (or `off_hand_item()`). The entity's own `interact` handlers hear it first, then this item's. Then the player's own `interact_entity`, then `nf.on("player_interact_entity")`, with the same event, so `event:cancel()` here cancels it for all of them and `event:stop()` keeps it from them.

events.name: consume
events.doc: A player finished eating or drinking a stack of this item (`event.item`). Then the player's own `consume_item`, then `nf.on("player_consume_item")`, with the same event, so `event:cancel()` here cancels it for all of them and `event:stop()` keeps it from them.

events.name: hit
events.doc: A player is attacking an entity with a stack of this item in their main hand: `event.attacker` is the player, `event.entity` who is hit, `event.amount` the damage (writable). Read the stack with `event.attacker:held_item()`. Then the entity's own `damage`, then `nf.on("entity_damage")`, with the same event.

events.name: break_block
events.doc: A player is breaking a block with a stack of this item in their main hand (read it with `event.player:held_item()`). Then the world's own `block_break`, then `nf.on("block_break")`, with the same event; assign `event.drops` and `event.experience` to change what it drops.

events.name: drop
events.doc: A player is dropping a stack of this item (`event.item`). Then the player's own `drop_item`, then `nf.on("player_drop_item")`, with the same event, so `event:cancel()` here cancels it for all of them and `event:stop()` keeps it from them.

events.name: render
events.doc: The server is making a stack of this item, or rewriting one to the item's file after it changed: assign `event.display_name` and `event.lore` to give it a name and lore worked out from the stack (its `data`, its count), which the file's can't say: a prefix in the name, stats in the lore. It's heard for every stack `nf.items.create`, `ProjectItem:create` and a loot roll make, and for every stack that takes a changed file's look, so a name worked out here survives the file changing (one set any other way goes back to the file's then). A stack whose `data` a script changes keeps its name until it's made again: hand it to `nf.items.create` with its `data` to work it out anew.
events.example:
this:on("render", function(event)
  local prefix = event.item.data and event.item.data.prefix
  if prefix then
    event.display_name = "<green>" .. prefix .. " Copper Sword"
  end
end)

events.name: view
events.doc: A stack of this item is being sent to one player's game: their inventory (hotbar, armour and offhand too), a window they have open, the stack on their cursor. Assign `event.display_name` and `event.lore` to change how it looks to `event.player` alone, now: a price while they have a shop open, a hint for their class. Nothing the server keeps changes: not the stack, how it stacks, what's saved, what anyone else sees, nor what scripts read from inventories. Both start as the stack's own (after its `render`), so this adds to them. The game is sent a stack again only when it changes, so call `player:refresh_items()` when what this works out from changes (a menu opening or closing). If a handler fails, the stack is sent as it is. Then `nf.on("item_view")`, with the same event; `event:stop()` keeps it from there.
events.example:
this:on("view", function(event)
  local menu = event.player:menu()
  if menu and menu:kind() == "shop" then
    local lore = event.lore or {}
    lore[#lore + 1] = "<gold>Sells for 5 coins"
    event.lore = lore
  end
end)

events.name: pickup
events.doc: A player is picking up a stack of this item (`event.item`) from the item entity `event.entity`. Then the player's own `pickup_item`, then `nf.on("player_pickup_item")`, with the same event, so `event:cancel()` here cancels it for all of them and `event:stop()` keeps it from them.

functions.name: id
functions.doc: Its id: its folder name under `items/`.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether the project still has it.

functions.name: create
functions.doc: A stack of it, as an `Item` table: the same as `nf.items.create(this:id(), overrides)`. `nil` once the item is gone.

params.name: overrides
params.doc: `Item` fields for this stack: `{ count = 3, data = { found = "cave" } }`. A field the item's file sets is replaced only until the file changes (see `nf.items.create`).

functions.name: properties
functions.doc: Its `properties` from its `item.json`: the project's own facts about it, any JSON (`{ damage = 12, class = "melee" }`), as a table. A new table each call, so keep it rather than ask in a loop. An empty table when the file has none, `nil` once the item is gone.
functions.example:
local stats = assert(this:properties())
log(stats.damage)

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `item:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: Effect
classes.doc: One playing particle effect, from `nf.particles.play`. Once it has ended (it finished, was stopped, lost what it followed, its file was deleted, or the script that played it unloaded) its methods answer `nil` or `false` rather than erroring, except `kind()`. An effect is ephemeral: it has no `id()` and can't be saved in a `data()` table.

events.name: end
events.doc: The effect ended, for any reason (`event.reason` says which): heard once, while the handle still answers (`is_active()` is still true and `location()` says where it was; `stop()` is `false`, as it's already ending), so `nf.wait_for(effect, "end")` hands back the event. After it, the effect is gone and so is every handler on it. A looping effect never ends `"finished"`.
events.example:
effect:on("end", function(event)
  if event.reason == "target_gone" then
    log("they left before it was over")
  end
end)

functions.name: kind
functions.doc: Which effect it is: its folder name under `particles/`, even after it has ended.

functions.name: is_active
functions.doc: Whether it's still playing. `false` once it has ended, for any reason (its `end` handlers still see `true`).

functions.name: stop
functions.doc: Ends it now, with reason `"stopped"`. Particles already spawned live out their short lives on the players' screens.

returns.doc: `false` when it had already ended.

functions.name: location
functions.doc: Where it is now, facing the way it faces: in world space. `nil` once it has ended.

functions.name: teleport
functions.doc: Moves it, and stops it following anything. A `Location`'s `yaw` and `pitch` become its facing (nil is 0); a `Vec3` keeps its world and its facing.

params.name: location_or_position
params.doc: Where to, in world space.

returns.doc: `false` once it has ended.

functions.name: follow
functions.doc: Makes it follow something, from the next tick on. Each tick, before it spawns anything, the effect moves to the target: its position (a node's `world_position()`), facing the target's yaw (a node's centity's), pitch 0. When the target stops existing (a removed centity, a player who left, an entity that died or was removed, a centity or entity whose chunk unloaded) the effect ends with reason `"target_gone"`. Calling it again switches targets; `teleport` stops following.

params.name: target
params.doc: What to follow.

params.name: offset
params.doc: Where the effect sits from the target, in the effect's own space (turned with the target's yaw): `vec3(0, 2, 0)` is above its head, `vec3(0, 0, 1)` in front. Default `vec3.zero`.

returns.doc: `false` once it has ended.

functions.example:
local here = player:location()
local halo = here and nf.particles.play("halo", here, { loop = true })
if halo then
  halo:follow(player, vec3(0, 2.2, 0))
end

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.example:
local here = this:location()
local effect = here and nf.particles.play("sparkle", here)
if effect then
  effect:on("end", function(event)
    log("sparkle ended:", event.reason)
  end)
end

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `effect:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: HttpStream
classes.doc: A streamed HTTP response, from `nf.http.stream`: its `open`, each `message` and its one `end` are events on it. It belongs to the script that opened it and ends with reason `"unloaded"` when that script unloads (a reload, the server stopping). Once it has ended its methods answer as an ended stream does rather than erroring. Ephemeral: it can't be saved in a `data()` table.

events.name: open
events.doc: The response has begun: its status and headers are in. Any status opens it, so check `event.status`: an error's body arrives as messages like any other. Heard at most once, never after `end`.

events.name: message
events.doc: A piece of the response arrived: a line, a Server-Sent Event or a chunk, as the stream's `format` says. Messages come in order, on the main thread, a limited number a tick per stream (`connections.messages-per-tick`); while scripts haven't taken them, at most `connections.max-queued-messages` wait and the server stops reading from the network, so nothing is ever dropped.

events.name: end
events.doc: The stream ended, for any reason (`event.reason` says which): heard once, after every message that arrived before it, while the handle still answers. After it, every handler on the stream is gone. Opening a new stream is how to reconnect.
events.example:
stream:on("end", function(event)
  if event.reason == "failed" then
    log("feed failed: " .. event.detail)
  end
end)

functions.name: url
functions.doc: The URL it was opened with, even after it has ended.

functions.name: state
functions.doc: `"connecting"` until its `open` event, then `"open"`, and `"ended"` once its `end` event has been heard.

functions.name: status
functions.doc: The response's status code once it has opened (`200`, `404`); `nil` before, and once it has ended (its `end` event has it).

functions.name: close
functions.doc: Ends it now, with reason `"closed"`: the connection is dropped and messages that arrived but weren't handed over yet are thrown away.

returns.doc: `false` when it had already ended.

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.example:
local stream = nf.http.stream({ url = "https://feed.example.com/live.ndjson" })
stream:on("message", function(event)
  local item = nf.json.decode(event.data)
  log("got", item.kind)
end)

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `stream:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: WebSocket
classes.doc: A WebSocket, from `nf.http.websocket`: `send` text on it, and hear its `open`, each `message` and its one `end` as events. It belongs to the script that opened it and ends with reason `"unloaded"` when that script unloads (a reload, the server stopping). Once it has ended its methods answer as an ended socket does rather than erroring. Ephemeral: it can't be saved in a `data()` table.

events.name: open
events.doc: The connection is made and ready. What `send` sent before it goes now, in order. Heard at most once, never after `end`.

events.name: message
events.doc: A text message arrived. Messages come in order, on the main thread, a limited number a tick per socket (`connections.messages-per-tick`); while scripts haven't taken them, at most `connections.max-queued-messages` wait and the server stops reading from the network, so nothing is ever dropped. A binary message isn't taken: the socket is closed (code `1003`) and ends `"failed"`.

events.name: end
events.doc: The socket ended, for any reason (`event.reason` says which): heard once, after every message that arrived before it, while the handle still answers. After it, every handler on the socket is gone. Opening a new socket is how to reconnect.

functions.name: url
functions.doc: The URL it was opened with, even after it has ended.

functions.name: state
functions.doc: `"connecting"` until its `open` event, then `"open"`, and `"ended"` once its `end` event has been heard.

functions.name: protocol
functions.doc: The subprotocol the other side chose from `options.protocols`, while it's open; `nil` before and after, or when it chose none.

functions.name: send
functions.doc: Sends a text message. Before the socket opens it waits and goes, in order, once it does. A message over `connections.max-message-bytes` is an error at the script's line; one past the package's `connections.bytes-per-minute` ends the socket (reason `"limit"`) instead of going.

params.name: text
params.doc: The message, as text (UTF-8).

returns.doc: `false` when the socket has ended (or just ended over the limit), so nothing was sent.

functions.example: socket:send(nf.json.encode({ op = 1, d = sequence }))

functions.name: close
functions.doc: Ends it now, with reason `"closed"`: the other side is told with `code` and `reason`, and messages that arrived but weren't handed over yet are thrown away.

params.name: code
params.doc: The close code: `1000` (a normal close, the default) or one from `3000` to `4999`, which applications define.

params.name: reason
params.doc: Why, for the other side to read: at most 123 bytes.

returns.doc: `false` when it had already ended.

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.example:
local socket = nf.http.websocket({ url = "wss://chat.example.com/live" })
socket:on("message", function(event)
  log("said:", event.data)
end)

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `socket:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: Route
classes.doc: A route a script answers, from `nf.web.route`. It goes when its script unloads or `remove` is called.

functions.name: remove
functions.doc: Stops answering: later requests to it are `404`, and requests still waiting are answered `503`.

returns.doc: `false` when it was already gone.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether it still answers.

classes.name: WebResponse
classes.doc: How a route's handler answers its request: once, with `send`, `json` or `redirect`, during the handler or later (from a task, or a callback). Every answer also says `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and `Cache-Control: no-store` unless you set one. One not answered within `web.handler-timeout-seconds` is answered `504`; one whose route's script unloads first, `503`. Ephemeral: it can't be saved in a `data()` table.

functions.name: send
functions.doc: Answers with `status`, `body` and `headers`. The `Content-Type` is `text/plain; charset=utf-8` unless `headers` sets one (`["content-type"] = "text/html; charset=utf-8"` for a page). A body over `web.max-response-bytes`, a status that isn't one, or a header that can't be sent (one the server sets, like `Content-Length`) is an error at the script's line.

params.name: body
params.doc: The body, as text (UTF-8). Default empty.

params.name: headers
params.doc: Response headers by name.

returns.doc: `false` when it was already answered (or timed out), so nothing was sent.

functions.example:
response:send(200, "

Hello

", { ["content-type"] = "text/html; charset=utf-8" })

functions.name: json
functions.doc: Answers with `status` and `value` written as JSON (`application/json`), as `nf.json.encode` writes it.

params.name: status
params.doc: The status code, 100 to 599.

params.name: value
params.doc: What to write: a table, a string, a number, a boolean.

returns.doc: `false` when it was already answered.

functions.example: response:json(200, { online = #nf.players.online() })

functions.name: redirect
functions.doc: Answers with a redirect to `url` (`302`, or `status`: `301`, `303`, `307` or `308`).

params.name: url
params.doc: Where to: an absolute URL, or a path on this server.

params.name: status
params.doc: Default `302`.

returns.doc: `false` when it was already answered.

functions.name: is_pending
functions.doc: Whether it still waits for an answer: `false` once it's answered, timed out, or its route's script unloaded.

classes.name: OAuthFlow
classes.doc: A "log in with…" flow, from `nf.web.oauth`: `begin` a login for a player, and hear its `complete` or `fail`. It belongs to the script that made it.

events.name: complete
events.doc: A player finished logging in: the service sent them back, and the server traded the code for a token. Their browser is shown a page saying they can go back to the game.

events.name: fail
events.doc: A player's login didn't finish: they declined, the service answered with an error, the token couldn't be had, or the login expired (10 minutes after `begin`). Their browser is shown a page saying so. A callback that matches no login of this flow (forged, or used twice) is refused with no event.

functions.name: begin
functions.doc: Begins a login for `player`: the address of the service's page to send them to (as a link in chat), with a new state and code challenge that only this login's callback can use, for 10 minutes. `nil` while the server owner hasn't turned web routes on, or once the flow has gone.

params.name: player
params.doc: Who logs in: their `complete` or `fail` names them.

functions.name: remove
functions.doc: Ends the flow: its callback route goes and logins under way are forgotten.

returns.doc: `false` when it was already gone.

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `flow:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: WasmInstance
classes.doc: An instance of a WebAssembly module, from `nf.wasm.instantiate`: its own memory, kept from call to call, so a function can build state another reads. Its calls run off the main thread one at a time, in the order they were made. It belongs to the script that made it and is closed when that script unloads. Ephemeral: it can't be saved in a `data()` table.

functions.name: module
functions.doc: The module it is an instance of, as the calling script names it.

functions.name: call
functions.doc: Calls one of the functions the module exports and gives its results. It's stopped past `wasm.max-call-seconds`; a call that traps (an out-of-bounds read, `unreachable`, a division by zero) or is stopped fails with `nil, err`, and the instance is closed after it (its memory may be half-written). It works off the main thread, so its results arrives later: give `callback`, which is called with `results, err` once it's done, or call it inside a task (`nf.task`) without one, and it waits and returns `results, err`. Without a callback outside a task, it's an error. When it fails, `results` is `nil` and `err` says why.

params.name: name
params.doc: The exported function: `"sample"`.

params.name: arguments
params.doc: The arguments, in order, one for each of the function's parameters: an `integer` for an `i32` or `i64`, a `number` for an `f32` or `f64`. A `string` is copied into the module's memory and passed as two `i32`s, where it starts and how many bytes it is (UTF-8): the module must export its `memory` and an `alloc(size) -> pointer` (or `malloc`) to copy it into, and the server frees it after the call with the module's `dealloc(pointer, size)` (or `free(pointer)`) when it exports one, so a function that keeps the text copies it. A count or type that doesn't match the function is an error at the script's line.

params.name: callback
params.doc: Called on the main thread once it's done, as this script's code, with its results in order (an `i32` or `i64` as an `integer`, an `f32` or `f64` as a `number`), empty for a function that returns nothing (or `nil` and why not). Not called if the script has stopped by then.

functions.example:
nf.task(function()
  local results, err = instance:call("add", { 2, 3 })
  assert(results and results[1] == 5, err)
end)

returns.doc: Only without a callback, in a task: its results in order (an `i32` or `i64` as an `integer`, an `f32` or `f64` as a `number`), empty for a function that returns nothing, or `nil`.
Why it failed, when it did; `nil` when it worked.

functions.name: call_text
functions.doc: Calls a function that answers with text: it returns two `i32`s (where the text starts and how many bytes it is) or one `i64` holding both (the start in its high 32 bits). The text is read from the module's memory as UTF-8, then freed as `call` frees a string argument. Otherwise as `call`: for text in and text out, JSON included. It works off the main thread, so its text arrives later: give `callback`, which is called with `text, err` once it's done, or call it inside a task (`nf.task`) without one, and it waits and returns `text, err`. Without a callback outside a task, it's an error. When it fails, `text` is `nil` and `err` says why.

params.name: name
params.doc: The exported function: `"plan"`.

params.name: arguments
params.doc: The arguments, in order, one for each of the function's parameters: an `integer` for an `i32` or `i64`, a `number` for an `f32` or `f64`. A `string` is copied into the module's memory and passed as two `i32`s, where it starts and how many bytes it is (UTF-8): the module must export its `memory` and an `alloc(size) -> pointer` (or `malloc`) to copy it into, and the server frees it after the call with the module's `dealloc(pointer, size)` (or `free(pointer)`) when it exports one, so a function that keeps the text copies it. A count or type that doesn't match the function is an error at the script's line.

params.name: callback
params.doc: Called on the main thread once it's done, as this script's code, with the text it answered (or `nil` and why not). Not called if the script has stopped by then.

functions.example:
nf.task(function()
  local answer, err = instance:call_text("plan", { nf.json.encode({ from = 1, to = 9 }) })
  if answer then
    local plan = nf.json.decode(answer)
    log("the plan has", #plan.steps, "steps")
  end
end)

returns.doc: Only without a callback, in a task: the text it answered, or `nil`.
Why it failed, when it did; `nil` when it worked.

functions.name: close
functions.doc: Closes it now, freeing its memory: calls still waiting fail, and later ones do at once. Unloading the script that made it closes it too.

returns.doc: `false` when it was already closed.

classes.name: WasmProcess
classes.doc: A program started with `nf.wasm.start`: `send` it lines and hear each line it prints as `output`, then its one `end`. It runs on a thread of its own, waiting while it reads input nobody has sent. It belongs to the script that started it and ends with reason `"unloaded"` when that script unloads (a reload, the server stopping). Once it has ended its methods answer as an ended program does rather than erroring. Ephemeral: it can't be saved in a `data()` table.

events.name: output
events.doc: The program printed a line (to its standard output or error), without its line ending. Lines come in order, on the main thread, at most `wasm.lines-per-tick` a tick per program; while scripts haven't taken them, at most `wasm.max-queued-lines` wait and the program is paused when it prints the next, so nothing is dropped. A line longer than `wasm.max-line-bytes` comes in pieces of that size.

events.name: end
events.doc: The program ended, for any reason (`event.reason` says which): heard once, after every line it printed before, while the handle still answers. After it, every handler on the program is gone; start it again to restart it.
events.example:
engine:on("end", function(event)
  if event.reason ~= "unloaded" then
    log("engine ended:", event.reason, event.exit_code, event.detail)
  end
end)

functions.name: module
functions.doc: The module it runs, as the calling script names it, even after it has ended.

functions.name: state
functions.doc: `"running"` until its `end` event, then `"ended"`.

functions.name: send
functions.doc: Writes a line to its input, with a line ending after it: the program reads it when it next reads. A line over `wasm.max-line-bytes` is an error at the script's line.

params.name: line
params.doc: The line, without its line ending: `"go movetime 500"`.

returns.doc: `false` when it has ended or its input was closed, so nothing was sent.

functions.example: engine:send("position startpos moves e2e4 e7e5")

functions.name: close_input
functions.doc: Ends its input: once it has read what was sent, it reads the end of the file, which most programs answer by finishing what they were doing and exiting.

returns.doc: `false` when it had already ended or its input was closed.

functions.name: stop
functions.doc: Ends it now, with reason `"stopped"`: lines it printed that weren't handed over yet are thrown away.

returns.doc: `false` when it had already ended.

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.example:
local engine = nf.wasm.start("stockfish")
engine:on("output", function(event)
  log("engine says:", event.line)
end)

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `engine:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: NetworkChannel
classes.doc: A channel of the network, from `nf.network.channel`: publish on it with `publish`, ask one server with `request`, and hear messages and requests as its `message` and `request` events. A server listens to a channel while any of its scripts has a handler on it; handlers go with their scripts, as any handler does.

events.name: message
events.doc: Something was published on the channel, by any server of the network (this one included): to every server, or to this one alone. While a script of this server has a handler on it, the server listens to the channel; a message published while it had none never arrives.

events.name: request
events.doc: Another server (or this one) asked this server on the channel (`channel:request`): assign `event.reply` the answer, which goes back as it is once the handlers have run. Handlers run in order and the last value assigned is the answer; with none assigned the asker gets `nil`. Answer in the handler: the asker is waiting.

functions.name: name
functions.doc: Its name, as the calling package names it: bare when it's the caller's own, `namespace:name` otherwise.

functions.name: publish
functions.doc: Publishes `value` on the channel: every server listening hears it as a `message` event, this one included, or only `options.server`. It goes at once, through the hub; nothing waits for it. Anything a `data()` table can hold, sent as JSON with the same codec: tables, strings, numbers, booleans, `Vec3`, `Location` (its world by name) and handles to entities and worlds (by UUID and name, which another server may not have). At most `max-value-bytes` as JSON (the proxy's `hub.properties`, 64 KiB unless its owner says otherwise); a value over it, or one that can't be written as JSON, is an error at the script's line.

params.name: value
params.doc: What to send.

params.name: options
params.doc: Which server alone, if not every one.

returns.doc: `false` when it didn't go: this server isn't connected, or its package went over `network.messages-per-minute`.

functions.example: nf.network.channel("alerts"):publish({ text = "Restarting in 5 minutes" })

functions.name: request
functions.doc: Asks `server` on this channel: its `request` handlers answer, and the answer comes back here. It fails (`nil, err`) when this server isn't connected, that server isn't, nothing there handles requests on the channel, a handler there errored, or no answer came within `network.request-timeout-seconds`. A handler that answers `nil` gives `nil` with no `err`. Anything a `data()` table can hold, sent as JSON with the same codec: tables, strings, numbers, booleans, `Vec3`, `Location` (its world by name) and handles to entities and worlds (by UUID and name, which another server may not have). At most `max-value-bytes` as JSON (the proxy's `hub.properties`, 64 KiB unless its owner says otherwise); a value over it, or one that can't be written as JSON, is an error at the script's line. It works off the main thread, so its reply arrives later: give `callback`, which is called with `reply, err` once it's done, or call it inside a task (`nf.task`) without one, and it waits and returns `reply, err`. Without a callback outside a task, it's an error. When it fails, `reply` is `nil` and `err` says why.

params.name: server
params.doc: The server's name in the network, as the proxy names it (`"lobby"`); `nf.network.servers()` lists them.

params.name: data
params.doc: What to ask with: their handlers read it as `event.value`.

params.name: callback
params.doc: Called on the main thread once it's done, as this script's code, with the answer, what that server's handlers assigned to `event.reply` (or `nil` and why not). Not called if the script has stopped by then.

functions.example:
nf.task(function()
  local price, err = nf.network.channel("prices"):request("survival", "diamond")
  if err then
    log("survival didn't answer: " .. err)
  else
    log("a diamond costs", price)
  end
end)

returns.doc: Only without a callback, in a task: the answer, what that server's handlers assigned to `event.reply`, or `nil`.
Why it failed, when it did; `nil` when it worked.

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.example:
local alerts = nf.network.channel("alerts")
alerts:on("message", function(event)
  nf.server.broadcast("<red>" .. event.value.text)
end)

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `channel:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: NetworkMap
classes.doc: A map the whole network shares, from `nf.network.map`: string keys, any values. Reads (`get`, `all`) answer at once from this server's copy. Writes go to the hub, which makes them in the order they arrive and tells every server that has the map: `set` and `delete` don't wait, and this server's copy has the new value once the hub has made the change (the next tick or so, when `change` is heard); `add` and `insert` wait for the hub's answer, so they're safe when two servers write one key at once. A key may expire. The hub keeps them for the whole network, saved on the proxy, within the limits of its `hub.properties` (how many keys and bytes each package may keep).

events.name: change
events.doc: A key of the map changed, on any server of the network (this one included), or expired: heard on every server that has the map, once the hub has made the change, in the order the hub made changes. This server's copy has the new value when it's heard.
events.example:
local scores = nf.network.map("scores")
scores:on("change", function(event)
  log(event.key .. " is " .. tostring(event.value) .. " (" .. event.cause .. " on " .. tostring(event.server) .. ")")
end)

events.name: ready
events.doc: This server's copy of the map arrived from the hub for the first time, so `get` and `all` answer with what the network holds. Heard once.

functions.name: name
functions.doc: Its name, as the calling package names it: bare when it's the caller's own, `namespace:name` otherwise.

functions.name: is_ready
functions.doc: Whether this server's copy has arrived from the hub: until then `get` answers `nil` and `all` an empty table. Its `ready` event says when.

functions.name: get
functions.doc: A key's value in this server's copy, or `nil` when it has none (or the copy hasn't arrived). A table comes back new each call: changing it changes nothing.

params.name: key
params.doc: The key.

functions.name: all
functions.doc: Every key and its value in this server's copy.

functions.name: set
functions.doc: Sets a key, for the whole network: through the hub, without waiting. Anything a `data()` table can hold, sent as JSON with the same codec: tables, strings, numbers, booleans, `Vec3`, `Location` (its world by name) and handles to entities and worlds (by UUID and name, which another server may not have). At most `max-value-bytes` as JSON (the proxy's `hub.properties`, 64 KiB unless its owner says otherwise); a value over it, or one that can't be written as JSON, is an error at the script's line. A key is 1 to 256 characters. What the hub refuses (a package over its limits) is logged.

params.name: key
params.doc: The key.

params.name: value
params.doc: Its value. `nil` deletes it, as `delete` does.

params.name: options
params.doc: When the key expires, if it should.

returns.doc: `false` when it didn't go: this server isn't connected, or its package went over `network.messages-per-minute`.

functions.example:
local parties = nf.network.map("parties")
parties:set(player:id(), { leader = player:name() }, { expires = 20 * 60 * 30 })

functions.name: delete
functions.doc: Deletes a key, for the whole network: through the hub, without waiting.

params.name: key
params.doc: The key.

returns.doc: `false` when it didn't go: this server isn't connected, or its package went over `network.messages-per-minute`.

functions.name: add
functions.doc: Adds `amount` to a key's number, made by the hub in one step: two servers adding at once both count. A key with no value starts at 0; one holding something that isn't a number fails. It keeps the expiry it had, unless `options.expires` gives a new one. It works off the main thread, so its total arrives later: give `callback`, which is called with `total, err` once it's done, or call it inside a task (`nf.task`) without one, and it waits and returns `total, err`. Without a callback outside a task, it's an error. When it fails, `total` is `nil` and `err` says why.

params.name: key
params.doc: The key.

params.name: amount
params.doc: What to add; negative to take away.

params.name: options
params.doc: When the key expires, if it should.

params.name: callback
params.doc: Called on the main thread once it's done, as this script's code, with the key's value after adding (or `nil` and why not). Not called if the script has stopped by then.

functions.example:
nf.task(function()
  local total = nf.network.map("stats"):add("games_played", 1)
  log("games played across the network:", total)
end)

returns.doc: Only without a callback, in a task: the key's value after adding, or `nil`.
Why it failed, when it did; `nil` when it worked.

functions.name: insert
functions.doc: Sets a key to `data` only if it has no value, made by the hub in one step: of two servers inserting one key at once, exactly one gets `true`. A claim, a lock or a reservation: give it `options.expires` so a server that stops holding it can't keep it forever. It works off the main thread, so its inserted arrives later: give `callback`, which is called with `inserted, err` once it's done, or call it inside a task (`nf.task`) without one, and it waits and returns `inserted, err`. Without a callback outside a task, it's an error. When it fails, `inserted` is `nil` and `err` says why.

params.name: key
params.doc: The key.

params.name: data
params.doc: Its value. Anything a `data()` table can hold, sent as JSON with the same codec: tables, strings, numbers, booleans, `Vec3`, `Location` (its world by name) and handles to entities and worlds (by UUID and name, which another server may not have). At most `max-value-bytes` as JSON (the proxy's `hub.properties`, 64 KiB unless its owner says otherwise); a value over it, or one that can't be written as JSON, is an error at the script's line.

params.name: options
params.doc: When the key expires, if it should.

params.name: callback
params.doc: Called on the main thread once it's done, as this script's code, with `true` when it was set, `false` when the key already had a value (or `nil` and why not). Not called if the script has stopped by then.

functions.example:
nf.task(function()
  local mine = nf.network.map("arenas"):insert("arena_1", nf.network.server_name(), { expires = 20 * 60 })
  if mine then
    log("arena_1 is this server's for a minute")
  end
end)

returns.doc: Only without a callback, in a task: `true` when it was set, `false` when the key already had a value, or `nil`.
Why it failed, when it did; `nil` when it worked.

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.example:
local scores = nf.network.map("scores")
scores:on("change", function(event)
  log(event.key, "is now", event.value)
end)

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `map:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: Cutscene
classes.doc: One cutscene playing for one player, from `nf.cutscenes.play`. Once it has ended (it finished, was stopped or skipped, was replaced by another, its player left, or the script that played it unloaded) its methods answer `nil` or `false` rather than erroring, except `kind()` and `length()`. A cutscene is ephemeral: it has no `id()` and can't be saved in a `data()` table.

events.name: end
events.doc: The cutscene ended, for any reason (`event.reason` says which): heard once, after the player has been put back (so a handler that moves them or changes their game mode has the last word), while the handle still answers (`is_active()` is still true; `stop()` is `false`, as it is already ending), so `nf.wait_for(cutscene, "end")` hands back the event. After it, the cutscene is gone and so is every handler on it. When the player left, `event.player` is them offline.
events.example:
local scene = nf.cutscenes.play(player, "intro")
if scene then
  scene:on("end", function(event)
    if event.reason == "skipped" then
      event.player:send_message("<gray>You skipped the intro.")
    end
  end)
end

events.name: cue
events.doc: The cutscene reached a cue that names an `event` (`cues` in its file), at that time.
events.example:
local scene = nf.cutscenes.play(player, "intro")
if scene then
  scene:on("cue", function(event)
    if event.cue == "boom" then
      event.player:play_sound("minecraft:entity.generic.explode")
    end
  end)
end

functions.name: kind
functions.doc: Which cutscene it is: its file name under `cutscenes/`, even after it has ended.

functions.name: length
functions.doc: How long it lasts, in seconds, even after it has ended.

functions.name: player
functions.doc: Who is watching. `nil` once it has ended.

functions.name: is_active
functions.doc: Whether it's still playing. `false` once it has ended, for any reason (its `end` handlers still see `true`).

functions.name: time
functions.doc: Seconds played so far. `nil` once it has ended.

functions.name: stop
functions.doc: Ends it now, with reason `"stopped"`, and puts the player back.

returns.doc: `false` when it had already ended.

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.example:
local intro = nf.cutscenes.play(player, "intro")
if intro then
  intro:on("end", function(event)
    log("intro ended:", event.reason)
  end)
end

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `cutscene:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: Screen
classes.doc:
A screen: maps (each 128 by 128 pixels) side by side, which scripts draw on and play videos on, shown in item frames (`place`, or the file's `place`) or as map items in players' hands (`item`). Pixel `0, 0` is its top left. What it shows is the server's to send and isn't saved: draw it whenever its script starts. Once a screen is gone (a script's screen whose script unloaded, a project screen whose file was deleted) its drawing does nothing and its getters answer `nil` or `false`.

A screen is drawn for every player near it (`viewers = "near"`), or only for those a script shows it to. `for_player` gives a player a view of their own: the same maps, drawn differently for them alone.

events.name: click
events.doc: A player clicked the screen: `event.x` and `event.y` are the pixel they aimed at. A click on one of its frames always counts; from further than the game's reach, a swing of the arm aimed at the screen does, up to its click range. Only players it's drawn for can click it. The game's own use of the click (breaking, turning the map) never happens.
events.example:
this:on("click", function(event)
  if event.x < 64 then
    event.player:send_message("Left half!")
  end
end)

events.name: hover
events.doc: The pixel a player is aiming at moved: heard each tick their aim lands on another pixel, within the screen's click range. Costs nothing while nobody listens.

events.name: leave
events.doc: A player who was aiming at the screen (a `hover` was heard for them) looks away from it, goes out of range or leaves.

functions.name: name
functions.doc: The project's screen it is (its folder name under `screens/`), or the `key` a script made it with; `nil` for a script's screen made without one.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether it's still there.

functions.name: width
functions.doc: How wide it is, in pixels: 128 a map.

functions.name: height
functions.doc: How tall it is, in pixels: 128 a map.

functions.name: clear
functions.doc: Fills the whole screen with one colour. Nothing happens once the screen is gone.

params.name: color
params.doc: A colour, `#rrggbb` (drawn as the nearest of the colours a map can show), or `"clear"` for none: the map shows through. Default `"clear"`.

functions.name: pixel
functions.doc: One pixel's colour, as the map draws it: `#rrggbb`, or `"clear"`. `nil` for a pixel off the screen, or once the screen is gone.

params.name: x
params.doc: From the left edge, 0 first.

params.name: y
params.doc: From the top edge, 0 first.

functions.name: set_pixel
functions.doc: Sets one pixel. One off the screen is left alone. Nothing happens once the screen is gone.

params.name: x
params.doc: From the left edge, 0 first.

params.name: y
params.doc: From the top edge, 0 first.

params.name: color
params.doc: A colour, `#rrggbb` (drawn as the nearest of the colours a map can show), or `"clear"` for none: the map shows through. `nil` is `"clear"`.

functions.name: pixels
functions.doc: A block of pixels' colours, row by row (`#rrggbb`, or `"clear"`): what `set_pixels` takes. Pixels off the screen are `"clear"`; an empty list once the screen is gone. A block of more than 65536 pixels is an error.

params.name: x
params.doc: The block's left, in pixels from the screen's left edge.

params.name: y
params.doc: The block's top, in pixels from the screen's top edge.

params.name: width
params.doc: In pixels.

params.name: height
params.doc: In pixels.

functions.name: set_pixels
functions.doc: Sets a block of pixels from a list of colours, row by row, `width` to a row: the quick way to draw many pixels at once. What's off the screen is left alone. Nothing happens once the screen is gone.

params.name: x
