params.doc: The block's left, in pixels from the screen's left edge.

params.name: y
params.doc: The block's top, in pixels from the screen's top edge.

params.name: width
params.doc: Pixels in a row of `colors`.

params.name: colors
params.doc: Each pixel's colour. A colour, `#rrggbb` (drawn as the nearest of the colours a map can show), or `"clear"` for none: the map shows through.

functions.name: fill
functions.doc: Fills a rectangle with one colour. Nothing happens once the screen is gone.

params.name: x
params.doc: The rectangle's left, in pixels from the screen's left edge.

params.name: y
params.doc: The rectangle's top, in pixels from the screen's top edge.

params.name: width
params.doc: In pixels.

params.name: height
params.doc: In pixels.

params.name: color
params.doc: A colour, `#rrggbb` (drawn as the nearest of the colours a map can show), or `"clear"` for none: the map shows through.

functions.name: rectangle
functions.doc: Draws a rectangle: filled, outlined, or both, with rounded corners if `style.radius` says. Nothing happens once the screen is gone.

params.name: x
params.doc: The rectangle's left, in pixels from the screen's left edge.

params.name: y
params.doc: The rectangle's top, in pixels from the screen's top edge.

params.name: width
params.doc: In pixels.

params.name: height
params.doc: In pixels.

params.name: style
params.doc: Its fill and outline.

functions.example: this:rectangle(8, 8, 112, 40, { fill = "#202040", outline = "#ffcc00", thickness = 2, radius = 6 })

functions.name: line
functions.doc: Draws a straight line between two pixels, both included. Nothing happens once the screen is gone.

params.name: x1
params.doc: Where it starts.

params.name: x2
params.doc: Where it ends.

params.name: color
params.doc: A colour, `#rrggbb` (drawn as the nearest of the colours a map can show), or `"clear"` for none: the map shows through.

params.name: thickness
params.doc: In pixels, 1 to 32 (default 1).

functions.name: circle
functions.doc: Draws a circle round a pixel: filled, outlined, or both. Nothing happens once the screen is gone.

params.name: x
params.doc: Its middle, from the left edge.

params.name: y
params.doc: Its middle, from the top edge.

params.name: radius
params.doc: In pixels, 0 or more.

params.name: style
params.doc: Its fill and outline (`radius` is not used).

functions.name: ellipse
functions.doc: Draws an ellipse round a pixel. Nothing happens once the screen is gone.

params.name: x
params.doc: Its middle, from the left edge.

params.name: y
params.doc: Its middle, from the top edge.

params.name: radius_x
params.doc: Across, in pixels.

params.name: radius_y
params.doc: Down, in pixels.

params.name: style
params.doc: Its fill and outline (`radius` is not used).

functions.name: polygon
functions.doc: Draws a closed shape through points, `{ x1, y1, x2, y2, … }` (at least three points). Fewer than three, or an odd count of numbers, is an error. Nothing happens once the screen is gone.

params.name: points
params.doc: The corners, each an x then a y.

params.name: style
params.doc: Its fill and outline (`radius` is not used).

functions.name: text
functions.doc: Writes text with its top left at a pixel. Lines break at `\n`, and at spaces past `options.width` when it's given. MiniMessage colours, `<b>`, `<u>` and `<st>` are drawn; glyphs and other tags aren't. An unknown font is an error. Returns how big it was, as `nf.screens.measure_text` would say (`0` by `0` once the screen is gone).

params.name: x
params.doc: The text's left, in pixels from the screen's left edge.

params.name: y
params.doc: The text's top, in pixels from the screen's top edge.

params.name: text
params.doc: What to write.

params.name: options
params.doc: Font, colour, size, alignment.

functions.example: this:text(64, 4, "<gold>Lobby</gold>\n<gray>3 players", { align = "center", scale = 2 })

functions.name: image
functions.doc: Draws a picture: a texture of a resource pack, as `<pack>/<path>` (`ui/logo` is `resource_packs/ui/textures/logo.png`). Its colours become map colours as `options.dither` says; pixels less than half opaque draw nothing. A picture the project doesn't have is an error. Returns `false` when the picture can't be read. Nothing happens once the screen is gone.

params.name: x
params.doc: The picture's left, in pixels from the screen's left edge.

params.name: y
params.doc: The picture's top, in pixels from the screen's top edge.

params.name: image
params.doc: The texture, `<pack>/<path>` without `.png`.

params.name: options
params.doc: Its size and dithering.

functions.example: this:image(0, 0, "ui/logo", { width = 256, height = 128 })

functions.name: copy
functions.doc: Copies a rectangle of the screen to another place on it (overlapping is fine): a quick way to scroll. What's off the screen is left alone. Nothing happens once the screen is gone.

params.name: x
params.doc: The rectangle copied's left, in pixels from the screen's left edge.

params.name: y
params.doc: The rectangle copied's top, in pixels from the screen's top edge.

params.name: width
params.doc: In pixels.

params.name: height
params.doc: In pixels.

params.name: to_x
params.doc: Where its left goes.

params.name: to_y
params.doc: Where its top goes.

functions.example:
-- Scroll everything up by 10 pixels.
this:copy(0, 10, this:width(), this:height() - 10, 0, 0)

functions.name: place
functions.doc: Hangs it on a wall: an invisible, fixed item frame a map, its top left map at `location`'s block (the air in front of the wall) and the rest going right and down as a player facing it sees them. The frames need no wall behind them. A screen already hanging somewhere is moved. A project screen hangs where its file says again when the server restarts. Returns `false` when the world isn't loaded.

params.name: location
params.doc: Where its top left map goes.

params.name: facing
params.doc: The way it faces: out of the wall, towards whoever looks at it.

functions.example: this:place(nf.worlds.default():location(vec3(0, 72, 0)), "south")

functions.name: take_down
functions.doc: Takes its frames down. It can still be drawn on, and its map items still show it.

returns.doc: `false` when it hung nowhere.

functions.name: location
functions.doc: Where its top left map hangs; `nil` when it hangs nowhere.

functions.name: facing
functions.doc: Which way it faces where it hangs; `nil` when it hangs nowhere.

functions.name: item
functions.doc: A map item showing one of its maps, to give a player or put in a frame: `column` and `row` count from 0 at its top left. A map off the screen is an error. A screen made without a `key` gets new map numbers each time it's made, so its items show nothing after a restart.

params.name: column
params.doc: Which map across, 0 first (default 0).

params.name: row
params.doc: Which map down, 0 first (default 0).

functions.example: player:give_item(this:item())

functions.name: show_to
functions.doc: Draws it for a player, whoever it's drawn for otherwise (a `viewers = "script"` screen is drawn only for those it's shown to). Lasts until `hide_from`, or the screen goes.

params.name: player
params.doc: Who.

returns.doc: `false` when they are offline or the screen is gone.

functions.name: hide_from
functions.doc: Stops drawing it for a player (they see blank maps, and can't click it), until `show_to`.

params.name: player
params.doc: Who.

returns.doc: `false` when they are offline or the screen is gone.

functions.name: is_shown_to
functions.doc: Whether it is drawn for a player now: shown to them, or near them on a `"near"` screen, and not hidden from them.

params.name: player
params.doc: Who.

functions.name: viewers
functions.doc: Everyone it is drawn for now.

functions.name: for_player
functions.doc: A player's own view of the screen: drawing on it changes what they see alone (the same maps, the same frames), starting from what everyone sees now. It lasts until `release`, they leave, or the screen goes; drawing on the shared screen meanwhile doesn't reach them. Called on a player's own view, it's that view.

params.name: player
params.doc: Whose view.

functions.example:
nf.on("player_join", function(event)
  local mine = this:for_player(event.player)
  mine:text(4, 4, "Hello, " .. event.player:name())
end)

functions.name: player
functions.doc: Whose own view this is; `nil` for the screen everyone sees.

functions.name: release
functions.doc: Ends a player's own view (see `for_player`): they see what everyone sees again.

returns.doc: `false` when this isn't a player's own view, or it has ended.

functions.name: play
functions.doc: Plays a video (`videos/<id>/`) on the screen, from its top left (`options.x`, `options.y` move it), replacing any video playing on it (that one ends, reason `"replaced"`). Its sound plays to the players it's drawn for who are near where it hangs. It belongs to the script that played it: when that script unloads, it ends. A video the project doesn't have is an error; one not yet converted in the editor gives `nil`.

params.name: video
params.doc: Its folder name under `videos/`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How it plays.

returns.doc: `nil` when it can't be played, or the screen is gone.

functions.example:
local show = this:play("trailer", { loop = true })
if show then
  show:on("end", function(event)
    log("trailer ended:", event.reason)
  end)
end

functions.name: playback
functions.doc: The video playing on it now; `nil` when none is.

functions.name: remove
functions.doc: Takes a script's screen away for good: its frames come down, and its video ends. A screen made with a `key` gives up its maps' numbers too: one made again with that key gets new ones, and an item or frame of the old ones shows nothing. A project screen can't be removed (its file says it's there): that's an error.

returns.doc: `false` when it was already gone.

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `screen:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: Playback
classes.doc: A video playing on a screen, from `screen:play`. Once it has ended its methods answer `nil` or `false`, except `video()` and `length()`; `exists()` says whether it has.

events.name: end
events.doc: The video ended, for any reason (`event.reason` says which). After it, the playback is gone and so is every handler on it; the screen keeps showing its last frame.

events.name: frame
events.doc: A frame of the video was drawn: as often as the video's rate while it plays. Costs nothing while nobody listens.
events.example:
local show = this:play("trailer")
if show then
  show:on("frame", function(event)
    if event.frame == 40 then
      this:text(4, 4, "<yellow>Here it comes!")
    end
  end)
end

functions.name: video
functions.doc: Which video it is: its folder name under `videos/`, even after it has ended.

functions.name: screen
functions.doc: The screen it plays on; `nil` once it has ended.

functions.name: length
functions.doc: How long the video lasts, in seconds, even after it has ended.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether it hasn't ended: paused counts.

functions.name: is_paused
functions.doc: Whether it is paused.

functions.name: pause
functions.doc: Holds it on the frame it shows, its sound stopped.

returns.doc: `false` when it was paused already, or has ended.

functions.name: resume
functions.doc: Plays it on from where it was paused, its sound from there too.

returns.doc: `false` when it wasn't paused, or has ended.

functions.name: stop
functions.doc: Ends it now, with reason `"stopped"`. The screen keeps its last frame.

returns.doc: `false` when it had already ended.

functions.name: time
functions.doc: Where it is, in seconds from the video's start; `nil` once it has ended.

functions.name: seek
functions.doc: Jumps to a time in the video, in seconds (held to 0 and its length); its sound starts again from there.

params.name: seconds
params.doc: Where to.

returns.doc: `false` when it has ended.

functions.name: speed
functions.doc: How fast it plays: 1 is as recorded. `nil` once it has ended.

functions.name: set_speed
functions.doc: Plays it faster or slower, 0.25 to 4 (held to that). Its sound plays only at speed 1.

params.name: speed
params.doc: The new speed; `nil` is 1.

returns.doc: `false` when it has ended.

functions.name: volume
functions.doc: Its sound's volume, 0 to 1; `nil` once it has ended.

functions.name: set_volume
functions.doc: Changes its sound's volume, 0 to 1 (held to that); its sound starts again at the new volume.

params.name: volume
params.doc: The new volume; `nil` is 1.

returns.doc: `false` when it has ended.

functions.name: is_looping
functions.doc: Whether it starts again when it reaches its end.

functions.name: set_looping
functions.doc: Whether it starts again when it reaches its end.

params.name: looping
params.doc: Loop or not.

returns.doc: `false` when it has ended.

functions.name: on
functions.doc: Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`.

params.name: options
params.doc: How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

functions.example:
local show = this:play("trailer")
if show then
  show:on("end", function(event)
    log("trailer ended:", event.reason)
  end)
end

functions.name: once
functions.doc: Like `playback:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

params.name: event
params.doc: The event's name.

params.name: handler
params.doc: Called with the event.

returns.doc: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.

classes.name: File
classes.doc: A path in the scripts' data directory (`plugins/NetherForge/data/`, on the editor's dev server too). The only state a script has that survives a restart. Files are capped at 1 MiB; writes past it are refused, not truncated.

functions.name: path
functions.doc: The path from the data directory; `""` for the directory itself.

functions.name: name
functions.doc: The last part of the path.

functions.name: parent
functions.doc: The folder it's in, or `nil` for the data directory itself.

functions.name: child
functions.doc: Something inside this folder, whether or not it exists yet. `nil` for a name that isn't allowed.

params.name: name
params.doc: One name, no `/`.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc: Whether anything is there.

functions.name: is_folder
functions.doc: Whether it's a folder.

functions.name: size
functions.doc: Its size in bytes, or `nil` when it isn't a file.

functions.name: children
functions.doc: What's directly inside, sorted by name; empty for a file or nothing.

functions.name: read
functions.doc: The contents, or `nil` when there's no file.

functions.name: write
functions.doc: Replaces the contents, creating folders above it as needed.

returns.doc: `false` for a folder, past the size cap, or on a disk error.

functions.name: append
functions.doc: Adds to the end.

functions.name: read_json
functions.doc: The contents parsed as JSON, as `nf.json.decode` does, or `nil` when there's no file or it isn't JSON.

functions.name: write_json
functions.doc: Writes a value as JSON, as `nf.json.encode` does.

returns.doc: `false` for something JSON can't hold (a function, a table inside itself) or a failed write.

functions.name: modified_time
functions.doc: When it last changed, as Unix time in milliseconds (like `nf.server.unix_time()`), or `nil` when there's nothing there.

functions.name: lines
functions.doc: An iterator over its lines, for a `for` loop: each without its line ending (`\n` or `\r\n`). Nothing for a file that isn't there.
functions.example:
for line in nf.files.get("motd.txt"):lines() do
  player:send_message(line)
end

functions.name: rename
functions.doc: Moves it (a file, or a folder and everything in it) to another path in the data directory, creating folders above it as needed. Nothing already there is overwritten.

params.name: path
params.doc: From the data directory, as `nf.files.get` takes it.

returns.doc: It at its new path; `nil` when there's nothing to move, the path isn't allowed or is taken, or the move failed.

functions.example: assert(nf.files.get("scores.json")):rename("backups/scores-1.json")

functions.name: copy_to
functions.doc: Copies a file to another path in the data directory, creating folders above it as needed. Nothing already there is overwritten. Folders can't be copied.

params.name: path
params.doc: From the data directory, as `nf.files.get` takes it.

returns.doc: The copy; `nil` when it isn't a file, the path isn't allowed or is taken, or the copy failed.

functions.name: create_folder
functions.doc: Creates the folder, and any above it.

functions.name: delete
functions.doc: Deletes a file or an empty folder.

classes.name: Subscription
classes.doc: What `:on` and `:once` return: one handler listening for one event on one handle (or on `nf`). A handler lives as long as **both** the script that registered it and the handle it's on: a module's handler on a centity's node goes when the module unloads or the centity is removed, whichever comes first; one on a menu window goes with the window. A handler that errors 20 times in a row is cancelled.

functions.name: cancel
functions.doc: Stops the handler being called. Cancelling one already cancelled does nothing.

functions.name: is_active
functions.doc: Whether the handler is still listening: `false` once it's cancelled (by `cancel()`, after a `once` handler ran, or after 20 errors in a row), its script has unloaded, or the handle it's on has gone.

classes.name: Task
classes.doc: What `nf.task`, `nf.after` and `nf.every` return: a task that may be waiting, or a callback waiting to run.

functions.name: cancel
functions.doc: Ends it: a task stops where it's waiting and never carries on; a callback doesn't run (again). A task that cancels itself stops at its next wait. Cancelling one that has ended does nothing.

functions.name: is_active
functions.doc: Whether it will still run: `false` once it's cancelled, once a task has finished, errored or lost the handle it was waiting on, once an `nf.after` callback has run, after an `nf.every` callback's 20th error in a row, or once its script has unloaded.

classes.name: Schedule
classes.doc: What `nf.schedule.daily`, `weekly` and `cron` return: a schedule that will run at its next time, until it is cancelled or its script unloads.

functions.name: cancel
functions.doc: Ends it: it doesn't run again. What it last ran is kept, so a schedule made again with the same `id` doesn't catch up a run it already made. Cancelling one that has ended does nothing.

functions.name: is_active
functions.doc: Whether it will still run: `false` once it's cancelled or its script has unloaded.

functions.name: next_run
functions.doc: When it runs next, as Unix time in milliseconds (like `nf.server.unix_time()`; `nf.time.format` writes it as a date). `nil` once it has ended.

classes.name: Random
classes.doc: A random generator from `nf.random.new`: numbers that repeat for its seed, apart from `math.random` and every other generator.

functions.name: integer
functions.doc: A whole number from `min` to `max`, both included, each as likely as the others. `min` greater than `max` is an error.

functions.name: number
functions.doc: A number from 0 up to (not including) 1, or from `min` up to `max`.

params.name: min
params.doc: Give both or neither.

functions.name: pick
functions.doc: One item of a list, each as likely as the others. `nil` for an empty list.

params.name: list
params.doc: A list, numbered from 1.

functions.example: local greeting = rng:pick({ "Hello", "Welcome back", "Hi there" })

functions.name: shuffle
functions.doc: Puts a list in a random order, in place.

params.name: list
params.doc: A list, numbered from 1.

functions.name: weighted
functions.doc: One key of a table, picked with odds in proportion to its number: in `{ common = 3, rare = 1 }`, `"common"` comes up three times in four. Keys with weight 0 never come up; `nil` when there are none with more. A weight that is negative or not a number is an error. The same seed picks the same keys when the keys are strings, numbers or booleans.

params.name: weights
params.doc: Each choice, with its weight.

functions.example: local kind = rng:weighted({ ["minecraft:diamond"] = 1, ["minecraft:iron_ingot"] = 9 })

classes.name: Hud
classes.doc: One player's HUD: the elements of the project's resource packs (`hud` in `pack.json`: bars, rows of icons, lines of text, each at its place on the screen), shown with what a script sets here. An element nobody set isn't drawn. It's drawn in their action bar, sent again whenever something changes and every second, so `player:send_actionbar` shows its line alongside it while the HUD is up (on its own for a moment, when the server can't measure it). What it shows is the server's to remember, not saved: set it again when they join. A name that isn't one of the packs' elements, or is another kind of element, is an error.

functions.name: player
functions.doc: Whose HUD it is.

functions.name: fill_bar
functions.doc: Fills a bar: `value` out of `max`, shown as that much of its segments (to the nearest half segment, for a bar with a half picture). A `value` past `max` or below 0 is shown full or empty; a `max` of 0 or less is an error. With `segments`, only that many of the bar's segments are drawn (1 to the bar's own), placed by the bar's `align`.

params.name: name
params.doc: The bar, as `<pack>/<key>`: a key of a resource pack's `hud.bars` (a package's as `ns:<pack>/<key>`).

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.example:
local hud = player:hud()
hud:fill_bar("ui/health", player:health() or 0, player:max_health() or 20)
hud:fill_bar("ui/mana", 40, 100)

functions.name: fill_bars
functions.doc: Fills several bars as one long bar, each `per_segment` of `max` a segment: as many segments are drawn as `max` needs, filling the first bar's, then the next's (rows of hearts, ten to a row). A bar no segment reaches is removed. Every name must be a bar; `per_segment` and `max` more than 0.

params.name: names
params.doc: Bars, `<pack>/<key>`, in the order they fill.

params.name: per_segment
params.doc: How much of `max` a segment stands for.

returns.doc: How many segments were drawn in all; 0 when they're offline.

functions.example:
-- 20 life a heart, ten hearts a row, up to three rows.
local hud = player:hud()
hud:fill_bars({ "ui/life1", "ui/life2", "ui/life3" }, 230, 400, 20)

functions.name: bar
functions.doc: What a bar shows, or `nil` when nothing set it (or they're offline).

params.name: name
params.doc: The bar, as `<pack>/<key>`: a key of a resource pack's `hud.bars` (a package's as `ns:<pack>/<key>`).

functions.name: set_icons
functions.doc: Shows these of a row's icons, in this order: status effects, buffs, keys held. An empty list shows none. An icon the row doesn't have is an error.

params.name: name
params.doc: The row of icons, as `<pack>/<key>`: a key of a resource pack's `hud.icons` (a package's as `ns:<pack>/<key>`).

params.name: icons
params.doc: Keys of the row's `icons`.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.example: player:hud():set_icons("ui/effects", { "poison", "regeneration" })

functions.name: icons
functions.doc: The icons a row shows, in order, or `nil` when nothing set it (or they're offline).

params.name: name
params.doc: The row of icons, as `<pack>/<key>`: a key of a resource pack's `hud.icons` (a package's as `ns:<pack>/<key>`).

functions.name: set_text
functions.doc: Sets a line of text, on the action bar's own line where the line's `x` and `align` put it. The server measures it with the game's font (`fonts/default.json`) to put it there; one it can't measure isn't drawn.

params.name: name
params.doc: The line of text, as `<pack>/<key>`: a key of a resource pack's `hud.texts` (a package's as `ns:<pack>/<key>`).

params.name: text
params.doc: MiniMessage; glyphs are fine.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline.

functions.example:
local mana = 40
player:hud():set_text("ui/mana_label", "<aqua>" .. mana .. "/100")

functions.name: text
functions.doc: A line's text, or `nil` when nothing set it (or they're offline).

params.name: name
params.doc: The line of text, as `<pack>/<key>`: a key of a resource pack's `hud.texts` (a package's as `ns:<pack>/<key>`).

functions.name: remove
functions.doc: Stops drawing one element (any kind), until something sets it again.

params.name: name
params.doc: A HUD element, `<pack>/<key>`.

returns.doc: `false` when they're offline, or nothing was drawn for it.

functions.name: clear
functions.doc: Stops drawing every element: their action bar is the game's again.

values.name: Vec3
values.doc: Three numbers: a position, an offset, a velocity, a direction or a scale. Every place the API takes or gives one of those, it's a `Vec3`. Build one with `vec3(x, y, z)`. Vectors are immutable: methods and operators return a new vector, and assigning to `v.x` is an error. `a == b` compares the numbers exactly, and `tostring(v)` is `"vec3(1, 2, 3)"`.

fields.name: x
fields.doc: East (+) and west (−).

fields.name: y
fields.doc: Up (+) and down (−).

fields.name: z
fields.doc: South (+) and north (−).

operators.doc: `a * b`: component by component, for scales.

functions.name: length
functions.doc: How long it is.

functions.name: length_squared
functions.doc: Its length squared: cheaper than `length()`, and enough for comparing distances.

functions.name: normalized
functions.doc: The same direction with length 1. The zero vector stays zero rather than becoming NaN.

functions.name: dot
functions.doc: The dot product.

functions.name: cross
functions.doc: The cross product: a vector at right angles to both, by the right-hand rule.

functions.name: distance
functions.doc: How far it is to another point.

functions.name: distance_squared
functions.doc: The distance squared: cheaper than `distance()`, and enough for comparing.

functions.name: lerp
functions.doc: The point `fraction` of the way to `other`: 0 is this vector, 1 is `other`.

params.name: fraction
params.doc: Usually 0 to 1; outside that it carries on past either end.

functions.name: clamp_length
functions.doc: The same direction, scaled down to at most `max_length` long: a copy if it is no longer than that already. Keeps a velocity under a top speed.

params.name: max_length
params.doc: The longest it may be, 0 or more.

functions.example: local velocity = vec3(3, 0, 4):clamp_length(2.5)

functions.name: reflect
functions.doc: Mirrored off a surface: `v - 2 * v:dot(n) * n` for the surface's unit normal `n`, so the part into the surface turns back out and the part along it carries on. How a shot bounces off a wall, with a sweep's `normal`.

params.name: normal
params.doc: Which way the surface faces. Any length but zero: it is normalized first.

functions.example: local bounced = vec3(1, -2, 0):reflect(vec3.up)

functions.name: closest_on_segment
functions.doc: The point on the line segment from `start` to `finish` nearest to this point: its foot on the segment, or the nearer end when that falls past one. `start` when the two are the same point. With `distance`, how far a point is from a beam or a path.

params.name: start
params.doc: One end.

params.name: finish
params.doc: The other end.

functions.example: local nearest = player:position():closest_on_segment(vec3(0, 64, 0), vec3(10, 64, 0))

functions.name: flat
functions.doc: A copy with `y` set to 0: the horizontal part.
functions.example: local toward = (target - player:position()):flat():normalized()

functions.name: with_x
functions.doc: A copy with `x` replaced.

functions.name: with_y
functions.doc: A copy with `y` replaced.

functions.name: with_z
functions.doc: A copy with `z` replaced.

functions.name: floor
functions.doc: Each component rounded down: the block a position is in.

functions.name: round
functions.doc: Each component rounded to the nearest whole number, halves up.

functions.name: rotated
functions.doc: Turned about an axis through the origin, by the right-hand rule: with your right thumb along the axis, positive degrees turn the way your fingers curl. About `vec3.up`, 90 degrees turns east into north.

params.name: axis
params.doc: Any length but zero.

functions.example: local left = forward:rotated(vec3.up, 90)

functions.name: unpack
functions.doc: The three numbers, for code that wants them separately.

returns.doc: x
y
z

functions.example: local x, y, z = v:unpack()

library.name: vec3
library.doc: Builds vectors (`vec3(x, y, z)`), and holds the common ones and `vec3.from_yaw_pitch`.

functions.name: from_yaw_pitch
functions.doc: The unit direction a yaw and pitch face, in Minecraft's convention: yaw 0 faces south (+z), 90 west (−x), 180 north, −90 east; pitch −90 is straight up, 90 straight down.

params.name: yaw
params.doc: Degrees.

params.name: pitch
params.doc: Degrees.

functions.example: local ahead = vec3.from_yaw_pitch(player:yaw() or 0, 0) * 2

values.name: Location
values.doc: A position in a particular world, with an optional facing. Immutable, like `Vec3`. What `location()` returns on a player or a centity; build one with `world:location(position, yaw?, pitch?)`. Methods that place things (`teleport`, `nf.centities.spawn`) take a `Location`, or a bare `Vec3` meaning "in the same world". `a == b` when every field is equal.

fields.name: world
fields.doc: Which world.

fields.name: position
fields.doc: Where in the world.

fields.name: yaw
fields.doc: Which way it faces horizontally, in degrees (0 south, 90 west), or `nil` for a location with no facing.

fields.name: pitch
fields.doc: How far up or down it faces, in degrees (−90 up, 90 down), or `nil` for a location with no facing.

functions.name: with_position
functions.doc: A copy somewhere else in the same world, keeping the facing.

functions.name: offset
functions.doc: A copy moved by an offset, keeping the facing.
functions.example: player:teleport(player:location():offset(vec3(0, 10, 0)))

functions.name: direction
functions.doc: The unit direction it faces (`vec3.from_yaw_pitch`, a missing pitch counting as level), or `nil` when it has no facing.

aliases.name: Text
aliases.doc: MiniMessage a player reads, like `"<green>Done!"`: a string. A `<glyph:pack/key>` tag in it names a glyph the way the script's own files would: one of its own package's resource packs bare, or `<glyph:namespace:pack/key>` for one a package it depends on exports. The tag means that glyph wherever and whenever the text is shown, whoever shows it; one naming a glyph the script can't use draws nothing, and the server log says why. Text handed back to a script names its glyphs the same way.

surfaces.name: centity
surfaces.doc: A centity's script (`centities/<id>/*.lua`, named by `script` in `centity.json`). One copy runs per spawned instance, with its own globals; `this` is the instance. The script's body runs every time it starts (spawning, a restart, a reload): that's where it sets up its nodes and registers its handlers, with `this:on(...)` and `this:node(name):on(...)`.

globals.name: this
globals.doc: The centity instance this script runs on.

surfaces.name: module
surfaces.doc: A module's files (`modules/<id>/**/*.lua`). `init.lua` runs when the server loads the module; other files run when something requires them. All of a module's files share one set of globals. Modules listen with `nf.on` (and `:on` on any handle they hold) and add commands with `nf.commands.register`.

surfaces.name: menu
surfaces.doc: A menu's script (`menus/<id>/*.lua`, named by `script` in `menu.json`). Every window gets its own copy, with its own globals, started when the window is made: when it's opened for someone, or at load for a `shared` one. The body runs before anyone sees the window, so it's where to fill it in and register handlers (`this:on("click", ...)`, `this:slot(13):on("click", ...)`). Its handlers go with the window.

globals.name: this
globals.doc: The window this script runs for.

surfaces.name: dialog
surfaces.doc: A dialog's script (`dialogs/<id>/*.lua`, named by `script` in `dialog.json`). There's one of each dialog, so its script runs once, from load until the dialog is reloaded. Its body registers handlers: `this:on("press", ...)`, `this:button(key):on("press", ...)`, `this:on("close", ...)`.

globals.name: this
globals.doc: The dialog this script belongs to.

surfaces.name: item
surfaces.doc: A project item's script (`items/<id>/*.lua`, named by `script` in `item.json`). There's one of each item, so its script runs once (not once per stack), from load until the item is reloaded. Its body registers handlers for what players do with any stack of the item: `this:on("use", ...)`, `this:on("hit", ...)`, `this:on("pickup", ...)`.

globals.name: this
globals.doc: The project item this script belongs to.

surfaces.name: block
surfaces.doc: A project block's script (`blocks/<id>/*.lua`, named by `script` in `block.json`). There's one of each block, so its script runs once (not once per placed block), from load until the block is reloaded. Its body registers handlers for what players do with any block of it: `this:on("click", ...)`, `this:on("break", ...)`, `this:on("tick", ...)`.

globals.name: this
globals.doc: The project block this script belongs to.

surfaces.name: screen
surfaces.doc: A screen's script (`screens/<id>/*.lua`, named by `script` in `screen.json`). There's one of each screen, so its script runs once, from load until the screen is reloaded. Its body draws the screen (what a screen shows isn't saved, so this is where it's drawn after every restart) and registers handlers: `this:on("click", ...)`, `this:on("hover", ...)`.

globals.name: this
globals.doc: The screen this script belongs to.

shapes.name: Event
shapes.doc: What every event handler receives: a table with the event's own fields (its payload, named `<Something>Event` in this reference) and these. What a handler returns means nothing; it changes what happens through `stop`, `cancel` and the event's writable fields. A field the event doesn't list as writable can't be assigned.

functions.name: stop
functions.doc: No later handler hears it: none further along its path (a parent node, the centity, `nf`), and none after this one on the same handle.

functions.name: cancel
functions.doc: Cancels what caused it: the click doesn't move an item, the block isn't broken. Only for cancellable events; on any other, it's an error. A later handler can still `uncancel()`.

functions.name: uncancel
functions.doc: Undoes an earlier handler's `cancel()`, or a locked menu's.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The event's name where the handler is listening: `"click"` on a node, `"centity_click"` on `nf`.

fields.name: current
fields.doc: The handle whose handler is running (the node, centity, slot, menu, button or dialog), or `nil` in an `nf.on` handler. As an event bubbles it changes; `target` stays what was hit.

fields.name: cancelled
fields.doc: Whether what caused it will be cancelled, as things stand. Read-only: use `cancel()` and `uncancel()`.

fields.name: stopped
fields.doc: Whether a handler called `stop()`. Read-only.

shapes.name: EventOptions
shapes.doc: How `:on` listens. Every key is optional, and each applies only to the events that say so: a key that isn't one of these, or one the event doesn't take, is an error.

fields.name: every
fields.doc: For `tick`: run every this many ticks instead of every tick (at least 1). `every = 20` is once a second. Which of those ticks is fixed by the server's tick count and the thing it's on (a centity's handlers all agree, and different centities fall on different ticks; each `nf.on` handler has its own), not by when the handler was added, so the first call can come sooner than `every` ticks.

shapes.name: SettingChangedEvent
shapes.doc: One of the package's settings changed.

fields.name: setting
fields.doc: The setting's name, as `netherforge.json` declares it.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: What it is now, as `nf.config` gives it.

fields.name: previous
fields.doc: What it was.

shapes.name: DaylightEvent
shapes.doc: Night is falling or day is breaking in a world.

fields.name: world
fields.doc: The world.

fields.name: time_of_day
fields.doc: The world's time of day when it was seen, in ticks, as `world:time_of_day()` says: 13000 or a little past at dusk, 23000 or a little past at dawn, or wherever `/time set` put it.

shapes.name: TickEvent
shapes.doc: A server tick went by.

fields.name: tick
fields.doc: The server tick it is, the same as `nf.server.tick()`.

shapes.name: ClickEvent
shapes.doc: A player clicked a centity's hitbox. Heard by the clicked node, then each node above it, then the centity, then `nf.on("centity_click")`.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: target
fields.doc: The node whose hitbox was clicked. `event.current` is the node or centity whose handler is running.

fields.name: click
fields.doc: Which kind of click: the left (attack) or right (use) button.

fields.name: hit_position
fields.doc: Where the player's line of sight met the hitbox, as a world position: what `node:apply_impulse_at` takes. `nil` when the server couldn't tell.

fields.name: hit_normal
fields.doc: The unit direction straight out of the face that was hit, in world space. `nil` when the server couldn't tell.

shapes.name: CentityEvent
shapes.doc: Something happened to a centity instance as a whole.

fields.name: centity
fields.doc: The instance.

shapes.name: CentityNaturalSpawnEvent
shapes.doc: A centity is about to appear by itself, from its `spawning` rules, near a player.

fields.name: centity
fields.doc: Which centity, as the project names it: its folder name under `centities/` (`wisp`), or `acme:wisp` for one a package brings.

fields.name: location
fields.doc: Where it will stand, facing included (its yaw is the way the centity turns). Writable: assign another `Location` to put it somewhere else, in any world the server has; the spawner does not check its rules again there.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: The player it is appearing near.

shapes.name: AnimationEvent
shapes.doc: One of a centity's animations started or ended.

fields.name: centity
fields.doc: The instance.

fields.name: animation
fields.doc: The animation's name.

shapes.name: NodeEvent
shapes.doc: Something happened to a node's physics body.

fields.name: node
fields.doc: The node.

shapes.name: CollideEvent
shapes.doc: A physics body started touching something it wasn't touching the tick before: the moment of impact, not every tick while it rests there.

fields.name: node
fields.doc: The body that hit something.

fields.name: other
fields.doc: The other body when it was one of the same centity's, or `nil` for a block or another centity's hitbox.

fields.name: hit_position
fields.doc: Where they touched, as a world position.

fields.name: hit_normal
fields.doc: The unit direction from what it hit towards the body, in world space.

fields.name: speed
fields.doc: How fast they were closing, in blocks per second: small for a touch, large for a crash. Handy for how loud a sound should be.

shapes.name: PlayerJoinEvent
shapes.doc: A player joined the server.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: first_join
fields.doc: Whether they have never played here before.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: The join message everyone sees, as MiniMessage. Writable: assign another, or `nil` for none.

shapes.name: PlayerQuitEvent
shapes.doc: A player left the server.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: The leave message everyone sees, as MiniMessage. Writable: assign another, or `nil` for none.

shapes.name: PlayerChatEvent
shapes.doc: A player is saying something in chat.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: What they said, as plain text: never MiniMessage, so it can be shown as it is. Writable: assign other text to change what everyone sees.

fields.name: format
fields.doc: How the line is shown, as MiniMessage, where `<player>` is the player's display name and `<message>` what they said (both shown as they are, never read as tags). Starts as Minecraft's own look, `"\\<<player>> <message>"`. Writable: assign another, like `"<gray><player>: <white><message>"`.

shapes.name: PlayerInteractEvent
shapes.doc: A player clicked a block or the air with one hand. The game asks for each hand in turn, so one right click can arrive twice: once for the main hand and, unless that did something, once for the off hand.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: click
fields.doc: Which kind of click: the left (attack) or right (use) button.

fields.name: block
fields.doc: The block, or `nil` for a click on the air.

fields.name: face
fields.doc: Which face of the block was clicked, or `nil` for a click on the air.

fields.name: item
fields.doc: What's in the hand the click was with, or `nil` for an empty hand.

fields.name: hand
fields.doc: Which hand: the game asks for each hand in turn.

shapes.name: BlockBreakEvent
shapes.doc: A player is breaking a block: heard by its world, then `nf.on("block_break")`.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: block
fields.doc: The block. A handle reads the world live, so what it says depends on when you ask: `state` is what it was when this happened.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: Its whole block state as it was being broken, like `"minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=bottom,shape=straight,waterlogged=false]"`.

fields.name: drops
fields.doc: What it will drop, for the tool they're breaking it with: an empty list for nothing. Writable: assign another list of items (or change this one) to drop those instead.

fields.name: experience
fields.doc: The experience it will drop (an ore's, say). Writable: assign another to change it.

shapes.name: BlockPlaceEvent
shapes.doc: A player is placing a block: heard by its world, then `nf.on("block_place")`.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: block
fields.doc: The block. A handle reads the world live, so what it says depends on when you ask: `state` is what it was when this happened.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: The whole block state being placed, like `"minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=bottom,shape=straight,waterlogged=false]"`.

fields.name: against
fields.doc: The block it was placed against: the one they clicked.

shapes.name: PlayerEvent
shapes.doc: Something a player did that needs no more said.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

shapes.name: PlayerSwapHandsEvent
shapes.doc: A player pressed the swap-hands key.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: item
fields.doc: What is going to their off hand: what is in their main hand, or in the slot they point at with an inventory screen open.

fields.name: off_hand_item
fields.doc: What is leaving their off hand.

fields.name: in_inventory
fields.doc: Whether they pressed it over a slot with an inventory screen open, rather than with their hands.

shapes.name: PlayerMoveEvent
shapes.doc: A player walked, swam, flew or fell into another block.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: from
fields.doc: Where they were, facing included: in the block they are leaving.

fields.name: to
fields.doc: Where they are going, facing included: in another block from `from`.

shapes.name: PlayerTeleportEvent
shapes.doc: A player is being teleported.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: from
fields.doc: Where they are, facing included.

fields.name: to
fields.doc: Where they are going, facing included. Writable: assign another `Location` to send them there instead (a world the server doesn't have leaves it as it was).

fields.name: cause
fields.doc: Why, as Minecraft names it: `"command"`, `"plugin"` (a plugin or a script), `"ender_pearl"`, `"chorus_fruit"`, `"nether_portal"`, `"end_portal"`, `"end_gateway"`, `"spectate"`, `"dismount"`, `"exit_bed"`, `"unknown"`, …

shapes.name: PlayerChangeWorldEvent
shapes.doc: A player went from one world to another.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: from
fields.doc: The world they left.

fields.name: to
fields.doc: The world they are in now.

shapes.name: PlayerDeathEvent
shapes.doc: A player died.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: killer
fields.doc: Who killed them, when someone did.

fields.name: cause
fields.doc: What killed them, as Minecraft names it, the same as `EntityDamageEvent`'s `cause`: `"entity_attack"`, `"fall"`, `"lava"`, `"void"`, …

fields.name: message
fields.doc: The death message everyone sees, as MiniMessage. Writable: assign another, or `nil` for none.

fields.name: keep_inventory
fields.doc: Whether they keep what they carry. Writable: `true` keeps their inventory, and then nothing from it drops (unless `drops` is assigned too).

fields.name: drops
fields.doc: What they drop where they died. Writable: assign another list of items (or change this one) to drop those instead.

shapes.name: PlayerRespawnEvent
shapes.doc: A player is coming back after dying (or leaving the end).

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: location
fields.doc: Where they will appear: their bed, respawn anchor or the world's spawn. Writable: assign another `Location` to bring them back there (a world the server doesn't have leaves it as it was).

shapes.name: PlayerItemEvent
shapes.doc: A player did something with an item stack.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: item
fields.doc: The item stack.

shapes.name: PlayerPickupItemEvent
shapes.doc: A player is picking up a dropped item.

shapes.name: CentityFilter
shapes.doc: Which centities `nf.centities.all` lists. Every key is optional; an instance is listed when it matches all of those given. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: Only instances of this centity: its folder name.

fields.name: world
fields.doc: Only instances in this world.

fields.name: near
fields.doc: Only instances whose position is within `radius` of this point (in any world, unless `world` says which). Needs `radius`.

fields.name: radius
fields.doc: How far from `near`, in blocks. Needs `near`.

fields.name: shooter

shapes.name: ProjectileHitEvent

fields.name: cause
fields.doc: Why, as Minecraft names it: `"closest_player"`, `"target_attacked_entity"`, `"target_attacked_nearby_entity"`, `"forgot_target"`, `"target_died"`, `"temptation"`, `"custom"` (a plugin or a script), …

shapes.name: ExplodeEvent
shapes.doc: Something exploded: an entity (`entity_explode`) or a block (`block_explode`).

fields.name: entity
fields.doc: What exploded, for `entity_explode`; `nil` for a block.

fields.name: block
fields.doc: Where the block that exploded was, for `block_explode` (it has gone already); `nil` for an entity.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: The whole block state of the block that exploded, for `block_explode`; `nil` for an entity.

fields.name: location
fields.doc: Where it exploded.

fields.name: blocks
fields.doc: The blocks it will break, as their handles: read them to see what would go.

fields.name: breaks_blocks
fields.doc: Whether `blocks` will break. Writable: `false` keeps every block standing, but the explosion still hurts and pushes what is near.

fields.name: yield
fields.doc: The chance each broken block drops as an item, 0 to 1. Writable: assign another (1 drops everything).

fields.name: source
fields.doc: The entity that set it alight (a flaming arrow, whoever swung a fire aspect sword), when one did.

fields.name: block
fields.doc: The block that set it alight (fire, lava), when one did.

fields.name: cause
fields.doc: Why, as Minecraft names it: `"potion_drink"`, `"potion_splash"`, `"beacon"`, `"milk"`, `"expiration"`, `"command"`, `"plugin"` (a plugin or a script), `"food"`, `"attack"`, …

fields.name: from

fields.name: to

shapes.name: PlayerClickInventoryEvent
shapes.doc: A player clicked in an inventory that isn't one of the project's menus.

fields.doc: Who it was.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: What kind of inventory they have open: `"crafting"` when it is only their own (opened with the inventory key), else as `PlayerInventoryEvent.kind` says (`"chest"`, `"furnace"`, …).

fields.name: inventory
fields.doc: The inventory clicked, when it's a real one: their own (`player:inventory()`), a container block's, an entity's, their ender chest. `nil` for a click outside both, and in one with nothing kept in it (the crafting grid, an anvil).

fields.name: own
fields.doc: Whether the click landed in their own inventory (hotbar, main slots, armour, off hand) rather than in the one above it or outside both.

fields.name: index
fields.doc: The slot clicked, from 0, in the inventory clicked. In their own: 0 to 8 the hotbar, 9 to 35 the rest, 36 to 39 armour (boots first), 40 the off hand, as `player:inventory()` numbers them. `nil` for a click outside both.

fields.name: click
fields.doc: What kind of click it was. `swap_offhand` is the swap-hands key (F) over a slot: what is in it and what is in the off hand change places.

fields.name: hotbar_index
fields.doc: For `number_key`: the hotbar slot, 0 to 8.

fields.name: item

fields.name: cursor_item

fields.name: inventory

fields.name: indices
fields.doc: The slots of the inventory above their own the stack is spread over, from 0, in order (the crafting grid's 1 to 4 when only their own is open, 0 being its result).

fields.name: own_indices
fields.doc: The slots of their own inventory the stack is spread over, in order, numbered as `player:inventory()` numbers them.

fields.name: click
fields.doc: `"left"` spreads the stack evenly over the slots, `"right"` puts one in each.

fields.name: cursor_item

shapes.name: CentityPathOptions
shapes.doc: How a centity walks where `centity:move_to` sends it. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: speed
fields.doc: How fast, in blocks a second: more than 0, at most 20. Default 4.3, a player's walk.

fields.name: fly
fields.doc: Flies there, through the air in any direction, rather than walking on the ground: no steps, drops or falling. Finding a way costs the server more. Default false.

fields.name: face
fields.doc: Turns it to face the way it goes, about its feet, a little each tick. Default true.

fields.name: width
fields.doc: How wide a gap it needs, in blocks: more than 0, at most 8. Default: its hitboxes' wider side, as they're placed when it sets off (1 without hitboxes). It's taken as square, whichever way it faces.

fields.name: height
fields.doc: How tall a gap it needs, in blocks: more than 0, at most 16. Default: its hitboxes' height (1 without hitboxes).

fields.name: step_height
fields.doc: Walking: how high a step it goes straight up, in blocks: at least 0. Default 1, a block, as a mob jumps one.

fields.name: max_drop
fields.doc: Walking: how far down it will drop off an edge, in blocks: at least 0. Default 3.

fields.name: open_doors
fields.doc: Walking: goes through the game's wooden doors and fence gates (`#minecraft:wooden_doors`, `#minecraft:fence_gates`), opening each as it comes to it and shutting it again once it's through (one it found open stays open). Iron doors stay in its way. Default `false`.

fields.name: range
fields.doc: How far from where it sets off it looks for a way, in blocks: more than 0, at most 128. A target further away than this is `false`. Default 48. One search looks at no more than 4096 places, so a long way round may only take it part of the way.

shapes.name: CentityPathEndEvent

fields.name: centity
