fields.name: handler
fields.doc: Runs when someone types it. A handler that errors is logged and whoever typed the command is told; the command stays.

shapes.name: CommandArgument
shapes.doc: One argument of a command. Its `type` decides what may be typed, what tab completion offers, the usage message, and the value the handler gets in `event.arguments[name]`. On Paper it's a real Brigadier argument, so the player's client checks and completes it as they type. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Its key in `event.arguments`, and what the usage message shows (`<amount>`). Letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit; unique within the command.

fields.name: type
fields.doc: What it takes, and what the handler gets: `"word"`: one word, a `string`. `"text"`: the rest of the line, spaces and all, a `string`. `"integer"`: a whole number, within `min` and `max` when given, a `integer`. `"number"`: any number, within `min` and `max` when given, a `number`. `"boolean"`: `true` or `false`, a `boolean`. `"choice"`: one of `choices`, as typed, a `string`. `"player"`: an online player by name, or a selector that picks exactly one (`@p`, `@s`), a `Player`. `"players"`: a name or a selector (`@a`, `@a[distance=..10]`) picking at least one player, a `Player[]`. `"entity"`: a selector that picks exactly one entity, an online player's name, or a loaded entity's UUID (a `Player` for a player), an `Entity`. `"entities"`: a selector, name or UUID picking at least one entity, an `Entity[]`. `"world"`: a loaded world by name, a `World`. `"position"`: three coordinates, each a number, `~` (relative to the sender) or `^` (local to where they look); whole numbers are block centres in x and z, as in vanilla commands, a `Vec3`. `"location"`: the same three coordinates, in the sender's world facing the way they face (the default world and no facing from the console), a `Location`. `"block_state"`: a block state like `oak_stairs[facing=east]`, given back in full with every property (`"minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=bottom,…]"`), a `string`. `"item"`: an item like `diamond_sword`, or with components on Paper (`diamond_sword[enchantments={sharpness:3}]`), an `Item`. `"centity"`: a live centity by its instance id (completed from the live ones), a `Centity`. `"centity_kind"`: one of the project's centities, by its folder name, a `string`. `"menu"`: one of the project's menus, by its id, a `string`. `"dialog"`: one of the project's dialogs, by its id, a `Dialog`.

fields.name: default
fields.doc: Makes it optional: the value the handler gets when it's left out. A value of the argument's type (a number for `integer`, a `Vec3` for `position`, one of `choices` for `choice`), or `false` for "nothing", the way to make a `player` or `item` argument optional: then `event.arguments.target or event.player`.

fields.name: min
fields.doc: The smallest value an `integer` or `number` argument takes.

fields.name: max
fields.doc: The largest value an `integer` or `number` argument takes.

fields.name: choices
fields.doc: What a `choice` argument takes: single words. Required for `choice`, and only for it.

fields.name: complete
fields.doc: Tab completion of its own, instead of what its type offers. Gets the event so far (`event.arguments` holds the arguments before this one) and what has been typed of this argument; returns the suggestions. NetherForge keeps those starting with `partial`. Runs in the module's scope, within its instruction budget, every time a player's client asks, so keep it cheap.

shapes.name: CommandEvent
shapes.doc: What a command handler, and an argument's `complete`, receives.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The command's name, as registered.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: What they typed to run it: the name, or one of its aliases.

fields.name: arguments
fields.doc: The arguments by name, typed by their declaration: a `Player` for a `player` argument, a `Vec3` for a `position`, an `integer` for an `integer`. An optional argument left out has its `default`.

fields.name: input
fields.doc: Everything typed after the command's name, subcommands included, as typed.

fields.name: sender
fields.doc: Who ran it, player or console. Answer them with `event.sender:send_message(text)`.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: The player who ran it, or `nil` from the console. Never `nil` in a `players_only` command.

shapes.name: WorldCreateOptions
shapes.doc: How `nf.worlds.create` makes a world. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: generator
fields.doc: Which of the game's own world types generates it: the usual (`"normal"`), the default superflat (`"flat"`), nothing at all (`"void"`, for maps built or placed by scripts), or one of the other vanilla world types (`"amplified"`, `"large_biomes"`). Default `"normal"`. Not with `terrain`, which is one of the project's instead. Only a `"normal"` environment takes it: a nether or an end always generates as the game's own.

fields.name: terrain
fields.doc: One of the project's terrains (`terrain/<id>.json`; `"acme:hills"` for a package's), which generates it in place of the game's own. Not with `generator`. Kept with the world, so it generates the same way when it's loaded again; a terrain the project changes later only shapes chunks generated afterwards. A world with a terrain is a `"normal"` environment.

fields.name: environment
fields.doc: Which kind of dimension: its sky, its light, whether water boils. Default `"normal"`.

fields.name: dimension_type
fields.doc: One of the project's dimension types (`dimension_types/<id>.json`; `"acme:deep"` for a package's): the world's build limits, light, sky and rules (beds, respawn anchors, piglins, raids) are its. Kept with the world, so it loads the same again. The server learns dimension types only as it starts: one it didn't start with (added or fixed since) is an error until it restarts. Default: the environment's own (the game's overworld, nether or end).

fields.name: seed
fields.doc: Its seed: a project generator makes the same world for the same seed. Default: a random one.

fields.name: structures
fields.doc: Whether villages, temples and the like generate. Default `true`.

fields.name: keep_spawn_loaded
fields.doc: Whether the chunks around its spawn stay loaded with nobody near. Default `false`.

shapes.name: WorldUnloadOptions
shapes.doc: How `world:unload` lets a world go. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: save
fields.doc: Whether it saves first. Default `true`; `false` throws away what changed since the last save (with `delete`, nothing is saved either way).

fields.name: delete
fields.doc: Whether its files are deleted afterwards, and the project forgets it. Default `false`.

fields.name: move_players_to
fields.doc: Which world the players in it go to, at its spawn. Default: the main world. To send them somewhere exact, teleport them before unloading.

shapes.name: BorderSizeOptions
shapes.doc: How `border:set_size` changes it. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: ticks
fields.doc: How long it takes to get there, moving steadily. Default 0: at once.

shapes.name: BorderDamage
shapes.doc: How a border hurts players outside it: what `border:damage()` gives and `border:set_damage` takes. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: amount
fields.doc: Damage each second for every block past `buffer` (half a heart is 1). The game starts at 0.2.

fields.name: buffer
fields.doc: How many blocks outside the border are safe. The game starts at 5.

shapes.name: BorderWarning
shapes.doc: When players' screens turn red as a border comes near: what `border:warning()` gives and `border:set_warning` takes. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: distance
fields.doc: Within this many blocks of it. The game starts at 5.

fields.name: ticks
fields.doc: When a shrinking border will reach them within this many ticks. The game starts at 300 (15 seconds).

shapes.name: StructureSaveOptions
shapes.doc: What `world:save_structure` keeps. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: entities
fields.doc: Whether the entities in the box are saved with the blocks (never players, and never what centities are drawn with). Default `false`.

shapes.name: StructurePlaceOptions
shapes.doc: How `world:place_structure` places one. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: rotation
fields.doc: How far it turns clockwise (seen from above) about its smallest corner, in degrees: 0, 90, 180 or 270 (any multiple of 90). Default 0.

fields.name: mirror
fields.doc: Whether it's mirrored first: `"left_right"` flips it along z, `"front_back"` along x. Default `"none"`.

fields.name: integrity
fields.doc: How much of it is placed, 0 to 1: each block is kept with this chance. Default 1: all of it.

fields.name: entities
fields.doc: Whether the entities saved with it are placed too. Default `true`.

shapes.name: GradualPlaceOptions
shapes.doc: How `world:place_gradually` places one. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: rotation
fields.doc: How far it turns clockwise (seen from above) about its smallest corner, in degrees: 0, 90, 180 or 270 (any multiple of 90). Default 0.

fields.name: mirror
fields.doc: Whether it's mirrored first: `"left_right"` flips it along z, `"front_back"` along x. Default `"none"`.

fields.name: integrity
fields.doc: How much of it is placed, 0 to 1: each block is kept with this chance. Default 1: all of it.

fields.name: entities
fields.doc: Whether the entities saved with it are placed too, once its blocks are in. Default `true`.

fields.name: per_tick
fields.doc: The most blocks it places in one tick, 1 or more: slower than the server's share, never faster. Default: as many as its share allows.

shapes.name: GradualFillOptions
shapes.doc: How `world:fill_gradually` fills. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: update
fields.doc: Whether neighbours react to each block (sand falls, water flows), as `BlockSetOptions` says. Default `true`.

fields.name: per_tick
fields.doc: The most blocks it goes through in one tick, 1 or more: slower than the server's share, never faster. Default: as many as its share allows.

shapes.name: BlockBoxOptions
shapes.doc: What `world:blocks` gives for each block. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: what
fields.doc: What a block is given as: `"kind"` its block id (`"minecraft:stone"`), `"solid"` whether it's solid, as `block:is_solid()` says, or `"class"` a number, `0` for a block nothing stands in the way of (air, grass, a torch), `1` for water or lava, `2` for a solid one. Default `"kind"`.

fields.name: custom
fields.doc: Whether a block of the project's own gives its id (`"wooden_chair"`, as `block:custom():id()` says) in place of what `what` would make of the note block it's held as. Default `false`.

shapes.name: BlockBox
shapes.doc: What `world:blocks` read: each block of the box, in one list, and the box's size and corner.

fields.name: cells
fields.doc: Each block, x fastest, then z, then y: the block `x`, `y`, `z` from the corner is at `1 + x + size_x * (z + size_z * y)`. What each is depends on `options.what` (and `options.custom`).

fields.name: size_x
fields.doc: How many blocks the box is along x.

fields.name: size_y
fields.doc: How many blocks the box is along y.

fields.name: size_z
fields.doc: How many blocks the box is along z.

fields.name: corner
fields.doc: The block the box starts from: the lowest x, y and z of its corners, floored.

shapes.name: SkyOptions
shapes.doc: How a sky comes or goes. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: fade_ticks
fields.doc: Ticks it takes to fade in or out, through the sky's steps (its file's `fade`). Default 0: at once.

shapes.name: BlockSetOptions
shapes.doc: How a block is changed. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: update
fields.doc: Whether its neighbours react (sand falls, redstone updates, water flows), as when a player places a block. Default `true`; `false` sets it quietly.

shapes.name: ParticleOptions
shapes.doc: How particles are spawned. Every key is optional; which ones a particle takes depends on its kind, and one it doesn't take is an error, as is any key that isn't one of these.

fields.name: count
fields.doc: How many, scattered around the position by `spread`. Default 1. With 0, one particle is sent moving along `spread` (a direction) at `speed`.

fields.name: spread
fields.doc: How far they scatter along each axis (a Gaussian spread), in blocks. Default none. With `count = 0`, the direction the one particle moves in.

fields.name: speed
fields.doc: How fast they move, for particles that move. Default 0.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: `"#rrggbb"`: dust, dust that changes colour, and coloured particles. Default white.

fields.name: to_color
fields.doc: `"#rrggbb"`: what dust that changes colour fades to. Default white.

fields.name: size
fields.doc: How big dust is, 0.01 to 4. Default 1.

fields.name: block_state
fields.doc: Which block block particles are made of: `"minecraft:stone"`. Required for those.

fields.name: item
fields.doc: Which item item particles show. Required for those.

fields.name: viewers
fields.doc: Only these players see them (those near enough). Default: everyone near enough.

fields.name: force
fields.doc: Show them even to players who turned particles down, and from up to 128 blocks away. Default `false`.

shapes.name: SoundOptions
shapes.doc: How a sound plays. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: volume
fields.doc: How loud, from 0. Default 1. Above 1 it carries further rather than getting louder: 16 blocks per 1.

fields.name: pitch
fields.doc: How high, 0.5 (an octave down) to 2 (an octave up). Default 1.

fields.name: category
fields.doc: Which of the player's volume sliders it follows. Default `"master"`.

shapes.name: WeatherOptions
shapes.doc: How weather set with `world:set_weather` lasts. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: ticks
fields.doc: How long it lasts before the game picks again (at least 1). Leave it out for a random length, as the game chooses.

shapes.name: ExplosionOptions
shapes.doc: How an explosion behaves. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: fire
fields.doc: Whether it sets fires. Default `false`.

fields.name: break_blocks
fields.doc: Whether it breaks blocks. Default `true`.

shapes.name: BiomeSearchOptions
shapes.doc: Where `world:locate_biome` looks. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: near
fields.doc: Where it looks from, in this world. Default the world's spawn.

fields.name: radius
fields.doc: How far it looks, in blocks across: 1 to 6400. Default 6400, as `/locate biome`.

shapes.name: LightningOptions
shapes.doc: How lightning strikes. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: effect_only
fields.doc: Only the flash and the thunder: no fire, no damage. Default `false`.

shapes.name: RaycastOptions
shapes.doc: What a ray can hit. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: blocks
fields.doc: Whether blocks stop it. Default `true`.

fields.name: entities
fields.doc: Whether entities (players included) stop it, by their hitboxes. Default `true`.

fields.name: ignore
fields.doc: Entities it goes through: the one it's cast from, usually. Default none.

fields.name: centities
fields.doc: Whether centities' hitboxes stop it. Default `true`.

fields.name: fluids
fields.doc: Whether water and lava stop it, as solid blocks. Default `false`: it goes through them.

shapes.name: FloodOptions
shapes.doc: How `world:flood` fills. A block is named as it is in a game block file: an id (`"minecraft:oak_log"`), a `#tag` (`"#minecraft:logs"`) or a project block's id (`"ruby_ore"`), or by what it is: `"solid"` (what players stand on), `"liquid"` (water and lava) or `"passable"` (neither: air, torches, flowers). A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: through
fields.doc: The blocks it fills: each one it reaches that any of these names. Required.

fields.name: except
fields.doc: Blocks it doesn't fill even when `through` names them: `{ "#minecraft:doors" }` keeps a room's air from leaking out through a door. Default none.

fields.name: directions
fields.doc: Which neighbours it goes on to from each block, as offsets of whole blocks (`vec3(0, 1, 0)` is the one above), at most 2 on each axis. Default the six that share a face: `vec3(1, 0, 0)`, `vec3(-1, 0, 0)` and so on. A tree felled up and sideways but never down leaves out every offset with y = -1.

fields.name: limit
fields.doc: The most blocks it fills, at least 1, at most 32,768. Default 4,096. `stopped` is `"limit"` when there was more.

fields.name: bounds
fields.doc: `{ min = Vec3, max = Vec3 }`: it never fills a block outside this box (both corners' blocks included), and `stopped` is `"bounds"` when it would have. Default: no box.

fields.name: kinds
fields.doc: Also answer what each block is (`kinds`, `edge_kinds`): its id without properties (`"minecraft:oak_log"`), or a project block's id. Default `false`.

shapes.name: FloodResult
shapes.doc: What `world:flood` filled.

fields.name: positions
fields.doc: Every block it filled, as its lowest corner (whole numbers), the start first, then outward a step at a time.

fields.name: edges
fields.doc: Every block next to one it filled that it didn't fill (a tree's leaves, a room's walls and door), once each. Not a block in an unloaded chunk or outside its `bounds`.

fields.name: kinds
fields.doc: With `kinds = true`, what each of `positions` is, in the same order. `nil` otherwise.

fields.name: edge_kinds
fields.doc: With `kinds = true`, what each of `edges` is, in the same order. `nil` otherwise.

fields.name: stopped
fields.doc: Why it didn't fill everything it reaches: `"limit"` (more past its limit), `"unloaded"` (a chunk that isn't loaded, or the world's top or bottom, in its way) or `"bounds"`. `nil` when it filled all of it: a closed room, a whole tree.

shapes.name: QueryOptions
shapes.doc: What a spatial query (`world:overlap_box`, `overlap_sphere`, `overlap_cone`, `nearest`) finds. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: centities
fields.doc: Whether it finds centities. Default `true`.

fields.name: players
fields.doc: Whether it finds players. Default `true`.

fields.name: entities
fields.doc: Whether it finds entities that aren't players (mobs, dropped items, arrows...). Default `true`.

fields.name: kinds
fields.doc: Only centities of these kinds (their folder names), and entities of these types (`"minecraft:zombie"`). Default: any.

fields.name: exclude
fields.doc: What it leaves out: whatever is asking, usually. Default none.

fields.name: limit
fields.doc: At most this many, the nearest. At least 1. Default: all.

fields.name: line_of_sight
fields.doc: Only what a ray from the query's own point (the middle of a box, the centre of a sphere, a cone's tip, a sweep's start) reaches without a block in the way, aimed at its hitbox's nearest point. Default `false`.

shapes.name: SweepOptions
shapes.doc: How `world:sweep` moves and what it finds: everything `QueryOptions` takes, and these. A key that isn't one of them is an error.

fields.name: centities
fields.doc: Whether it finds centities. Default `true`.

fields.name: players
fields.doc: Whether it finds players. Default `true`.

fields.name: entities
fields.doc: Whether it finds entities that aren't players (mobs, dropped items, arrows...). Default `true`.

fields.name: kinds
fields.doc: Only centities of these kinds (their folder names), and entities of these types (`"minecraft:zombie"`). Default: any.

fields.name: exclude
fields.doc: What it leaves out: whatever is asking, usually. Default none.

fields.name: limit
fields.doc: At most this many, the nearest. At least 1. Default: all.

fields.name: line_of_sight
fields.doc: Only what a ray from the query's own point (the middle of a box, the centre of a sphere, a cone's tip, a sweep's start) reaches without a block in the way, aimed at its hitbox's nearest point. Default `false`.

fields.name: radius
fields.doc: The moving sphere's radius, in blocks, at least 0. Default 0: a point.

fields.name: blocks
fields.doc: Whether blocks stop it (their collision shapes, as `raycast` sees them). Default `true`. A block stops the sphere's middle, not its edge.

fields.name: fluids
fields.doc: Whether water and lava stop it, as solid blocks. Default `false`.

shapes.name: QueryHit
shapes.doc: One thing a spatial query found. Exactly one of `centity`, `entity` and `block` is set: a `block` only ends a `world:sweep`.

fields.name: centity
fields.doc: The centity found, or `nil`.

fields.name: node
fields.doc: Which of `centity`'s nodes was nearest (its hitbox), or `nil` for anything else.

fields.name: entity
fields.doc: The player or entity found, or `nil`.

fields.name: block
fields.doc: The block a `world:sweep` stopped at, or `nil`.

fields.name: position
fields.doc: Where: for an overlap or `nearest`, the point of the hitbox nearest the query's own point; for a `sweep`, where the sphere's middle is when it first touches (on a block, where it stops).

fields.name: distance
fields.doc: How far that is from the query's own point; along the way, for a `sweep`. 0 when the point is inside the hitbox.

fields.name: normal
fields.doc: For a `sweep`'s block, the unit direction straight out of the face it met: what a bounce reflects off. `nil` otherwise.

shapes.name: RaycastHit
shapes.doc: What `world:raycast` hit: where, and what. Exactly one of `block`, `entity` and `centity` is set.

fields.name: position
fields.doc: Where the ray met it, in the world.

fields.name: normal
fields.doc: The unit direction straight out of the face it hit, in the world.

fields.name: distance
fields.doc: How far along the ray that is, in blocks.

fields.name: block
fields.doc: The block it hit, or `nil`.

fields.name: entity
fields.doc: The entity it hit, or `nil`.

fields.name: centity
fields.doc: The centity whose hitbox it hit, or `nil`.

fields.name: node
fields.doc: Which node of `centity` it hit (its hitbox), or `nil` for anything else.

shapes.name: BossBarAttachOptions
shapes.doc: How `bossbar:attach` ties a bar to a centity. Every key is optional; a key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: range
fields.doc: How near a player must be to see it, in blocks. Default 48.

fields.name: health
fields.doc: Its progress follows the centity's `health` (when it has any). Default `true`.

fields.name: remove_with
fields.doc: Removed when the centity is. Default `true`.

shapes.name: BossBarOptions
shapes.doc: What `nf.bossbars.create` makes a bar with. Every key is optional; a key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: text
fields.doc: What it says, MiniMessage. Default none.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: Default `"pink"`, the way vanilla bars start.

fields.name: style
fields.doc: One bar, or split into notches. Default `"progress"`, one bar.

fields.name: progress
fields.doc: How full, 0 to 1. Default 1.

fields.name: icon
fields.doc: A glyph (`<pack>/<key>`) drawn just left of the bar's left end, wherever the centred text puts its words: a boss's head, say. It's drawn on the text's line at the glyph's own `ascent`: the bar sits 2 pixels below the text's baseline, so a lower ascent (even a negative one) hangs it down beside the bar. Placing it needs the text's width, so text the server can't measure (no `fonts/default.json`) draws it in front of the words instead. Default none.

shapes.name: LootContext
shapes.doc: What `nf.loot.roll` and `nf.loot.fill` roll with: who and what the roll is for, which the table's conditions ask about. Every key is optional; a key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: The player behind the roll: who killed the mob, broke the block or opened the chest. A `player` condition passes only with one. Default none.

fields.name: tool
fields.doc: What the player killed or broke it with, for `tool` and `enchantment` conditions. Default none: those conditions don't pass.

fields.name: luck
fields.doc: The roll's luck: more `bonusRolls`, and each entry's weight shifted by its `quality`. Default 0.

fields.name: looted
fields.doc: The entity whose loot this is, which a game table for a mob needs. Default none.

fields.name: location
fields.doc: Where a game table is rolled. Default the player's place, else the looted entity's.

fields.name: seed
fields.doc: Rolls with this seed give the same items every time, on the server and in the editor. Default a new one each roll.

shapes.name: HudBar
shapes.doc: What a HUD bar shows: `hud:bar(name)`.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: How much of it is full, as set.

fields.name: max
fields.doc: Out of how much.

fields.name: segments
fields.doc: How many of its segments are drawn.

shapes.name: HudFillOptions
shapes.doc: How `hud:fill_bar` draws a bar.

fields.name: segments
fields.doc: Draw only this many of the bar's segments, 1 to its own. Default all of them.

shapes.name: SpawnCheck
shapes.doc: What a spawn condition (`nf.spawning.condition`) is asked about: one centity at one place.

fields.name: centity
fields.doc: Which centity, as the project names it: its folder name under `centities/` (`wisp`), or `acme:wisp` for one a package brings.

fields.name: location
fields.doc: Where it would stand: the block its feet would be in.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: The player it would appear near.

shapes.name: ProjectBlockPlaceEvent
shapes.doc: A block is about to be placed.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who is placing it, or `nil` for a script.

fields.name: block
fields.doc: Where it goes: what is there now is replaced, so `block:custom()` is `nil` until it has been placed (`this:id()` says which block is being placed).

fields.name: item
fields.doc: The stack placing it, or `nil` for a script.

fields.name: facing
fields.doc: The way it will face, for a block that turns: toward the player placing it. `nil` for one that doesn't turn.

shapes.name: BlockPlaceOptions
shapes.doc: How `project_block:place` places one. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: facing
fields.doc: The way its front faces, for a block that turns (`rotation` in its `block.json`): a way it can't face is an error. Default north.

shapes.name: ProjectBlockClickEvent
shapes.doc: A block was clicked.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who clicked.

fields.name: block
fields.doc: The block.

fields.name: click
fields.doc: Which button: the left (hit) or right (use).

fields.name: face
fields.doc: Which face of the block was clicked.

fields.name: item
fields.doc: What's in the hand the click was with, or `nil` for an empty hand.

fields.name: hand
fields.doc: Which hand: the game asks for each hand in turn.

shapes.name: ProjectBlockTickEvent
shapes.doc: A block ticked.

fields.name: block
fields.doc: The block that ticked.

shapes.name: TeamOptions
shapes.doc: What `nf.teams.create` makes a team with. Every key is optional; a key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: display_name
fields.doc: What it's called where Minecraft names a team, MiniMessage. Default its name.

fields.name: prefix
fields.doc: What goes before each member's name, MiniMessage. Default none.

fields.name: suffix
fields.doc: What goes after each member's name, MiniMessage. Default none.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: The colour of members' names and glow. Default none.

fields.name: friendly_fire
fields.doc: Whether members can hurt each other. Default `true`.

fields.name: see_invisible_teammates
fields.doc: Whether members see each other while invisible. Default `true`.

fields.name: nametags
fields.doc: `"always"` (the default), `"never"`, `"hide_for_other_teams"` (only teammates see them) or `"hide_for_own_team"` (only players outside the team see them).

fields.name: collision
fields.doc: `"always"` (the default), `"never"`, `"push_other_teams"` (members pass through each other) or `"push_own_team"` (members push only each other).

shapes.name: ScheduleOptions
shapes.doc: What a schedule is called and what to do about a run the server missed. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: A name for the schedule, which what it last ran is kept under, so it's known across restarts. Lowercase letters, digits and `_` (starting with a letter or digit, at most 64 characters), and no two of a package's live schedules share one. Default none: the schedule is forgotten when it stops.

fields.name: catch_up
fields.doc: Run once when the script starts if a run was missed since the schedule last ran (the server was off over its time). Needs an `id`; a schedule seen for the first time has missed nothing. Default `false`: a missed run is skipped.

shapes.name: DatabaseStatement
shapes.doc: One statement of `db:transaction`.

fields.name: sql
fields.doc: One SQL statement in the database's own dialect (SQLite's for the package's own database; MySQL's or PostgreSQL's for a connection the server owner set up), with `?` where a value goes: the values come in `params`, never inside the text, so a name a player typed can't become SQL. A second statement after a `;` is an error: use `db:transaction` for several. On PostgreSQL a literal `?` (the JSON operators) is written `??`.

fields.name: params
fields.doc: The values for the `?`s, in order: `{ player_name, 5 }`. Each is a `string`, `number`, `integer` or `boolean` (stored as 1 or 0); a hole in the list (`{ 1, nil, 3 }`) is SQL `NULL`, and so are the last `?`s when the list is shorter (Lua can't tell `{ name, nil }` from `{ name }`). Any other kind of value is an error, and more values than `?`s fails the statement.

shapes.name: DatabaseResult
shapes.doc: What `db:execute` (and each statement of `db:transaction`) did.

fields.name: changes
fields.doc: How many rows it inserted, updated or deleted.

fields.name: last_insert_id
fields.doc: On the package's own database, the `rowid` of the last row it inserted (the new row's `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`), or `nil` when nothing was ever inserted. On a MySQL connection, the `AUTO_INCREMENT` key the statement generated, or `nil` when it generated none. On PostgreSQL always `nil`: ask for the key with `INSERT ... RETURNING id` through `db:query`.

shapes.name: HttpRequestOptions
shapes.doc: What `nf.http.request` takes.

fields.name: url
fields.doc: An `http://` or `https://` URL, without a user name or password in it (send credentials in a header). Its host must be one the calling package declares in `requires`.

fields.name: method
fields.doc: The HTTP method; `"GET"` when left out.

fields.name: headers
fields.doc: Request headers by name. `Host`, `Content-Length`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Connection`, `Upgrade` and the like are set by the server and refused here. A `User-Agent` of `NetherForge` is sent unless you give one. `Authorization`, `Cookie` and `Proxy-Authorization` are dropped when a redirect leads to another host.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: The request body, as text (UTF-8). Its size is limited by `http.max-request-bytes` in the server's `config.yml`. A `GET`, `HEAD` or `OPTIONS` can't have one.

shapes.name: HttpResponse
shapes.doc: What `nf.http.request` gives.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: The status code: `200`, `404`.

fields.name: headers
fields.doc: The response headers by name in lowercase (`response.headers["content-type"]`); a header sent more than once is its values joined with `, `.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: The body as text, decoded by the charset the response names (UTF-8 when it names none), so a response that isn't text (an image) doesn't survive. Its size is limited by `http.max-response-bytes` in the server's `config.yml`.

fields.name: url
fields.doc: The URL the response came from: the request's own, or where its redirects ended.

shapes.name: HttpStreamOptions
shapes.doc: What `nf.http.stream` takes: `nf.http.request`'s options, and `format`.

fields.name: url
fields.doc: An `http://` or `https://` URL, as for `nf.http.request`. Its host must be one the calling package declares in `requires`.

fields.name: method
fields.doc: The HTTP method; `"GET"` when left out.

fields.name: headers
fields.doc: Request headers by name, as for `nf.http.request`. A `format` of `"events"` sends `Accept: text/event-stream` unless you give an `Accept`.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: The request body, as for `nf.http.request` (`http.max-request-bytes`).

fields.name: format
fields.doc: How the response is split into messages. `"lines"` (the default): one message per line, without its line ending (NDJSON, a log tail). `"events"`: Server-Sent Events (`text/event-stream`), one message per event, with its `type` and `id`; comments and `retry` are skipped. `"chunks"`: the text as it arrives, in pieces of no particular size. A line or event over `connections.max-message-bytes` ends the stream (reason `"limit"`); text is UTF-8.

shapes.name: WebSocketOptions
shapes.doc: What `nf.http.websocket` takes.

fields.name: url
fields.doc: A `ws://` or `wss://` URL, without a user name or password in it. Its host must be one the calling package declares in `requires.http`.

fields.name: headers
fields.doc: Headers for the opening request (an `Authorization`), with `nf.http.request`'s rules. The `Sec-WebSocket-*` headers are the server's to set.

fields.name: protocols
fields.doc: Subprotocols to offer (`Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`), in order of preference; `socket:protocol()` says which one the other side chose.

shapes.name: HttpStreamOpenEvent
shapes.doc: A stream's response began.

fields.name: stream
fields.doc: The stream.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: The status code: `200`, `404`.

fields.name: headers
fields.doc: The response headers by name in lowercase, as `nf.http.request` gives them.

shapes.name: HttpStreamMessageEvent
shapes.doc: A piece of a stream arrived.

fields.name: stream
fields.doc: The stream.

fields.name: data
fields.doc: The line (without its line ending), the event's data (its `data:` lines joined with line breaks), or the chunk.

fields.name: type
fields.doc: For `format = "events"`: the event's type, `"message"` when it names none. `nil` for the other formats.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: For `format = "events"`: the last event id the stream set (`id:`), which a script reconnecting sends back as `Last-Event-ID`. `nil` when none was set, and for the other formats.

shapes.name: HttpStreamEndEvent
shapes.doc: A stream ended.

fields.name: stream
fields.doc: The stream.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: Why: the server ended the response; `close()` was called; the connection couldn't be made or broke (a name that doesn't resolve, an address that isn't allowed, a refused connection, a redirect it couldn't follow, no answer within `http.timeout-seconds`); an owner's limit in `config.yml`'s `http:` section was reached (too many connections open, the request rate, a message over `connections.max-message-bytes`, the package's `connections.bytes-per-minute`); nothing arrived for `connections.idle-seconds`; or the script that opened it unloaded.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: The response's status, when it had opened.

fields.name: detail
fields.doc: What went wrong, in words, for `"failed"` and `"limit"`; `nil` otherwise.

shapes.name: WebSocketOpenEvent
shapes.doc: A WebSocket opened.

fields.name: socket
fields.doc: The socket.

fields.name: protocol
fields.doc: The subprotocol the other side chose, or `nil`.

fields.name: headers
fields.doc: The opening response's headers by name in lowercase.

shapes.name: WebSocketMessageEvent
shapes.doc: A text message arrived on a WebSocket.

fields.name: socket
fields.doc: The socket.

fields.name: data
fields.doc: The message.

shapes.name: WebSocketEndEvent
shapes.doc: A WebSocket ended.

fields.name: socket
fields.doc: The socket.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: Why: the other side closed it (`code` and `detail` say how); `close()` was called; the connection couldn't be made, was refused or broke (as for a stream; a server that doesn't speak WebSocket at that URL, or a binary message); an owner's limit in `config.yml`'s `http:` section was reached (too many connections open, the request rate, a message over `connections.max-message-bytes`, the package's `connections.bytes-per-minute`); nothing was sent or arrived for `connections.idle-seconds`; or the script that opened it unloaded.

fields.name: code
fields.doc: For `"finished"`: the close code the other side sent (`1000` is a normal close).

fields.name: detail
fields.doc: For `"finished"`: the reason the other side gave, if any. For `"failed"` and `"limit"`: what went wrong, in words. `nil` otherwise.

shapes.name: WebRequest
shapes.doc: A request a route answers.

fields.name: method
fields.doc: `"GET"`, `"POST"`, … (`"HEAD"` for a `GET` route asked only for headers).

fields.name: path
fields.doc: The path asked for, namespace and all: `"/shop/replays/12"`.

fields.name: params
fields.doc: The route's `:name` and `*name` segments by name, decoded.

fields.name: query
fields.doc: The query parameters by name, decoded. A name given more than once is its first value.

fields.name: headers
fields.doc: The request headers by name in lowercase; one sent more than once is its values joined with `, `.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: The body as text (UTF-8), at most `web.max-body-bytes`; `""` for none.

fields.name: form
fields.doc: The body's fields, decoded, when it's a form (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`); `nil` otherwise.

fields.name: ip
fields.doc: The address it came from. Behind a reverse proxy that's the proxy's, unless the owner set `web.trust-proxy-headers`, which makes it the client's from `X-Forwarded-For`.

shapes.name: SignatureOptions
shapes.doc: How `nf.web.verify_signature` checks a signature.

fields.name: secret
fields.doc: The secret the sender signs with.

fields.name: algorithm
fields.doc: The HMAC's hash. Default `"sha256"`.

fields.name: encoding
fields.doc: How the signature is written. Default `"hex"` (either case).

fields.name: prefix
fields.doc: Text before the signature to expect and skip, like `"sha256="`.

shapes.name: OAuthOptions
shapes.doc: What `nf.web.oauth` takes.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The flow's name, unique in the package: lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`. Its callback is `/<namespace>/oauth/<name>/callback`.

fields.name: authorize_url
fields.doc: The service's authorization page: an `https://` URL.

fields.name: token_url
fields.doc: The service's token endpoint: an `https://` URL whose host the package declares in `requires.http`.

fields.name: client_id
fields.doc: The client id the service gave you.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.doc: The client secret, for a service that wants one besides PKCE. Keep it in a setting (`nf.config`).

fields.name: scopes
fields.doc: The scopes to ask for, sent separated by spaces.

fields.name: client_auth
fields.doc: How the secret is sent to the token endpoint: in the form (`"body"`, the default) or as HTTP Basic (`"basic"`).

fields.name: parameters
fields.doc: More query parameters for the authorization page, like `{ prompt = "consent" }`.

shapes.name: OAuthCompleteEvent
shapes.doc: A login finished.

fields.name: flow
fields.doc: The flow.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who logged in (perhaps offline by now).

fields.name: access_token
fields.doc: The access token, to call the service as them.

fields.name: token_type
fields.doc: Its type, usually `"Bearer"`.

fields.name: refresh_token
fields.doc: A refresh token, if the service gave one.

fields.name: expires_in
fields.doc: How many seconds the access token lasts, if the service said.

fields.name: scope
fields.doc: The scopes granted, if the service said.

fields.name: id_token
fields.doc: An OpenID Connect ID token, if the service gave one.

shapes.name: OAuthFailEvent
shapes.doc: A login didn't finish.

fields.name: flow
fields.doc: The flow.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who was logging in.

fields.name: error
fields.doc: What went wrong, in words.

shapes.name: WasmFunction
shapes.doc: A function a module exports, from `nf.wasm.functions`.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Its name: `"sample"`.

fields.name: params
fields.doc: Its parameters' types in order: `"i32"`, `"i64"`, `"f32"`, `"f64"` (a `"v128"` or a reference can't be passed).

fields.name: results
fields.doc: Its results' types in order.

shapes.name: WasmRunOptions
shapes.doc: What `nf.wasm.run` takes.

fields.name: stdin
fields.doc: Its whole input; after it, the program reads the end of the file. None when left out.

fields.name: arguments
fields.doc: Its arguments, after its name (the module's id, `argv[0]`).

fields.name: environment
fields.doc: Its environment variables; none when left out (it never sees the server's).

shapes.name: WasmStartOptions
shapes.doc: What `nf.wasm.start` takes.

fields.name: arguments
fields.doc: Its arguments, after its name (the module's id, `argv[0]`).

fields.name: environment
fields.doc: Its environment variables; none when left out (it never sees the server's).

shapes.name: WasmRunResult
shapes.doc: What a program `nf.wasm.run` ran did.

fields.name: exit_code
fields.doc: Its exit code: `0` when it says it worked, as programs do.

fields.name: stdout
fields.doc: What it printed to its standard output, up to `wasm.max-output-bytes`.

fields.name: stderr
fields.doc: What it printed to its standard error, up to the same.

shapes.name: WasmOutputEvent
shapes.doc: A program printed a line.

fields.name: process
fields.doc: The program.

fields.name: line
fields.doc: The line, without its line ending (UTF-8).

fields.name: stream
fields.doc: Which it printed it to: its standard output or its standard error.

shapes.name: WasmEndEvent
shapes.doc: A program ended.

fields.name: process
fields.doc: The program.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: Why: it exited (`exit_code` says how), `stop()` was called, it failed (it trapped, or the module couldn't be compiled or started: `detail` says why), an owner's limit in `config.yml`'s `wasm:` section was reached, or the script that started it unloaded.

fields.name: exit_code
fields.doc: Its exit code, when it exited; `nil` otherwise.

fields.name: detail
fields.doc: What went wrong, in words, for `"failed"` and `"limit"`; `nil` otherwise.

shapes.name: NetworkServer
shapes.doc: A server of the network, from `nf.network.servers`.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Its name, as the proxy names it.

fields.name: connected
fields.doc: Whether NetherForge on it is connected to the hub now (a server without NetherForge never is).

fields.name: players
fields.doc: How many players are on it.

shapes.name: NetworkPlayer
shapes.doc: A player online in the network.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Their UUID, as a string: the same as `player:id()` on their server.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Their name.

fields.name: server
fields.doc: The server they're on; `nil` for a moment while the proxy is moving them.

shapes.name: NetworkPublishOptions
shapes.doc: What `channel:publish` takes. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: server
fields.doc: Only this server hears it (if it listens), by its name in the network; every server listening when left out.

shapes.name: NetworkMapWriteOptions
shapes.doc: What `map:set`, `add` and `insert` take. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: expires
fields.doc: Ticks (20 a second) from now until the hub deletes the key, as a `change` with cause `"expired"`; never when left out. Counted by the hub's clock, whatever any server's ticks do.

shapes.name: NetworkMessageEvent
shapes.doc: Something was published on a channel.

fields.name: channel
fields.doc: The channel.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: What was published.

fields.name: server
fields.doc: The server it was published on (maybe this one).

shapes.name: NetworkRequestEvent
shapes.doc: A server asked this one on a channel.

fields.name: channel
fields.doc: The channel.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: What it asked with.

fields.name: server
fields.doc: The server asking (maybe this one).

fields.name: reply
fields.doc: Writable: the answer, sent back once the handlers have run. Anything a `data()` table can hold, sent as JSON with the same codec: tables, strings, numbers, booleans, `Vec3`, `Location` (its world by name) and handles to entities and worlds (by UUID and name, which another server may not have). At most `max-value-bytes` as JSON (the proxy's `hub.properties`, 64 KiB unless its owner says otherwise); a value over it, or one that can't be written as JSON, is an error at the script's line.

shapes.name: NetworkMapChangeEvent
shapes.doc: A key of a shared map changed.

fields.name: map
fields.doc: The map.

fields.name: key
fields.doc: The key.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: Its value now; `nil` when it was deleted or expired.

fields.name: previous
fields.doc: Its value in this server's copy before.

fields.name: server
fields.doc: The server that changed it (maybe this one); `nil` when it expired.

fields.name: cause
fields.doc: What changed it: a write that set it (`set`, `add` or `insert`), a `delete` (or `set` to `nil`), or its expiry.

shapes.name: NetworkMapReadyEvent
shapes.doc: A shared map's copy arrived on this server.

fields.name: map
fields.doc: The map.

shapes.name: NetworkConnectEvent
shapes.doc: This server connected to its network's hub.

fields.name: server
fields.doc: This server's name in the network.

shapes.name: NetworkDisconnectEvent
shapes.doc: This server lost its connection to the network's hub.

fields.name: detail
fields.doc: What happened, in words, for the log.

shapes.name: NetworkServerEvent
shapes.doc: Another server of the network connected or disconnected.

fields.name: server
fields.doc: Its name in the network, as the proxy names it.

shapes.name: NetworkPlayerEvent
shapes.doc: A player joined or left the network.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who, and the server they joined or were last on.

shapes.name: NetworkPlayerSwitchEvent
shapes.doc: A player went from one server of the network to another.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who, and the server they are on now.

fields.name: previous
fields.doc: The server they came from.

shapes.name: PlayerArriveEvent
shapes.doc: A player sent here from another server joined.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: The player, on this server now.

fields.name: from
fields.doc: The server that sent them.

fields.name: data
fields.doc: What the script that sent them gave `send_player`, as `nf.json` would read it back; `nil` when it gave nothing.

shapes.name: ParticlePlayOptions
shapes.doc: How `nf.particles.play` plays an effect. Every key is optional; a key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: viewers
fields.doc: Only these players see it (still only those within range). Players who leave drop out. Default: everyone in range.

fields.name: scale
fields.doc: Multiplies its distances: shape sizes, offsets, spreads and speeds (not dust sizes). More than 0, at most 16. Default 1.

fields.name: loop
fields.doc: Whether it starts again after its last tick, until it's stopped. Default: what its file says.

fields.name: follow
fields.doc: Follow this from the start, as `effect:follow` does. Each tick, before it spawns anything, the effect moves to the target: its position (a node's `world_position()`), facing the target's yaw (a node's centity's), pitch 0. When the target stops existing (a removed centity, a player who left, an entity that died or was removed, a centity or entity whose chunk unloaded) the effect ends with reason `"target_gone"`. `location_or_position` is still needed: it's where the effect is if the target is already gone, which ends it on its first tick.

fields.name: offset
fields.doc: With `follow`: where the effect sits from the target, as for `effect:follow`. Without `follow` it's an error.

shapes.name: EffectEndEvent
shapes.doc: A particle effect ended.

fields.name: effect
fields.doc: The effect.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: Why: it played to its end; `stop()` was called; what it followed went; its file was deleted; or the script that played it unloaded (a reload, its centity removed, the server stopping).

shapes.name: CutscenePlayOptions
shapes.doc: How `nf.cutscenes.play` plays a cutscene. Every key is optional; a key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: origin
fields.doc: Where the path's coordinates are measured from: every camera position is added to it (the path is moved, not turned). A `Location` also says which world the cutscene is in (its `yaw` and `pitch` are not used); a `Vec3` is in the player's world. Default: the path's coordinates are the world's, in the player's world.

fields.name: skippable
fields.doc: Whether the player may end it early by sneaking (reason `"skipped"`). Default: what the cutscene's file says, which defaults to `false`.

shapes.name: CutsceneEndEvent
shapes.doc: A cutscene ended.

fields.name: cutscene
fields.doc: The cutscene.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who was watching.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: Why: it played to its end; `stop()` was called; the player sneaked, in a skippable one; another cutscene was played for the player; the player left the server; or the script that played it unloaded (a reload, the server stopping).

shapes.name: CutsceneCueEvent
shapes.doc: A cutscene reached a named cue.

fields.name: cutscene
fields.doc: The cutscene.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who is watching.

fields.name: cue
fields.doc: The cue's `event` name in the cutscene's file.

shapes.name: ScreenOptions
shapes.doc: A screen `nf.screens.create` makes: `width` and `height` are required; a key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: width
fields.doc: Maps across, 1 to 16.

fields.name: height
fields.doc: Maps down, 1 to 16.

fields.name: key
fields.doc: Keeps its maps' numbers for good, across restarts (see `nf.screens.create`): any name, unique among the screens this package's scripts make. Making one with a key a screen that's still there has is an error.

fields.name: background
fields.doc: What it starts filled with. A colour, `#rrggbb` (drawn as the nearest of the colours a map can show), or `"clear"` for none: the map shows through. Default `"clear"`.

fields.name: viewers
fields.doc: `"near"` (the default): every player near where it hangs, or everyone online while it hangs nowhere. `"script"`: only those `show_to` shows it to.

fields.name: range
fields.doc: How near is near, in blocks: 1 to 256 (default 64).

fields.name: glowing
fields.doc: Whether its frames glow, drawing it at full brightness (default true).

fields.name: click_range
fields.doc: How far a click reaches it from, in blocks: 0 to 64 (default 24). Within the game's reach a click on a frame always counts.

shapes.name: ShapeStyle
shapes.doc: How a shape is drawn: `fill`, `outline`, or both (neither is an error).

fields.name: fill
fields.doc: Its inside. A colour, `#rrggbb` (drawn as the nearest of the colours a map can show), or `"clear"` for none: the map shows through.

fields.name: outline
fields.doc: Its edge. A colour, `#rrggbb` (drawn as the nearest of the colours a map can show), or `"clear"` for none: the map shows through.

fields.name: thickness
fields.doc: The outline's width, in pixels: 1 to 32 (default 1).

fields.name: radius
fields.doc: A rectangle's rounded corners, in pixels (default 0).

shapes.name: ScreenTextOptions
shapes.doc: How text is drawn on a screen. Every key is optional.

fields.name: font
fields.doc: `"default"` (the game's own map font, the default) or one of the project's (`screen_fonts/<id>/`).

fields.name: color
fields.doc: Its colour where the text sets none, `#rrggbb` (default white).

fields.name: scale
fields.doc: Each pixel of the font drawn this many pixels a side: 1 to 8 (default 1).

fields.name: align
fields.doc: Where `x` is: its left (the default), its middle or its right, line by line.

fields.name: width
fields.doc: Breaks lines at spaces so none is wider than this, in pixels.

fields.name: shadow
fields.doc: Draws a shadow a pixel down and right of every pixel, in this colour.

fields.name: line_height
fields.doc: Pixels from one line's top to the next's (default the font's).

shapes.name: ScreenTextSize
shapes.doc: How big text is drawn, in pixels.

fields.name: width
fields.doc: Its widest line.

fields.name: height
fields.doc: All its lines.

shapes.name: ScreenImageOptions
shapes.doc: How a picture is drawn on a screen. Every key is optional.

fields.name: width
fields.doc: Drawn this wide, in pixels (default its own width, or kept in shape with `height`).

fields.name: height
fields.doc: Drawn this tall, in pixels (default its own height, or kept in shape with `width`).

fields.name: dither
fields.doc: How its colours become map colours: `"floyd_steinberg"` (the default) spreads each pixel's error to its neighbours, best for photos; `"ordered"` uses a fixed pattern; `"none"` takes each pixel's nearest.

shapes.name: VideoPlayOptions
shapes.doc: How `screen:play` plays a video. Every key is optional.

fields.name: loop
fields.doc: Starts it again when it ends (default false).

fields.name: speed
fields.doc: How fast: 0.25 to 4 (default 1). Its sound plays only at 1.

fields.name: start
fields.doc: Where to start, in seconds (default 0).

fields.name: volume
fields.doc: Its sound's volume, 0 to 1 (default 1); 0 plays it silent.

fields.name: x
fields.doc: Where its left is on the screen, in pixels (default 0).

fields.name: y
fields.doc: Where its top is on the screen, in pixels (default 0).

fields.name: audio_range
fields.doc: How near where the screen hangs a player must be to hear it, in blocks (default 32). A screen that hangs nowhere plays its sound to everyone it's drawn for.

shapes.name: ScreenPoint
shapes.doc: A pixel of a screen a player aims at.

fields.name: screen
fields.doc: The screen: the player's own view of it, when they have one.

fields.name: x
fields.doc: From its left edge.

fields.name: y
fields.doc: From its top edge.

fields.name: distance
fields.doc: From the player's eyes, in blocks.

shapes.name: ScreenClickEvent
shapes.doc: A player clicked a screen.

fields.name: screen
fields.doc: The screen clicked: the player's own view of it, when they have one.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who clicked.

fields.name: x
fields.doc: The pixel aimed at, from the left edge.

fields.name: y
fields.doc: From the top edge.

fields.name: click
fields.doc: Which button.

shapes.name: ScreenHoverEvent
shapes.doc: The pixel a player aims at on a screen moved.

fields.name: screen
fields.doc: The screen: the player's own view of it, when they have one.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who.

fields.name: x
fields.doc: The pixel aimed at now, from the left edge.

fields.name: y
fields.doc: From the top edge.

shapes.name: ScreenLeaveEvent
shapes.doc: A player stopped aiming at a screen.

fields.name: screen
fields.doc: The screen.

fields.name: player
fields.doc: Who.

shapes.name: PlaybackEndEvent
shapes.doc: A video stopped playing.

fields.name: playback
fields.doc: The playback.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: Why: it played to its end (and doesn't loop); `stop()` was called; another video was played on the screen; the screen went; or the script that played it unloaded.

shapes.name: PlaybackFrameEvent
shapes.doc: A frame of a video was drawn.

fields.name: playback
fields.doc: The playback.

fields.name: frame
fields.doc: Which frame, 0 first.

fields.name: time
fields.doc: Its time in the video, in seconds.

shapes.name: TimeOptions
shapes.doc: How `nf.time.format` and `nf.time.parse` read a clock time. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: zone
fields.doc: Which time zone the clock time is in: an IANA name like `"Europe/London"` or `"America/New_York"`, `"UTC"`, or an offset like `"+02:00"`. Default the server owner's zone (`schedules.time-zone` in `config.yml`, the server's own by default), the one `nf.schedule` runs in. A zone the server doesn't know is an error.

shapes.name: NoiseOptions
shapes.doc: Which noise `nf.random.noise2` and `noise3` give. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: seed
fields.doc: Which noise: each seed is a different pattern. Default 0.

fields.name: scale
fields.doc: What the coordinates are multiplied by first: smaller is smoother and wider (0.05 changes over about 20 blocks). Default 1.

shapes.name: TestNetworkMessage
shapes.doc: A message another server of a test's network heard, from `nf.test.network_received`.

fields.name: channel
fields.doc: The channel's name, as the calling package names it.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: What was published.

fields.name: server
fields.doc: The server it was published on.

shapes.name: TestWasmStub
shapes.doc: What `nf.test.stub_wasm` answers a module with. Every key is optional; a key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: functions
fields.doc: An instance's functions by name: each gets the call's `arguments` and returns its results, a list for `call` (`{ 5 }`) or a string for `call_text`.

fields.name: run
fields.doc: What `module:run` gives: it gets the run's options (`stdin`, `arguments`, `environment`) and returns a result table.

fields.name: input
fields.doc: A started program's answer to each line it's sent: the lines it prints (to its standard output), or `nil` for none.

shapes.name: TestShownOptions
shapes.doc: Where `nf.test.shown` looks. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: menu
fields.doc: Whether `slot` is one of the window they have open, numbered from 0 as `menu:slot` numbers them.

shapes.name: TestClickOptions
shapes.doc: How `nf.test.click` clicks. Every key is optional; a key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: hand
fields.doc: Which hand clicks, and whose item is used. Default `"main_hand"`.

fields.name: block
fields.doc: The block clicked, which must be in a loaded chunk. Default: none, a click at the air.

fields.name: face
fields.doc: Which face of `block` was clicked. Default `"up"`; only with `block`.

shapes.name: TestInputKeys
shapes.doc: The keys `nf.test.input` holds down: each `true` is held, and one left out (or `false`) isn't. A key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: forward
fields.doc: Forward (W).

fields.name: backward
fields.doc: Back (S).

fields.name: left
fields.doc: Left (A).

fields.name: right
fields.doc: Right (D).

fields.name: jump
fields.doc: Jump (space).

fields.name: sneak
fields.doc: Sneak (shift).

fields.name: sprint
fields.doc: Sprint (control).

shapes.name: TestAcceptOptions
shapes.doc: How `nf.test.accept` answers. Every key is optional; a key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: A stream's status: 100 to 599. Default `200`.

fields.name: headers
fields.doc: The response headers (names are lowercased). Default: none.

fields.name: protocol
fields.doc: A WebSocket's chosen subprotocol: one of those it offered. Default: none.

shapes.name: TestDisconnectOptions
shapes.doc: How `nf.test.disconnect` ends a connection. Every key is optional; a key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: code
fields.doc: A WebSocket's close code. Default `1000`.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: A WebSocket's close reason, its `end` event's `detail`.

fields.name: error
fields.doc: Break it instead: it ends `"failed"`, with this as `detail`.

shapes.name: TestRequestOptions
shapes.doc: What `nf.test.request` sends. Every key is optional; a key that isn't one of these is an error.

fields.name: headers
fields.doc: Request headers by name.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: The body. Default none.

fields.name: ip
fields.doc: The address it comes from. Default `"127.0.0.1"`.

shapes.name: TestWebResponse
shapes.doc: What `nf.test.request` gives back: the answer as the client got it.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: The status code.

fields.name: headers
fields.doc: The response headers by name in lowercase.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: The body (empty for a `HEAD`).

shapes.name: RaisedEvent
shapes.doc: What `nf.test.raise` gives back.

fields.name: cancelled
fields.doc: Whether a handler called `event:cancel()` (always `false` for an event that can't be cancelled).

fields.name: event
fields.doc: The payload as the handlers left it: a writable field they assigned (`message`) holds what they set.

commandArguments.name: text
commandArguments.doc: the rest of the line, spaces and all

commandArguments.name: integer
commandArguments.doc: a whole number, within `min` and `max` when given

commandArguments.name: number
commandArguments.doc: any number, within `min` and `max` when given

commandArguments.name: player
commandArguments.doc: an online player by name, or a selector that picks exactly one (`@p`, `@s`)

commandArguments.name: players
commandArguments.doc: a name or a selector (`@a`, `@a[distance=..10]`) picking at least one player

commandArguments.name: entity
commandArguments.doc: a selector that picks exactly one entity, an online player's name, or a loaded entity's UUID (a `Player` for a player)

commandArguments.name: entities
commandArguments.doc: a selector, name or UUID picking at least one entity

commandArguments.name: position
commandArguments.doc: three coordinates, each a number, `~` (relative to the sender) or `^` (local to where they look); whole numbers are block centres in x and z, as in vanilla commands

commandArguments.name: location
commandArguments.doc: the same three coordinates, in the sender's world facing the way they face (the default world and no facing from the console)

commandArguments.name: block_state
commandArguments.doc: a block state like `oak_stairs[facing=east]`, given back in full with every property (`"minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=east,half=bottom,…]"`)

commandArguments.name: item
commandArguments.doc: an item like `diamond_sword`, or with components on Paper (`diamond_sword[enchantments={sharpness:3}]`)

commandArguments.name: centity
commandArguments.doc: a live centity by its instance id (completed from the live ones)

commandArguments.name: centity_kind
commandArguments.doc: one of the project's centities, by its folder name

commandArguments.name: menu
commandArguments.doc: one of the project's menus, by its id

commandArguments.name: dialog
commandArguments.doc: one of the project's dialogs, by its id

constants.name: TARGET_DISTANCE
constants.doc: How far `target_block` and `target_entity` look by default, in blocks.

constants.name: PATH_REACH
constants.doc: How close a mob's or a centity's walk has to come to its target to count as reached, in blocks.

constants.name: REPATH_TICKS
constants.doc: How often a walk after an entity or a centity looks for a new path to where it is, in ticks.

constants.name: START_DROP
constants.doc: How far below a centity's feet a walk looks for ground to start from, in blocks.

constants.name: NODE_LIMIT
constants.doc: How many places one path search may look at.
